Requirement Description: The Ocean Sciences Division, NRL Code 7300, Center for Geospatial Sciences (CGS), Code 7340 requires IT support in its software, hardware, and cybersecurity infrastructure. The NRL CGS utilizes a broad array of computing hardware and software to accomplish sponsor-funded research goals. There are roughly 150 individuals in the CGS performing research on nearly 700 systems, both physical and virtualized.  Current hardware includes desktops and workstations, hosting servers and database systems, portable electronic devices (e.g., smart phones), printers and scanners, local and wide area network equipment (e.g. Layer 2/3 Switches, Firewalls, load balancers, etc.), and virtualized systems.  Major software products supported on these systems include (but are not limited to) Windows, Mac OSX, and Linux operating systems; various Microsoft enterprise systems, various calendaring and scheduling systems, Anti-Virus/Firewall system server, Adobe products, various scientific and data analysis applications, as well as internally developed Government-Off-The-Shelf (GOTS) applications.  The IT infrastructure must continually evolve and improve as new technologies become available and as new computing requirements are developed.

Every time the building loses power or it takes a power hit the south side UPS powers down (killing all the lights) and needs to be restarted by someone at NH-94. All of these spaces do not have any emergency lights installed since the project had them installed to a UPS system. Project is to remove lighting circuit from UPS system (not required) and install emergency lights.



This is a life safety issue.

Requirement Title: CLDJ-419 Repair/Replace Open Bay CLU Upper
Requirement Description:
CURRENT SITUATION: 18 PAX open bay CLU located on Camp Legacy is currently uninhabitable and needs to be replaced.  The CLU has a center failing beam, birds living within the roof area, and the smell of urine and decay throughout the unit.



REQUIREMENT:

We are requesting to have the entire unit repaired or replaced so that it is an appropriate living space for personnel.  The roof will need to be replaced, along with a new center beam.  The floors will need to be replaced.  The walls will need to be cleaned and repaired.  Any furniture that is unsafe for use due to animal excrement and urine, will need to be replaced.  Electrical and plumbing will need to be replaced if deemed unsalvageable.  Doors and windows will need to be assessed and replaced if damage is excessive.

Requirement Description: This design/build project will add local, manual steam pressure reducing control stations at the main carrier docking piers, Pier 'B" (B722) and Pier 'D' (B724), allowing steam pressure and flow to be reduced to the minimum acceptable pressure.  The selected pressure and flow reduction will maintain both the steam and condensate systems in good working order when implemented (i.e. when there no aircraft carrier or vessel requiring steam services docked at either location).  Independent stations will be provided for each pier location.  Normal steam service to either pier shall be restored to full pressure prior to any scheduled docking of an aircraft carrier or any other vessel requiring steam utilities.

Requirement Description:
1. WORK LOCATION: Naval Base Ventura



    BASE: Point Mugu



    BUILDING NO.:  55

  



3. PROJECT TITLE: Install Lightning Protection PM55

4. IMPACT: Launch Pad PM55 does not have lightning protection for the facility; the NOSSA waver expires in 2026.  NOSSA has released information that as of 2026 these facilities are no longer authorized to be covered under waiver to remain operational. The development of the Hull, Mechanical & Electrical (HM&E) controls is the primary focus of the Integrated Power and Energy

System (IPES) Test Facility (ITF). This program includes a requirement for HM&E controls system development. To investigate and

develop the control systems requires a workspace of approximately 3300 sf. The requested design shall incorporate the use of the

existing platform from the DDX/DDG-1000 test site in the northeast corner of bldg. 77H and user requirements as identified in the

attachment. The existing DDX/DDG 1000 site is approximately 106 ft. x 32 ft.

The design shall incorporate a site investigation to obtain all building data, existing site conditions and determination of utilities to

meet user requirements.

The design shall include all space requirements related to architecture, security, electrical, cooling and fire protection. All design

elements shall consider NSWCPD standards and meet the applicable code requirements from State, local, and Federal authorities.

Requirement Title: CFAO076_Install BFP on fire systems CFAO wide (RB)
Requirement Description:
As identified in the 2022 sanitary survey CSH-6106 needs to have a backflow preventer installed to protect the Camp Shields water system from contamination from the CSH-6106 fire suppression system. On the exterior of building is the fire riser. This exterior piping needs to be reconfigured and have a 6”doublel check valve installed. Please see PowerPoint that is in PIR folder for the recommended installation location/direction/, and backflow preventer type.



Project Scope of Work (Objective):

To meet AWWA and JEGS standards CFAO must install backflow preventers on all fire suppression systems to protect the drinking water. The following buildings need backflow preventers installed on separate systems. The recommended backflow preventers are from the inspectors from the 2020 Cross Connection Control Backflow Preventer Survey. The inspectors said we must have the specified type, and models of backflow preventers to meet the requirement.

Requirement Title: LC-U33-Rodriguez Range-De-lead and Repair Berms on Outdoor Ranges
Requirement Description: De-leading and re-establishing the impact areas and the berms on Rodriguez Outdoor Rifle and Pistol Ranges. Berms   need to be de-leaded, cleaned and re-established periodically to avoid lead and casing buildup which can cause ricochets and or fires. Ricochets may also result in round returning towards firing line or Chesapeake Bay Bridge Tunnel. The sand berm on both outdoor ranges behind the target lines has been cut out due to repetitive firing. Request the impact berm be excavated of all sloughed material at the face of the existing impact area and rebuild the impact berm with sifted fill material replaced to an acceptable state to act as and impact SDZ to meet current safety standards.

Oil-based paint cans with 1" or less of dry paint can be bagged and disposed in as solid waste. Paint cans with >1" must be properly disposed. Management and disposal of waste paint, brushes, rags, and rollers must be determined by Installation Hazardous Waste Media Manager.

EM22 NSWC BLDG 143 FULL FACILITY BACKUP GENERATOR FOR NOSSA SITE APPROVAL 20625885


Requesting installation of a full building generator for Building 143 to protect against loss of critical one-of-a-kind equipment from electrical surge damage, cost of downtime, and loss of data.  Please see attached spreadsheet for mission requirements descriptions and impact on cost of equipment.  Some one-of-a-kind equipment may not be replaced.



During power outages or power glitches, Contractor and SSP maintained test consoles experience adverse effects of surges and outages.  Equipment damage ranges from blown fuses to full system failures.  This equipment also requires a 4-hour warm up every time prior to resuming use.  



Generator to supply entire building with backup power and include full building line buffering surge protection or UPS for each test system - whichever is more cost effective.  Building will have classified areas requiring backup power for security monitoring.  Generator to be placed on concrete pad, fenced enclosure, and have all environmental reviews, approvals, and permits.  



Building contains one-of-a-kind contractor equipment.  Need to address the issue and get a generator installed for the entire building to remedy the 4-hour warm up times on each console and reduce the possibility of test data loss.  See attached Critical Equipment spreadsheet.

Requirement Title: NSN LP-40 Install In-Line Receipt Filtration
Requirement Description:
Currently, there is no means of inbound filtration of JP-5 fuel that offloaded via a barge at the South Wall at Naval Station Norfolk and transported through approximately 2.5 miles of underground pipeline to the bulk fuel tanks at Chambers Field FF. Fuel that is loaded at DFSP Craney Island into barges for transport and delivery to Chambers Field FF is not filtered.  Therefore there are only two filtration points at Chambers, the truck fill stand and the truck prior to issue to aircraft. 



The new filters will replace the existing ones that are no longer in use. The existing in-line fuel pump may need to be replaced due to possibly being oversized.

Requirement Title: CONSTRUCTION for UM - REHAB NS-04 WETWELL AND INCOMING LINE
Requirement Description:
(DBB) Rehab/coat wetwell and incoming sewer mains entering station up to second manhole in both directions for the gravity sewer.  Station is experiencing heavy infiltration due to tidal influences.  Wetwell is leaking into dry well from specific points.



Rehabilitate/coat wetwell and incoming wastewater main to the NS-04 pump station that services the SWWCAAS collection system at Mike, Sierra, Yankee, Kilo, and Hotel piers.  NS-04 wetwell has cracks in the common wall between wetwell and pump room.  Continued degredation can cause the wetwell to flood.  The incoming sewer line has severe crown corrosion that allows groundwater infiltration.



This project repairs the wetwell NS04 for part of the tertiary treatment process and is necessary to comply with regulatory and permit requirements as it could have severe impacts on treatment operations and would result in regulatory violations and unfavorable media coverage.



Without this project, wastewater treatment will be inefficient.  JBPHH will remain limited on its capacity to bed-down new personnel or mission.  NAVFAC HI OPS has to approve every personnel increase beyond the agreed personnel number due to our sewage cap.

Requirement Description: Currently the roof over building 313B (2nd Lane Booth at the Main Gate) is sloped (Gable or A-Frame design) with a over hang about 1-2 feet out from the shack. The overhead heater can be remounted just above the door or the frame of the Guard Shack angled down to continue to operate and provide heat.  Lighting can be looked at once new roof is on and if needed a smaller light could be added to shack to ensure visibility.

Requirement Title: 1853902 -- (N42158) NFPC/CNIC B592 Crane Rail Survey and Alignment
Requirement Description:
NFPC Code 1460.2 requests NAVFAC MIDLANT PWD to provide the following services:

 Grouping: Lifting and Handling Dept.

 Equipment/function: Crane Rails

 Subject: NFPC Crane Rail Survey with an option to alignment if needed

 Comment: Replacement Crane RFP's cannot be submitted by Navy Crane Center until the results of the survey are identified.

-Perform survey of the crane rails and compare results to the latest REV of CMAA #70 requirements

-Develop repair plan to align rails to CMAA #70 requirements without degrading the capacity of the rail system (if applicable based on initial rail survey). The repair plan shall be able to be performed in phases on sections of rail with minimal disruption to production in the facility. 

-Confirm that the repair plan and change in rail position will still provide the CMAA #70 horizontal and overhead clearances for the existing crane/replacement crane.

Requirement Title: NWC B-1A Pringle Hall HVAC Upgrades SAES Design
Requirement Description:
Pringle Hall Auditorium is serviced by two condensing units installed in 2009.  Both units utilize R-22 refrigerant which has limited availability if required for unit repairs.  In addition, Pringle Hall Auditorium has been experiencing high humidity conditions (75% average between June 1st and Sept 23rd) which has created mold issues to the 95+ year old facility.  NWC is currently utilizing commercial dehumidifiers to assist, but these are frequently cycled off during events due to noise impacts.  After review with NAVFAC Design team, it was determined that this should be an outside design due to complexity of the current unit.

Requesting a Design project to replace condensing units and associated air handling unit cooling coils and add de-humidification capabilities.

Requirement Title: Crane Wheel Replacement & Alignment, EWH-2, B7137, SWFPAC
Requirement Description:
Requirement: 



1. Survey the rails and each wheel and develop a shimming plan to remove the

misalignment

2. Fabricate necessary shims.

3. Jack the crane to install necessary shims and replace all wheels with new

to meet OEM requirements.

4. Lower the crane, test run, and perform verification survey. 

5. Crane outage must be limited to 30 days. 



*Replacement Crane Wheels are being provided by SWFLANT and are enroute.

**Detailed SOW will be provided by the SWFPAC.



Justification: 



The crane wheels at EHW2 are misaligned causing excessive wear.  In

the 5 years the crane has been in service they have worn 35% and are

considered failed at 50%.  Further now that we have worn through the

hardened surface the wheel wear is accelerating.  Both the North and South

cranes are seeing this issue although the North is the worst.  Our

instructions requires that we have both cranes up to do operations and we

have no back-up with EHW1 down.  The cranes will not likely make it past 18

months.... might not even make it another year.

Repair or replace the fire alarm panel to ensure is fully functional.

Ensure all fire alarm systems/devices for the facility are fully communicating.

Validate the account for PH1477 or create a new account to have PH1477 fire alarm panel fully functional to communicate.

Requirement Title: PD21558363 - EN - REPAIR - RETAINING AND STAIRS - SEABEA-77 - MSRON11-HA 575
Requirement Description:
Soil erosion on the east side of the building has reached a point where there is no longer a secure path to service the mechanical equipment. The erosion has also started to impact the integrity of the foundations of the concrete pads for the equipment and the foundation for the exterior fire escape stairs. The fire escape stairs are metal and corrosion from the sea air has begun to deteriorate the condition of the metal.

This project will correct the problem caused by the erosion and provide a stable surface to access the mechanical equipment and to prevent any damage to the equipment foundation pads. The project will also replace the exterior stairs to provide a safe egress from the building.



Project requirement is to address the erosion occurring on the east side of Building 77 and Building 68.

YORK-28

The facility has new heat pump window units that currently provide adequate heating needs in office and personnel locations and no longer rely on steam heat. The following locations will still require steam heat in the event that the steam lines are replaced with new ones:



Fire Suppression Room

Tool Room

Front Main Bay 

2 X-Ray Rooms

This will limit the amount of new steam lines needing to be installed. A similar setup is located in the rear X-ray room of the building. 



Roughly 2,000 linear feet of steam heat pipe is currently installed in the facility.

Requirement Title: REPAIR NAVAID TRESTLE STRUCTURE & INSTALL LIGHTNING PROTECTION
Requirement Description:
The ILS (Instrument Landing System) is a dual antenna Navigational Aid (NAVAID) system located on Rota's airfield. One of the two antenna systems is situated on a tall, wooden trestle structure a little past the approach end of the runway. This antenna is associated to, but separate from, BLDG 3100. We would like to accomplish the following repairs/modifications to the trestle in order to ensure the safety of the equipment and the personnel who maintain it:



1. Repair deteriorated railings. The railings no longer have the capability to withstand a person's weight and need to be repaired. We would like to maintain the wood material as opposed to incorporating steel so that it does not interfere with the antenna's signal.



2. Treat lumber for the environment. The cross bracing, decking, rails, girders, railings, and beams need to be treated for the environment so that the wood material can withstand the local weather conditions.



3. Reconnect equipment grounding. The equipment ground was discovered to be disconnected and needs to be reconnected in accordance with MIL-HDBK-419 para 2.2.2.2.





4. Install two lightning protection structures on either side of the trestle structure in accordance with MIL-HDBK-419 para 2.2.3. Specific distance and placement restrictions are still being researched. However, we would like the lightning protection to be within the antenna's cone of protection in accordance with MIL-HDBK-419 para 3.5.2.





Justification / Impact if not executed

This NAVAID system is critical to pilot landing safety. If these repairs are not executed, the equipment could be severely damaged leading to a potential aircraft catastrophe. Additionally, it could lead to the injury or death of the equipment maintainers due to its high elevation.

Shutting down the bowling alley or the snack bar for an extended period is out of the question so the HVAC system replacement must be phased.  Cutting holes of sufficient size for roof top units is not an option due to the construction of the building.

FCI is 45 is from the 2023 PAVER projection from the 2020 PCI.

that can use (park or taxi) over these areas.

Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152852 RM22-0178 DD2 MAIN PUMP NO. 3 REPAIRS, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Background: DD2 pump well houses 4 main dewatering pumps, which are critical to the operation of the dry dock facility as it Provides the ability to dewater the dry dock during docking/undocking evolutions. Of the 4 pumps, 2 are operational while 1 is Currently undergoing repairs. The last main

pump, MP3, is no longer operational due to a damaged and worn bearing in its impeller. During the June 2021 NAVSEA 04 audit, it was identified that the pumps at DD2 are in need of repair. Having all pumps available is necessary to maintain optimum dewatering capacity and provides the facility with operational redundancy in the event that a pump fails.



SOW:

Repair MP3 impeller

• Disassemble and reassemble shaft and motor assemblies

• Inspect/repair/replace motor bearings

• Replace all bearings along shaft and impeller

• Includes crane lifts through pump well hatches and removal of all interferences



Perform Alignment Checks

• Check/inspect pump motor for proper gap tolerances

• Inspect all motor bearings for clearance

• Align pump motor with shaft, bearings, and impeller



Operationally test MP3

• Flood DD2 and dewater using MP3 to verify dewatering capacity

• Operational checks include vibration testing and temperature monitoring

Requirement Title: WR152948-WON 1774342 - BLDG 155 Repair Canopy at Plate Yard, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Structual Inspection report conducted FY22 (POC Regan Kobayashi), buidling restrictions have been in place to restrict movement under canopy. 

Comments from PHNSY and NFH are below:

Due to the height/weight of the canopy, PPE and forklift (unless fully enclosed) does not provide adequate protection when traveling under the canopy

We recommend providing a Matson container (or tunnel structure) to allow occupants to walk under the canopy area.

We understand the building occupants currently use a forklift to transfer material from the yard to the interior. To avoid traveling under the canopy, we recommend driving the forklift through the rear CIA access gate, around the canopy, and into the building instead.

Bridge crane is out of commission and is not an option to transport material.

Based on conversations, due to the height of the canopy, it does not appear the shops have the capability of performing the repair or demoing of the canopy structure. 

Upclose pictures of the canopy structure and its connections are needed, this will help with the future repair design.

Due to the height/weight of the canopy, PPE and forklift (unless fully enclosed) does not provide adequate protection when traveling under the canopy

We recommend providing a Matson container (or tunnel structure) to allow occupants to walk under the canopy area.

We understand the building occupants currently use a forklift to transfer material from the yard to the interior. To avoid traveling under the canopy, we recommend driving the forklift through the rear CIA access gate, around the canopy, and into the building instead.

Bridge crane is out of commission and is not an option to transport material.

Based on conversations, due to the height of the canopy, it does not appear the shops have the capability of performing the repair or demoing of the canopy structure. 

Upclose pictures of the canopy structure and its connections are needed, this will help with the future repair design.

Requirement Title: B-7CC Boiler # 2 Replace FD & ID Fans
Requirement Description: B_7 Repair Boiler #2’s Forced (FD) and Induced (ID) draft fans @ building 7, Coddington Cove, Central thermal plant. Work more specifically includes for the ID fan replacing roughly 250 sq. ft.  of internal steel plate that forms the separation between the inlet and outlet of the ID fan, as well as replacing rotating elements of the ID fan including bearings. Work for B2 FD fan includes removal and reinstallation of fan rotating members as well as the volute. 1. WORK LOCATION  



    BASE: Point Mugu



    BUILDING NO.: PM-3015

 



3. WHAT IS THE ISSUE: PM-3015 Section-C has multiple roof leaks throughout entire building (27,120 sqft). 



4. IMPACT: Rain water is coming through and spilling into office spaces and hangar bay areas, resulting in damaged equipment and furniture, and slip hazards due to wet floors. 



5. DETAIL DESCRIPTION OF WORK: 

a.    Provide repair and or replacement of existing roof and gutter systems. 

b.    At minimum, all roof and its components shall be replaced and ensure all gutters and downspouts are clean and clear of clogging debris and draining properly.

c.    Where needed, provide sheet metal fabrication and installation associated with metal roof system retrofitting for existing roofs.  All new fabrication for such items as flashings, curbs, stands and other penetrations shall match the existing material and color, so the new metal roof systems match the existing conditions for a complete blend between the old and the new throughout both buildings.

d.    Where needed, provide replacement of deteriorated edge metal coping with new stainless steel edge metal coping, 5-inch to 10-inch in width as needed. Including all mechanical clips and fastening devices. Fastening from the top side or surface of coping is not acceptable.

f.    Provide replacement of all deteriorated existing roof gutter systems, and install new stainless steel gutters and downspouts.

Underground piping has experienced several breaks and unless replaced more leaks are expected due to being close to its service life.

Requirement Description:
Repair sewer lines identified by the attached survey. The condition of the existing sanitary sewer system of the entire NSA Mechanicsburg facility in in poor condition. System was mostly built in the 1940’s with some add-on sections or replacements based on breaks. The system is mostly constructed of a variety of sizes but is dominantly 8”, 10”, and12” vitrified clay pipe (also known as terra cota). The objective of survey to briefly summarize the sanitary sewer system

condition and highlight the key findings. The system recommendation is based upon the existing sanitary sewer systems in place as of a televideo study done in 2017 and condition rating survey accomplished 2021. Over the intervening almost 80 years, the sanitary sewer system has become compromised, for various reasons, with pipe joints that have separated

to some degree, pipe cracks, pipe breaks, and other defects. There is also thought to be illicit cross-connects with the

storm sewer system. Due to infiltration and inflow issues, perceived to be from at NSA-Mechanicsburg, downstream pump

station owned and maintained by Hampden Township is experiencing significant and regular high water events.

Requirement Title: URGENT - New Service Water System at WRF Effluent Pump Station (B1684)
Requirement Description: Updating this request to "URGENT" to comply with future requirements of the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit for the Water Reclamation Facility (WRF), which will require continuous total residual chlorine (TRC) recordings for the Effluent Sampling Point, located at B1684; the updated NPDES Permit requirements are anticipated to become effective in September 2024. This project will provide a new potable water system to supply the Effluent Pump Station (EPS) screen wash and pump seals, instead of using the in-plant reuse water, which is chlorinated; the intent is to mitigate the introduction of chlorine to the wet well of the EPS to help comply with chlorine limits being added in the future NPDES Permit, as well as to mitigate potential corrosion of the metallic surfaces of the pumps and screen, which may lead to premature failure.

Requirement Title: (BTO)(CNIC)(UTIL) BALBOA-7 Conduct NDT on DA Tank
Requirement Description:
Work Type (contract or shops): Contract

Scope of work (include mission need dates, and or special requirements):  



Project Description: 

Inspection and evaluation for pressurized vessel integrity to include wall thickness of piping and tank. This is a boiler inspector requirement to maintain operations



SCOPE OF WORK



1. GENERAL REQUIREMENTS



The Contractor shall provide all labor, transportation, equipment, supplies, materials, approved methods, quality control & assurances, and construction supervision necessary to complete the work included in this document. In all cases, the contractor shall be required to fulfill all safety standards as well as local and federal building and environmental code regulations. Contractor is responsible to haul away all the debris to the dumpsite and the recyclable materials to the recycling facility on base.



1.1.    The Deaerating tank is a pressurized vessel with known degradation. Non-destructive testing shall be performed to determine vessel  and connected pipe thickness and integrity.

1.2.    Testing is being required by the boiler inspector for continued operations, and the project to replace the DA tank has been pushed to the right due to funding constraints. 

1.3.    Testing entity must coordinate with Cogen Plant Staff  for steam outages and Boiler Inspector for adequate reporting to satisfy his requirements.



2.    Record all findings and compile into a structural integrity evaluation and report. Include in the evaluation photos, summaries, and recommendations. Any major concerns shall be brought to the attention of the owner so they can be addressed immediately while the crew is on site

Requirement Title: UM - WW - JBPHH WWTP HEADWORKS SCREENS REPLACEMENT
Requirement Description:
Project scope involves replacing the existing Headworks screens with new screens of equal capacity to provide removal of large solids prior to the liquid settling and aeration portion of the JBPHH WWTP treatment process.  After purchasing replacement parts for one screen (out of two screens, only one left operating) that has been out of service for almost a year, after installing the parts, the screen is still mis-aligned (due to wear-and-tear and objects hitting the screen over time); the manufacturer's representative recommended that we replace both screens (the screens are not repairable).



Additionally, the existing screens are not the most efficient when it comes to removing solids, because they are 6 millimeter step (slotted) screens that directly face the flow direction; whereas the proposed future screens, while also being slotted (bar) screens, would have the slots orientation horizontally opposed to the flow direction, creating a greater capture efficiency by forcing the flow to change direction 90 degrees.

Furthermore, step screens utilize thin plates to separate the screen openings, versus bar screens that utilize thick and more robust bars that are less prone to losing alignment and screen mechanism failures.



Replacement of the screens will also require replacement of the wash-presses that compress and remove "excess" water from the screenings.



The regulatory agencies (EPA and State DOH) expect that the JBPHH WWTP can continuously screen wastewater influent.

Funding Source: CNIC Funded

FY Requested: FY26, Q3

Project Details/SOW: 

Problem Statement: Fire Protection Hydrants serving Naval Station Great Lakes have not been flow tested since 2015. 

Location: All Fire Hydrants serving GLMAIN, CAMP MOFETT, CAMP PORTER, CAMP JPJ, FORRESTALL VILLAGE, HALSEY VILLAGE, NEMITZ VILLAGE, WILLOW GLEN, and FHCC. 

Size: Approximately 634 Hydrants and 540 Hydrant Valves. 

Proposed Soultion: FOR CONTRACT EXECUTION. NO P&E REQUIRED. Contractor to conduct Flow Testing of Hydrants Serving Naval Station Great Lakes. Justification: Various Regulations, including National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 291 Standard for Hydrant Flow Testing requires hydrants to be flow tested every 5 years to ensure that changing conditions in the piping and system demands won't impede the hydrants' ability to deliver water. Hydrants have not been Flow Tested since 2015.

Requirement Description: Bldg. 77L NE Exterior Insulation Finishing System (EIFS) is failing, allowing moisture into the building. There is a larger design and project planned to correct the entire 77L EIFS System but it will be a few years until this work is started. Therefore, requesting the NE Exterior wall, from the center double doors to the NE corner of the building be temporarily repaired. Recommend repair include coating the entire wall with an Elastomeric Coating (Master Protect). Coating would likely need to be applied via spray and multiple coatings.  Coating shall match the exterior color of the existing EIFS. In addition, all small cracks would need to be raked out/enlarged and filled with polyurethane sealant prior to applying Elastomeric Coating. There is also possibly a small area of 750 SQFT with larger cracks and or multiple smaller cracks, which might be beneficial to repair part of the EIFS via by having a base coat applied with a mesh coat and then a finished coat to match the existing EIFS outer coating. Target start date is November 4th with a completion by November 18th. Will need to review the scope/IGE prior to proceeding to Acquisitions.

not back feed the utility service power feeders F515, F615 (Substation 5) and F611 (Substation 6) during unscheduled power outages. The noted

to communicate with the existing SEL relays at Substation 2 and at  Substation 5. Provide additional 115-kV CCVTs for voltage sensing for the new microprocessor relays as needed. 

Provide new IRIG rooftop antenna at Sub 3 and Sub 4.  Provide programming, installation, and commissioning of all the new  equipment. 

Work shall be in accordance with FC, UFC, and OPSEC policies.

Requirement Description:
Paint interior of CDC building 1901 to include all classrooms, training and lounge areas halls and lobby.

Using fresh no-toxic paint that makes surfaces easier to clean and improves the overall brightness of the rooms. Repainting also protects walls from damage and helps meet current safety regulations. A clean well maintained space boost staff morale and creates a more positive safe environment for the children. Some areas of the building have paint chipping off the walls which could also pose a safety hazard because the paint chips can be sharp, and children can possibly get scratch. Children can also put chips of paint in their mouth.

Scope, Design, and/or Study with Cost Estimate



Remodel current room of building SP91 to create a 12 terminal area authorized to process National Security Information. Design will meet or exceed all standards of a Secure Room as set forth in DoDM 5200.01 V3 pg 45 “VAULT AND SECURE ROOM CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS”.



Provide separate Scope, Design, and cost estimate for the remodeling of two areas (RM 119C, and RM 119B) one design will be chosen. All quotes will be evaluated on Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA), design, and time of delivery.



RM 119C Is currently configured as a 54’ x 26.5’ server room with elevated floors (servers have been removed), New design would be for 14’ x 26.5’ to be converted. Removing all existing HVAC equipment and installing new stand-alone units. Build new walls, and secure access as per DoDM 5200.01 V3 pg 45. Install new fiber conduit for NMCI use.



RM 119B Is currently configured as a 25’ x 32’ server room with elevated floors (servers have been removed), New design would be for whole room to be converted. Removing all existing HVAC equipment and installing new stand-alone units. Bring walls to specifications, and secure access as per DoDM 5200.01 V3 pg 45. Install new fiber conduit for NMCI use.

Requirement Title: B911 - Repair/Upgrade the Kingfisher Receiver - E2
Requirement Description:
Per Shops (Fire Alarm Technicians):



The Primary Side of the Kingfisher Receiver in the 911 Facility is no longer functioning. The motor/printer assembly looks to have finally failed completely. This leaves us with the secondary printer as the sole printed recordings of daily Kingfisher activity and we have now lost the ability to verify if all the Kingfisher Transmitters are communicating. Each morning we run a Code 2 on both receivers which generates a Poll to each transmitter on Dahlgren. After the Receiver is done printing we visually check for any missing box codes for all assigned addresses. This takes both receivers as one may see the box and one may not which means it will still transmit but now we don’t have that SOP format. Just an FYI. I spoke with Bill Henessy at Kingfisher regarding his proposal to verify it was a total turn key product Replacement/Upgrade to which I found out that did not include a new antenna cable pulled from outside antennas the facility to unit inside. This should not be a major impact to the cost provided to us on the existing quote but it will alter the cost. I think this needs to be included so as all parts and material are new in its entirety if and when we move in this direction so I will ask for an updated quote.

Requirement Title: NSWC BLDG 34 REPAIR EPOXY FLOOR RM19 20
Requirement Description:
EM24 NSWC BLDG 34 REPAIR EPOXY FLOOR RM19 20 24416654


WHO: WXR



WHAT:  Repair epoxy floor rm 19 and 20

WHERE: B34

WHY: 

* An estimate is needed for repair of epoxy floor. Room 020 has an epoxy coating that was applied to meet the Continued-Use

* Provisions specified in the PCB rules due to PCB contamination present in the floor. Cracks have developed in the epoxy and must be repaired. Remediation of the contamination was attempted in 2010. 

* Due to the extent and costs of remediation, the decision was made to utilize the provision to allow for continued use. Note that 40 CFR 761.30(p)(1)(iii)(A)(1) requires, "Two solvent resistant and water repellent coatings of contrasting colors to allow for a visual indication of wear through or loss of outer coating integrity" – it does not appear that there are 2 contrasting colors of epoxy on the floor. 

* It might be acceptable to seal the cracks and then add a contrasting color of epoxy on top of the floor.

Requirement Title: OUTLYING - NMC EAD PH - B543 - REPLACE ROOF
Requirement Description:
Objective: Project proposed to repair/replace existing roof.

                                                                                                                                                                                                                              Project proposed to replace the roofs of buildings Wesloc-543. Replacement of roofs includes and isn’t limited to the gutters, downspouts, soffits,  fascia, flashings, on the aforementioned building.  Design team to field verify by conducting an on-site inspection of the building roofs to identify conditions of the existing roofing system and related roofing components. Roofing materials - Investigate the existing condition of the roof deck material, expansion joints, flashings, caulking, and sealants, water repellents, etc.  Roof drains - Investigate the condition of all interior/exterior roof drains. Identify areas lacking positive drainage. Ensure that the drains are located properly and are sufficient in number and size to drain all accumulated water from the surface of the roof in accordance with code. Roof gutters and leaders - Perform a visual inspection to determine existing condition of materials. Ensure that the gutters and leaders are sufficient in size to drain all accumulated water from the surface of the roof in accordance with code.  Design team to field verify the exact amount of work necessary on the building.  Roofs may show signs of leaking, cracking. Gutters and downspouts may show signs of damage.  Work to include debris removal, and roofing and gutter removal and replacement as necessary.  Use all termite resistant materials for repairs.

Requirement Title: Requesting design and construction effort to expand the capacity of the existing  SITE 3 WASTE WATER PIT Near Bldg. CNRSV-1711
Requirement Description:
Requesting design and construction effort to expand the capacity of the existing Site 3 Waste Water Pit by sealing, lining, and converting an old concrete vault and providing connection piping between the two pits.  This waste water system is part of the oil water separator system that ensures storm water drainage is not contaminated with oil.



Current facility waste water pit only has a capacity of 1k gallons of waste water which is insufficient during a heavy rain event.  If not improved, the waste water system is at risk of being overcome by accumulated storm water and would overflow causing flooding, erosion, and violation of SPCC requirements.



The scope of work is to provide a liner or appropriate sealant in the existing underground tank convault (tank has already been removed) to ensure water tightness.  design and install pump and piping system between the existing waste water pit and the converted convault to allow drainage to and pumping from either pit to the existing pipelines towards Polaris point.  Check and repair damaged sections of the piping between lower Sasa Valley and Site 3 at Polaris point along Marine Drive at the bridges.

Requirement Title: NSN W-143 REPLACE SUSPENSION ROPES & REPAIRS TO PASSENGER ELEVATORS 12 &14
Requirement Description:
During semiannual inspection of the lobby passenger elevators in building W143, the suspension ropes on elevators 10,12 and 14 were sited for excessive wear. 



Commands are concerned about the safety of these elevators. 



Each elevator is suspended by six 1/2 inch 8x19 traction steel ropes with a breaking strength of 14,500 lbs. each.  The shives are manufactured by Otis Elevator and have composite liners that must be replaced as well. System configuration is 1:1 with one deflector shive and 6 landings. 



Asset numbers for the equipment and year ropes were last replaced are:

Requirement Description:
Project Title: Bldg. 1410 - Propane Pipe Leak Repairs 

Project Details/SOW:  

Small propane leaks detected near the threaded connections. 

Replace with socket weld to reduce the possibilities of future leaks. 

SOW  

- System will be isolated & secured at the main propane tanks. 

- All piping will be flared off after the point of isolation & purged with nitrogen before work begins. 

- Nitrogen purge during all welding operations. 

- Replace all piping on the north & south side of the building from the ground penetration up to the block valve. This pipe is currently all threaded, new piping will be socket welded to reduce possibilities of future leaks. 

- Repair or replace all leaking threaded fittings on the pump package with socket weld fings where possible. This will reduce the possibility of future leaks. 

- Repair all small fitting leaks by the vaporizers. 

- Replace the pipe from the vaporizers to the regulator manifold. Currently the pipe is threaded and leaking. The new pipe will be socket welded as much as possible from the red safety valve up to the regulator manifold. This will reduce the possibilities of future leaks. 

- This work will require 6 days of downtime. Trainer can be run cold during this time if needed.

Requirement Title: AIRFIELD - AF - KUNTZ AVE ROAD REPAIR
Requirement Description:
Scope: Area from Kuntz bridge all the way to Kuntz back gate needs to be inspected/surveyed for proper drainage, Base course and sub-grade stability. Additionally, the curbs and gutters need to be replaced to ensure proper drainage. Prior to design, a Topographical study will need to be completed to ensure the future design and execution of this project meets environmental standards for water run off and Sub grade stability to withstand heavy vehicular traffic. 







Justification: Currently their is approximately 30' wide/5,280' long/4'depth of asphalt riddled with potholes and standing water in multiple locations due to poor drainage. Shops have completed multiple temporary repairs that have expanded out due to Alligator, longitudinal, and transverse cracking. A study needs to be completed to determine the root cause of the drainage and pavement issue. Ultimately, all pavement, as well as the curbs, gutters, and ADA ramps need to be replaced from Kuntz bridge to the back gate of Kuntz.  See Pictures below.

Requirement Title: UM - BLDG 817 REPLACE MANANA HOUSING BOOSTER PUMP STATION, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Assess the existing Manana Booster Pump Station to identify options for replacement and/or upgrade, and provide recommendations including cost estimates.  Scope of work for design and construction will include the following or as modified based on the assessment:

- New 1500 GPM booster pumps with easily accessible parts

- New 1500 GPM Fire pump with easily accessible parts

- New ductile iron piping and fittings

- New gate valves

- New pressure reducing valves

- New electrical equipment if needed

- New pump station facility if needed



The existing Manana Booster Pump station was originally constructed in 1968 and is responsible for boosting pressure to the Manana Housing area.  Manana housing is currently fed via a 12IN transmission line that is connected to the 42IN Waiawa Waterline.  The booster pumps are needed to ensure adequate pressure for normal consumption as well as fire protection.  Due to the age of the existing booster pumps, there has been a difficulty in obtaining replacement pump parts thus at times limiting operations to one booster pump (1500 GPM).  Manana's average daily consumption is approximately 180,000 GPD.



The Board of Water Supply has an existing 8IN interconnection line that serves as a backup water source.  However, plans to remove this interconnection has been discussed and this scenario will need to be considered in the design and construction phasing.  The AE designer will need to consider a phasing plan that does not include shutting down the existing pump station.

Due to the urgency of this project, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard (PHNSY) is requesting to replace in kind two Drydock No. 2 main drain pumps, drain pumps #3 and #4 that seized during pumping operations. The scope shall involve removing the existing main drain pumps and motors, replacing them in kind and shall include all electrical work and appurtenances necessary to get the drain pumps operational. Work may involve concrete foundation work at the base of the pumps.  Other incidental work shall include leak checks, alignment checks, resetting all parameters and operational testing.



MIL-STD-1625, Safety Certification Program for Drydocking Facilities and Shipbuilding Ways for U.S. Navy Ships states that there shall be at least two drainage pumps available wherever a U.S. Navy ship is in graving dock and that each drainage pump alone shall have sufficient capacity for the removal of drainage water. The two drainage pumps serves to isolate the Navy ship by two methods of protection from all potential flooding sources, such as flooding and dewatering systems.  The main drain pumps are therefore critical components of the drydock system. The drainage pumps maintain the dry dock floor dry by pumping out the ground and sea water that seeps into the dock through numerous cracks and vertical construction joints on the walls into the drainage system.

Requirement Title: NSA SDA-347 MUSTER PAVILION IMPROVEMENTS (SIDING, HEATING, FANS)

Request to have weatherproofing sides installed throughout structure to protect from wind and rain.  Heating to be installed for winter use.  Ceiling fans to be installed to provide breeze during hot, humid, stale days. 



Student use. Prior to classing up at 0600, students have no area to seek shelter in other than the pavilion during winter, windy weather, and rain storms. DCASE Students do not have seating area outside of classroom to eat or take breaks in throughout their course of instruction (7 weeks, 0800-1600).  

Siding must be easily installed/removed/retracted by one or two Staff members. This is critical for hurricane season.

Prior DCASE location included lounge room for student breaks, nourishment and to facilitate studying. 



Students will not have shelter prior to classing up, eat, take breaks, or study in during inclement weather.

Requirement Title: CLDJ-901 Replace Tank Monitoring System to monitor reclaimed water tank water level.
Requirement Description:
Current Situation:



A radio switch inside the communication control panel (GPP18851) allows monitoring of water level at the reclaim water tank via radio frequency. The two switches, located at both WWTP and tank are currently not operational and the configurations of the switch & PLC are unknown. Utility radio frequency is not recommended to be utilized in CLDJ due frequency distortion on camp & cybersecurity concerns . 



Requirement:



Remove the components of the existing reclaim water tank monitoring system including the control panel comprised of PLC, Ethernet switch and radio antenna. The new control panel should monitor the level of water at the reclaimed water tank and send the continuous level signal to control panel at WWTP. The new system will allow the user to monitor the water level, set level of running the pump through HMI. All UFC requirements for cybersecurity should be addressed in contract, including but not limited, cybersecurity hygiene checklist, and Authority to Operate (ATO). CIO should be involved with cybersecurity requirements during RFP's development. Requesting Fiber to be pulled through current manhole access from tank to WWTP to link to new custom monitoring system designed by PMEB. Will security approval be needed.



Mission Impact:



BOSC personnel will continue to manually monitor tank level which reduces manning of the Waste Water Treatment Plant operations. Additionally, There is feasibility concerns in terms of radio frequency distortion and cyber-security vulnerabilities for the system which leads to insecure and inefficient operation for the system.

Requirement Description: Project will replace the roof system and repair the degraded envelope in building 104, The Bunker. The building houses the Installation Police Department and has the only Facility Restaurant for the occupants of the Blount Island Command. The building has deteriorated over the years and is in need of repairs. A recent study conducted in 2022 identified several deficiencies with the building envelope, such as unsealed pipe and duct penetrations, fixed louvers, degraded roof/wall insulation, damaged exterior wall panels, and lack of functional air and vapor barrier. The study also identified that the roof coating is weathered, pin-holed and peeling, the perimeter gutter is corroded and joint leakage is evident and impacting the metal eave trim below. The project will address the roof and envelope deficiencies in the building. The project will install a new roof system with new roof insulation, replace/repair interior ceiling system, install new gutters and below-gutter eave trim and repair, seal all envelope penetrations, cover existing louvers, replace degraded wall insulation, repair/replace exterior wall panels.

Requirement Description:
This WON scope is for multiple TF-1s: Repair/replacement of substations 1-3, replacement of distribution feeders and repairs to underground conduits and manhole systems. The project will be broken into phases.



Feeder cables & connectors have faulted several times over the past couple years. Cables are getting shorter

 as faulted portions are cut to replace cable connectors. Majority of the Cables are 35+ years old which is

well beyond the service life of 20 years. Few of them though the feeder lines are operational, are closer to 45 years of age.  Remove all cables and connectors from each terminating manhole from north to south or east to west to facilitate pulling in new cables and replacing all dead break connectors, splices and "T"s. Proof test all cables at end of construction to ensure cables & connectors have adequate insulation properties. If conduit is not replaced inspection is necessary. Conduct phase rotation checks before demolition of old cables and after new cables are energized on all three phase transformers to ensure proper rotation of three phase electrical loads. Additional work needed will include setting up light plants to locations identified per feeder cable project and generators to facility as needed to include  refueling of generator as needed. Scheduling each power outage well in advance to notify base populace.

The existing HVAC system in B701 has 3 266 ton Trane chillers that provide chilled water to B700. The 3 chillers have been in operation since 2003. Replace 3 266 ton chillers in B701 with new chillers installed in the existing chillers location. 



Demolition of the existing chillers and its complete removal from the site.



Disconnection and reconnection of the existing chilled water piping to

serve the new chiller, miscellaneous piping, fittings, valves, couplings, and pipe

insulation as required for a complete and operational system.



The new chillers will be connected to Trane Tracer BAS system. 



Provide testing, adjusting and balancing of water system after installation of new chillers.

Justification: Induction of this project is required due to the recent Notice of Violation Order (NOVO) for the WWTP. Several deficiencies were identified that need to corrective action which involves repairs. 



The work will be divided into two phases, based on the preliminary tank inspection.  The project scope for this first phase will be to repair aeration tanks #1 through #6, which involves:  draining each tank for concrete inspection and concrete defect mapping; coring tanks in select locations to determine concrete repairs; removing existing aeration piping and diffusers; removing all loose/bad concrete; removing/treating rust for exposed rebar; repairing concrete with polymer concrete to match existing surfaces; replacing existing aeration valving/piping with new aeration valving/piping and installing new diffusers; and replacing railings and walkways with new railings and walkways.

Requirement Title: WR 177188 TASK ORDER - B6846-B7000-B7024 INSTALL BIRD SCREEN RACK
Requirement Description:
WR 177188

Building 6846, 7000 and 7024, install removable leaf screen rack to prevent leaves, grass cuttings and other debris

from clogging up the air cooled condenser or the contaminating the open cooling tower condenser water. The

open air-cooled condensers at 7000 and 7024 are located in an area adjacent to large overhead large leaf trees

that fall and get sucked into the condenser fins and stick to the condenser until removed reduces the cooling

capacity/efficiency of the HVAC unit. At Building 6846, grass clippings and leaves are picked by the wind and

sucked into the cooling tower by the fan and fall into the water basin clogging the basin requiring frequent cleaning

of the condenser water basin and strainers which increases energy consumption, reduces cooling efficiency and

incurs unnecessary labor costs.

Area in room 1096 is approximately 1500 square feet.



Preferred color – blue.



“Baller Rally Class II” is distributed on GSA Advantage by vendor DIAMOND FITNESS SYSTEMS INC.



Product technical manual with installation instruction included in email attachment.





JUSTIFICATION: Improve safety for recruits who may pass out and fall to the floor during medical procedures.

Requirement Description:
Currently installed aviation fuel filter separators at facilities F-23-F (QTY 3) and F-31 (QTY 2) are outdated 3rd generation vessels. These vessels are beginning to show stress cracks. These vessels are 24yrs old makes replacement elements and repair parts extremely difficult to obtain.



 Remove and replace a total of five (QTY 5) 3rd Generation filter separator vessels; three at F-23-F and two at F-31 and replace with updated 6th Generation stainless steel for exterior vessels and carbon steel for internal vessels.  Do Not use CS IAW UFC 3-460-01 Design: Petroleum Fuel Facilities, section 3.14.3. While aluminum vessels are authorized, they are prone to stress cracking.  Therefore; use stainless steel for this project.

Requirement Title: DB Construction; HUBZONE MACC TO; PE2525M Repair 53 Area Training Tank Complex; CPEN
Requirement Description: The purpose of this project is to repair the 53 Area Training Tank Complex which serves as the only Marine Corps Underwater Egress Trainer (UET) on the West Coast.  Specifically, the Training Tank complex consists of bathhouse facility 53415 and the adjacent training tank facility 53417.  Project repairs include related plumbing and mechanical systems of both the bathhouse and the training tank, repair of the pool decking and the repair of the asphalt and gravel POV parking area that surrounds the Training Tank complex. If not repaired, the constant mold, mildew and standing water in the bathhouse and pool issues will continue to present immediate life, health, safety impacts and with significant negative impact on the mission training and combat readiness of Marines and Sailors.  This training tank is required to remain in use until its MILCON replacement in the 53 Area is programmed as no other training tank exists in this location aboard the installation

Requirement Title: REPAIR SIDING AND ROOF CONTROL TOWER PM355
Requirement Description:
1. WORK LOCATION  

    BASE: Point Mugu            

    BUILDING NO.: PM355 

3. PROJECT TITLE: Emergent Repair Control Tower Siding & Roof PM355

4. IMPACT: Numerous Service Requests have been submitted over the years for this same issue. Air Ops has attempted to capture water in buckets and divert water with makeshift shields to protect the air traffic control equipment within the “Horseshoe”, that serves critical air traffic control radar services throughout Ventura County. We a flirting with disaster of losing the ATC approach control facility equipment through continued roof and siding.  We have recently completed credit card repair action to patch the roof and recent heavy rains show that a permanent contract repair action is needed to stop the inundation of rain water into this area directly above the radar equipment room.

5. DETAIL DESCRIPTION OF WORK: Prior WO’s: HNYFX6, HTLNLR, F6R3DF, J3GNXM, J6LDLK, HPY4CY, J6K9HX, HZ9VP7, HZ9RZF: 1. Provide permanent roof and siding repairs at area where control tower and hangar roof meet on the West side of the roof top. This will include all necessary roof and siding removal and replacement for a complete and useable watertight repair.

2. Area to be repaired is approximately 60’ x 60’ section of roof and control tower wall siding to be removed and repaired or replaced.

3. Included in this work are repairs to sections of the roof covering and possibly the roof flashing located on the East side edge of the root top. This area is approximately 100 sf.

Requirement Title: RM22-0731 Repair Airfield Parking Apron Rows 1-6, Phase 1 of 5, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Project proposes to repair deteriorated asphalt concrete (AC) and concrete pavement at parking apron Rows 1 to 6 on Hickam Airfield at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH). This project will be completed in two phases, fiscal years FY26 and FY27.



Phase 1 will consist of the following:

Rows 4 to 6: Civil scope of work includes repairing existing AC and concrete pavement

areas, converting portions of the existing AC pavement areas to Portland Cement Concrete

(PCC) pavement for aircraft parking, grading of new AC and PCC pavement to ensure proper

drainage of surface runoff, provide smooth riding AC pavement transition, and provide new

pavement markings for new AC and PCC pavement.



Phase 2 will consist of the following:



Rows 1 to 3: Civil scope of work includes repairing existing AC and concrete pavement areas, converting portions of the existing AC pavement areas to Portland Cement Concrete (PCC) pavement for aircraft parking, grading of new AC and PCC pavement to ensure proper drainage of surface runoff, provide smooth riding AC pavement transition, and provide new pavement markings for new AC and PCC pavement.

Requirement Title: UM - KP 26 REBUILD AND REHABILITATE WETWELL
Requirement Description:
Project scope involves

1.  Overhaul pumps and piping – Replace pumps, pump motors, valves, fittings and associated piping (replace effluent piping to aboveground plug valve).  This work will require a bypass of the lift station wet well structure.  Bypass provisions shall provide the same performance duty point as the existing lift station with 100% pumping redundancy in accordance with 10-States Standard criterion for duplex pump configurations.  KTR shall monitor and maintain the interim bypass system at all times and provide emergency response as necessary to prevent system overflows/spills.  Existing lift station equipment will not be made available for the KTR’s use.  Provide spare pump.



2.  Reseal the interior wet well surfaces – Clean and reseal the interior surfaces of the wet well structure with approved epoxy-based commercial sealant that is specifically made for such wastewater applications.  KTR shall be responsible for all associated wet well cleaning, prepping and waste disposal.  Include EV sampling & testing for potential HAZMAT (lead; asbestos).



3.  Electrical - Replace existing motor control center and associated electrical wiring/conduits from the meter into the station.



4.  Structure Rebuild exterior structure and roof for station pumps and controls.  Walls are dilapidated and needs structural repair for continued use and occupancy.



4.  Prepare AM & EV project documentation -- reconcile pertinent site design details/provisions with CI DC.

SUBTORFAC suspends ordnance operations when the sprinkler system charges with water, which is what happens when a heat detector goes bad or goes off due to heat.

Requirement Title: UM - REPLACE Waiawa Electrical Switch Gear
Requirement Description:
Project to assess the existing Waiawa Pump Station electrical system, identify options for replacement and upgrade,

and provide recommendations including cost estimates.

The existing Waiawa Pump Station electrical equipment and switchgear was originally installed in 1955. Due to the age,

there have been difficulties in obtaining replacement parts. Portions of the electrical system was revised in 2013,

however, the overall system requires upgrade and replacement to meet current standards and needs. The Waiawa

Pump Station is the primary source and is responsible for supplying up to18 million gallons or 80% of the fresh water

that services JBPHH. Due to the Red Hill fuel contamination incident, the station is currently providing 100% of JBPHH

water demand. It is critical that the pump station is able to maintain current and future operations.

Project preference is for AE design and design-bid-build process. Project will require a charette to confirm the design

scope; planning and EV documents; and generation of design documents (i.e. basis of design, cost estimate,

construction plans, specifications, etc.).

Requirement Title: Building A324 main admin building-- HVAC upgrades
Requirement Description:
CHILLER IS BEYOND LIFE CYCLE AND IN NEED OF REPLACEMENT

- Replace existing YORK chiller with a new 43-ton TRANE unit.

- Condenser coil fouled/corroded beyond repair due to highly corrosive environment. 

- Excessive corrosion present near filter drier and all service valves, preventing technicians to service the unit in fear of maximum refrigerant loss and component failure. 

- Compressor vibration mounts corroded/dry rotted beyond repair, enabling the weight of the compressor to possibly fall through the bottom of the chiller. 

- Electrical components to include, contactors, conductors, fuses and controllers are exposed to the ambient corrosive environment causing rust accumulation, poor performance and humidity in all high/low voltage carrying equipment. 

- Replace DDC controllers.

- Inspect/Modify Duct Work as Needed.

- The current unit is 8 years old, and beyond its SEER efficiency rating.

Requirement Description:
1.1 PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The project involves renovating internal spaces of a building that houses the Navy Federal Credit Union bank within the Sigonella headquarters (Catania).

The building consists of a reinforced concrete structure and the intervention is located on the ground floor. The Task order 2 follows the completion of the previous Task Order 1 (Survey, Existing Conditions Floor Plan & Report), which presents the results of the inspection conducted on 11 September, 2023.

1.2 PROJECT OBJECTIVES

1.2.1 Mission Statement

The aim of the project is basically to redesign some internal spaces in the area of the building where the bank branches are located. Some rooms will also be redefined. A new restroom will be created and

the existing one modified by eliminating the anteroom.

The project must also include a rearrangement of the parts of the systems that are currently integrated with the existing furnishings.

For any further details, please refer to what is reported below and what is represented in the project graphics.

1.2.2 Project Specific Priorities

According to the planned renovation works, the aim is to minimize interference as much as possible with the activities taking place in the building.

1.2.3 Project activities involved

The disciplines involved in the design of this project are the following:

• Architectural design

• Electrical telecommunication system design

• Design of water and sewer systems

Please see below the main tasks included in the design of the project:

• Redifinition of the spaces and change of room use of the bank where the branches are located;

• Replacement of the office’s doors;

• Removal of the external safety grates;

• Replacement of existing windows;

• Repair cracks on external surfaces;

• Plan the systems layout where needed;

Requirement Title: Bldg. 2220 SN Firehouse Renovate Multi rooms
Requirement Description:
Requesting the current kitchen be remodeled to a commercial kitchen. The current kitchen is roughly around 15 years old and is

starting to show signs of age. A commercial kitchen design will give this kitchen more storage space and longer longevity compared to

a residential style. This kitchen is used 365 days a year by assigned personnel at Company 21 for meal purposes

- The HVAC system is not energy efficient and runs year round. Recommending review of HVAC/furnance system to include individual

room controls to meet energy efficiency. This station is manned 24 hours a day by 4 personnel

- Roof leaks have been noted from the Station 21 leadership. The leaks have been noticed in the common areas such has kitchen,

lounge and hallway. It is unknown where there leaks are as the roof is metal. The gutters on the building are not operable causing rain

and ice to drain directly to the sidewalk. Request for gutter repairs have been submitted previously but no actions have been taken to

address them. Requesting roof/gutter inspection to include repairs and/or replacement

- Both showers are in need of repair or replacement. Showers aren't draining properly causing structural damage to the adjacent wall

and rusting out metal wall and floor joist. Currently have a hole in the wall behind the showers and a work order was submitted but no

action has been taken since the issue has started

- Concrete in front of the the primary entry door bows during cold months creating a tripping hazard for personnel entering the building. It

was also noted the bow occasionally hinders the entry door from closing

- Entry doors on the building have gaps underneath due to concrete settlement. Doors also allow drafts in cooler months causing the

stations heating and cooling units to run constantly. Requesting doors to be replaced to enhance energy efficiency in the building

Requirement Title: HI2507M BRAVO Ramp Airfield Markings and Parking Spot Improvements, MCBH
Requirement Description:
Provide full design and construction services for airfield markings and parking spot improvements on Bravo Ramp / Apron at MCBH Kaneohe.  Project will accomplish repairs to MCBH Kaneohe Bay Airfield’s Bravo ramp to accommodate and maximize the amount of MV-22 aircraft parking on the ramp. Scope of work includes removal of existing taxiway striping, re-striping of the taxiway to maximize parking area for MV-22 aircraft, and installation of new grounding points and tie downs as required. Areas affected by repair/construction will be in compliance with applicable ATFP, fire suppression, seismic, accessibility, ASHRAE, LEEDs, and flood plain codes and standards (as required) upon completion of the project.



To accommodate MV-22 aircraft parking, taxiway striping which includes aircraft parking, lead-in, and lead-out lines will have to allow for proper spacing specific to MV-22 aircraft. Requirements for aircraft spacing and striping shall be in accordance with UFC 3-260-01. See attached DD1391 for additional details.



Design and construction shall be in compliance with all current codes and criteria.  The MCBH Design & Construction Standard (dated 11 Feb 2021) shall be followed as well as any updated requirements.

Project will accomplish repairs to MCBH Kaneohe Bay Airfield’s Bravo ramp to accommodate and maximize the amount of MV-22 aircraft parking on the ramp. Scope of work includes removal of existing taxiway striping, re-striping of the taxiway to maximize parking area for MV-22 aircraft, and installation of new grounding points and tie downs as required. Areas affected by repair/construction will be in compliance with applicable ATFP, fire suppression, seismic, accessibility, ASHRAE, LEEDs, and flood plain codes and standards (as required) upon completion of the project.



To accommodate MV-22 aircraft parking, taxiway striping which includes aircraft parking, lead-in, and lead-out lines will have to allow for proper spacing specific to MV-22 aircraft. Requirements for aircraft spacing and striping shall be in accordance with UFC 3-260-01. See attached DD1391 for additional details.



Design and construction shall be in compliance with all current codes and criteria.  The MCBH Design & Construction Standard (dated 11 Feb 2021) shall be followed as well as any updated requirements.

Requirement Title: 35824963, Construct Interim TFS Facility on U Lot, Bremerton
Requirement Description:
Requirement: Provide Tension Fabric/Membrane Structure (TFS) as interim Facility with a minimum square footage of 72,000 SF.   

TFS shall have interior lighting and all required fire protection for light industrial work and storage. 

TFS shall have a minimum of 4 large roll up doors for ingress and egress.  Provide personnel doors as required for emergency egress. 

Provide security fence with 4 vehicle gates around the perimeter of U Lot. 

Existing parking lot surface will be used as floor inside TFS. 

Demo and remove existing interior U Lot parking lot lighting and parking blocks.  Leave perimeter lights in place and operational. 

If another style of interim facility is proposed, maximize use of footage within the constraints of U-Lot.  If another type is proposed, provide issue paper with rationale and differences in cost and schedule for acceptance.

Justification: Background: During planning, a portion of the square footage (24,000 sq ft) in Building 462 was identified as being required to remain within the controlled industrial area (CIA) or Naval Base Kitsap-Bremerton (NBK-B). The remainder is slated for an off-site to a lease location, which is the subject of NAVFAC-PAC request for proposals that is due 26 May 25. There is no available space within the CIA or NBK-B at this time due to other SIOP initiatives and limitations on buildings due to seismic vulnerability.

Demolish Pretrial Confinement Complex



EV Comments:  Conduct NEPA review.  Lay-down areas must be pre-approved and NOT located near environmentally sensitive areas such as storm drains, floor drains and building air intakes.

Excess soils that will not be used as backfill at initial site *might* be required (by destination landfill) to be tested for hazardous properties and PFAS prior to removal from base.  If this is the case, please contact both H. Richtfort (PFAS) and D. Sytkowski (Haz Waste). HMR 12/22/23. Tree removals as a result of demolition will require Section 7 consultation with the US Fish and Wildlife Service prior to start of physical work. Provide NRM (Taylor Bozman) with number of trees and timing of project immediately as information becomes available. Communicate the Fugitive Dust Plan / debris containment plan/method to EV (Interim Air Mgr, Raghu Nagam & Stormwater Mgr, Madeleine Mahan). This plan should fully contain all debris, fugitive dust, and water produced. Protect all nearby storm drains. Surround the project area with silt fence. Use best management practices to manage any temporary soil/waste piles. Locate these piles and staging areas downhill of storm drains, preferably on a flat surface. A NOI will be required if the project area will be more than 1 acre (includes disturbed area and laydown/staging area).

CRM Comments:  B6801 is not historic, but demolition of a building must be coordinated with IL SHPO prior to starting any physical work.  NSGL CRM with draft and submit a notification letter in FY24.

The shore based facility will include 14 offices, a server room, a kitchenette, two (2) conference rooms and a lobby. Facility to satisfy the architectural design and construction

standards outlined in the Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 705 Technical

Specifications for Construction and Management.



This project will provide Anti-Terrorism/Force Protection (AT/FP) features and comply

with AT/FP regulations and physical security and progressive collapse mitigation in

accordance with DoD Minimum Anti-Terrorism Standards for Buildings. The AT/FP includes

standard force protection measures such as mass notification systems, emergency shutoffs

for ventilation systems, laminated windows, blast resistance window and door frames and

emergency lighting and signage.



Special costs include Post Construction Contract Award Services (PCAS) and cybersecurity

commissioning. The cybersecurity commissioning cost is to cover the contractor's

submittals, administrative actions and compliance with Navy's cybersecurity requirements

as well as Navy in-house costs to review contractor submittals and to implement steps

necessary for obtaining Authority to Operate. Facility-related control systems include

cybersecurity features in accordance with current Department of Defense criteria.

Sustainable design principles will be included in the design and construction of the

project in accordance with Executive Order 13423 and other laws and Executive Orders.



Facility will meet LEED ratings and comply with the Energy Policy Act of 2005 and the

Energy Independence and security Act of 2007. Low Impact Development will be included in

the design and construction of this project as appropriate.



Site preparation includes site clearing, excavation, grading and preparation for

construction.

Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152981 DD2 CAISSON 2I 5-YR UT, JBPHH
Requirement Description: Perform the 5-year Ultrasonic Testing (UT) on DD2 Caisson 2R plating in accordance with MIL-STD-1625D. The term caisson plating includes the entire hull, top deck, machinery deck, internal strength decks, bulkheads and breast hooks. Ultrasonic testing shall be performed at different location from previous inspections and a minimum 8-foot grid pattern is to be utilized. Additional measurements shall be taken to identify the full extent of unacceptable plating in areas found to have excessive wastage or areas that are suspected to be deficient by visual inspection. Submit AutoCAD drawings to depict the actual condition of the caisson and to indicate the locations of ultrasonic tests. Submit inspection reports with sketches and tables indicating original thickness of members, field ultrasonic readings, and percent loss of members. The report shall include the safety factor (referenced to yield or buckling stress) for plating that is corroded beyond the acceptable wastage. Any areas in need of repair will include weld repairs and replacement of structural steel members.

Please provide a design and cost estimate for the replacement of the existing handicap ramp used by

NAVSUP WSS employees to access the North end of building 311. The existing ramp is in poor

and falling off. The configuration of the ramp should be changed to allow ease of accessibility

for wheelchair bound employees. The handrails should be anchored to the concrete in lieu of using pockets. If possible, install a floor drain in all landings.

Requirement Title: OUTLYING – NMCPAC - ROOF REPAIR MAGAZINE GROUP 22 W 1 THROUGH 15
Requirement Description:
Reroof magazines at West Loch 22 Group. Project is required to repair leaks and prevent future leaks in the roofs of

Magazines. If repairs are not provided, tenant operations will continue to be adversely impacted and experience a

reduction in operational efficiency, which could eventually jeopardize the mission and fleet readiness.

- Water penetration into the magazines

- Erosion of rock cover on roofs

This is not a traditional magazine roof covering. The SOW is to cover each magazine listed below in the 22 group

magazine area with one solid sheet of coated and bonded membrane. The areas that overlap the concrete are secured

by a metal strap and concrete screws and grounded to the magazine grounding strap. At grade a small trench about 14

inches is dug and the membrane covers the trench and back filled with dirt and gravel. The membrane is bonded to this

magazine vent. The result is a total water proof magazine with a 20 year warranty.

Project is to remove and replace all the existing Suprotex Automatic Deluge valves and OS&Y control valves with new wet alarm valves and BFV w/tamper capabilities.   Project will include removal of all trim associated to the deluge valves including air lines, dryers, and drain lines. Project will also include installation of new paddle-type waterflow alarms to be installed.   All new fire alarm devices must be connected and tested with base building fire alarm system. Pre-test and Final testing are required with WNY, PWD fire Sector, Base Fire, BOSC and Facility BM for acceptance.

Requirement Title: OUTLYING - CNIC - HIKAFB B1122H MWR - REPAIR POOL COMPLEX AND DECK
Requirement Description:
Request repair of pool complex and deck. Large crack in bottom of pool, unsure if structural or a liner. Water leaks in expansion joints of deck where water leaks into womens restroom. Repairs should include Pool deck, Pool, railings, stairs and restroom renovations.



Requesting to Re-plaster the Pool:



Step 1 – Drain

The first step of the swimming pool resurfacing process is draining the pool. 

Confirm that all lights are working and tag them with a yellow tag that reads “do not turn on while your pool is empty".  Then drop a submersible pump into your swimming pool to begin draining it.



Step 2 – Prep

The second step of the pool resurfacing process involves expert sandblast, multi-coat, and strip crews for the preparation process. These crews thoroughly prepare the pool surface by removing old damaged surface material and preparing it to receive the new surface material.



Step 3 – Tile and Masonry

Prep pool tile, coping, and other decorative features such as ledger stone.



Step 4 – Plumbing and Seal

The fourth step is to seal the plumbing to ensure that your pool is water tight and ready for your selected pool surface finish. We will also wash your pool shell at this time.



Step 5 – Pool Finish Material Installation

The fifth step involves the installation of the pool surface finish material you selected. Now your remodeled swimming pool really starts to take shape.



Step 7 – Cleanup and Pool Fill

Once the specified material has been installed and acid washed (if needed), complete the general clean-up, and start to fill your pool. Keep an eye on the water level as it fills, and turn the water off once the water level hits the middle of your waterline tile.



Step 8 – Initial Water Treatment/Surface Curing

The final step in the pool resurfacing process, referred to as the Initial Water Treatment step, is one of the most important steps to be completed for the extended look and life of your new pool surface material.
