Requirement Title: UM - Replace Waiawa #2 and #3 Pumps & Motors
Requirement Description:
Project to replace main fresh water pumps #2 and #3 at the Waiawa Fresh Water Pump Station. The replacement will

include the following:

- Two(2) vertical turbine pump and motor, 6250 GPM at 190 FT TDH, 400 HP, 1200 RPM

- Associated piping

- Pump controls

Currently, Waiawa operates and maintains four main pumps that provide approximately 18 million gallons or 80% of the fresh water that is supplied to JBPHH. Pump #4 was replaced in 2018, while pumps #2 and #3 were last replaced in 1987. Typically one to two pumps are operated depending on the system demand and the tank levels at S1 and S2. S1 and S2 tanks must remain at a certain level for hydraulic and fire protection requirements. However, due to the fuel contamination incident, the Red Hill shaft has been temporarily disconnected from the distribution system and is not

serving the system at this time. Therefore the Waiawa has to continuously operate two pumps to maintain base demands. Replacing pumps #2 and #3 will be critical to continuously provide JBPHH with a reliable fresh water source.

Project preference is for AE design and design-bid-build process. Project will require planning and EV documents; and generation of design documents (i.e. basis of design, cost estimate, construction plans, specifications, etc.). Request AE to follow similar design as project title "REPLACE MAIN PUMP AND MOTOR #4 AT WAIAWA PUMP STATION." WON

1367046.

Requirement Title: NSN RW1028 TAXIWAY REPAIR, LP AREA (PHASE 1 OF 4)
Requirement Description:
Scope, Design, and/or Study



PHASE 1, specific work by pavement section includes:

Section TWA-T10A: Remove existing concrete and asphalt pavements and base materials.

Haul and dispose of unsuitable and contaminated soils. Provide clean fill; crush

concrete for reuse as a new base course. Replace with 13" PCC over 8" of cement

stabilized crushed aggregate base course. Apply high temperature sealant as required

and repaint all taxiway striping and markings to UFC requirement.

Section TWA-36A: Remove existing concrete and asphalt pavements and base materials.

Haul and dispose of unsuitable and contaminated soils. Provide clean fill; crush

concrete for reuse as a new base course. Replace with 13" PCC over 8" of cement

stabilized crushed aggregate base course. Apply high temperature sealant as required

and repaint all taxiway striping and markings to UFC requirement. Replacement

pavement section reduced in size by approximately 7,000 SY and returned to turf.

Sections TWASH-S07D; TWASH-S06D: Remove existing shoulders and provide replacement

taxiway shoulders total 25' wide paved with 2" of AC over 12" of compacted crushed

aggregate base course per UFC requirements. Haul and dispose of unsuitable and

contaminated soils and provide clean fill.



This is a CNIC funded project.

Requirement Title: B6301 Diamond refinishing, polishing and sealing system for Terrazzo floor
Requirement Description:
Scope of Work: 

This work is recommended to be done in 3 parts for the Main Lobby and Hallways only:

1. Diamond refinishing, polishing and sealing system for Terrazzo floor
-Supply labor and material to protect the working area with plastic covers, protective tapes and drop cloth.

-Supply labor and material to strip down terrazzo floor to remove existing coating or existing finish.

-Supply labor and material to grind terrazzo floor with low grit Metal/Copper bond diamond disc system to expose a new layer of terrazzo surface.

-Supply labor and material to repair and patch damaged areas and surface cracks with appropriate techniques.

-Supply labor and materials to continue grinding process with medium grit Meta/Copper bond diamond disc system to remove surface scratches left behind previous diamond set.

-Supply labor and material to grind terrazzo floor with 50 grit resin bond diamond disc system.

-Supply labor and material to continue grinding terrazzo floor with 120 grit resin bond diamond disc system.

-Supply labor and material to add hardening agent to terrazzo floor to increase surface density.

-Supply labor and material to grind terrazzo floor with 220 grit resin bond diamond system.

-Supply labor and material to hone terrazzo floor with 400/800/1500/ resin bond diamond disc system to achieve high resolution reflectivity and clarity.

-Supply labor and material to rinse terrazzo floor with neutralizing agent.

-Supply labor and material to apply appropriate sealing agent on terrazzo floor and burnish it with high speed burnisher.

Requirement Title: NDW25 B2168 REPAIR Broken Flue Pipe on HVAC Unit
Requirement Description:
Building 2168 boiler room 127 the flue pipe elbow has broken loose from the rest of the piping.  Please research and repair.

5/2/23 Found schedule 40 PVC flu pipe damaged from heat. This heater is an 80% product Heatco (manufacturer) is sending me venting information.

New Worklog was created by: STALLWORTHBM on Wed May 03 08:07:55 PDT 2023

Worklog Detail: This is to inform you the following work order will exceed the limit of liability.


Bldg. # 2168

Description: As seen above the flue was constructed of the wrong material type and has failed. A new flue will need to be installed that meets category 3 venting requirements also note the flue length requirements, existing is to long of a run. 



Worklog Detail: 5/22/23 DOAS unit not running appears to be control issue



Worklog Detail: 5/23/23 Traced out control wiring and checked all components unit just not getting a start command for supply fan and wire for start/stop does not land in control panel where diagram says it does will come back in the morning and trace out start/stop wire through all junction boxes



Worklog Detail: 5/24/23 Traced everything out and found no bad connections it appears DOAS controller is just not functioning properly got a quote from Havtech to come out and troubleshoot controls



Worklog Detail: 8/2/23 Went over again to verify issues would require controls Contractor.




Mission Impact Statement:



A new flue will need to be installed that meets category 3 venting requirements also note the flue length requirements,  the existing pipe is to long of a run.  This PVC piping was not designed to withstand the heat that the boilers produce and should have been made of metal piping.  With the flue pipe broken the HVAC system is not running at the prescribed efficiency for this system.  Causing it to run not according to specifications for heating and cooling.

Requirement Title: Tank U29 RVP to DVV Drain Line and Culvert Repairs, Tenjo Vista, NBG
Requirement Description:
Current Situation:

Tank U29 experienced a fuel leak in 2018 and NAVFAC MAR EV has a new project is underway to excavate and perform soil remediation (WON#1720400, ACQR#5908969).  Since that project is strictly soil remediation, this request is for a SRM project to perform repairs on the associated pipeline and the culvert.  The SRM contract will have to coordinate closely with the EV project to ensure that the pipeline and culvert can be accessed after excavation, but must not interfere with the soil remediation.   



SOW

It is estimated that drain line is approximately 120 LF of 6" diameter carbon steel pipe from the DVV to the RVP that needs to be replaced with new pipe.  The newly installed pipe pup and bypass line inside of the DVV shall remain in place.  Extent of pipe replacement is from the new pipe pup in the DVV to the first valve in the RVP.  Though the pipeline is empty and previously filled with water, it will still require gas free certification prior to any welding or cutting.  Upon installation of the new pipe, a full hydrostatic test will be required with both ends of the pipe blinded off.  The existing 3ft diameter culvert that runs underneath the RVP to DVV piping is currently clogged and undersized.  The work will require that the existing culvert be removed, and a new, appropriately sized concrete box culvert be installed.  Coordination between the fuel farm operators and the EV soil remediation contractor is necessary given that the EV contractor will be performing the excavation and backfill of the area.

Requirement Title: Replace Cooling Towers & Heat Exchangers, LAPSC, B/6500, SWFPAC (24556925)
Requirement Description:
CAT-2 IH-DB FY25/Q4



Requirement: Project will design and build replacement closed-circuit cooling

tower packages based on 10-15% Concept Design provided by Gov. 



Justification: The building's existing heat rejection system consists of a

pair of open-circuit cooling towers in the mechanical courtyard, which are

served by a pair of heat exchangers within the adjacent building's chiller

room. The open-circuit design of the towers allows any dirt, dust, and

debris that settles in the tower sumps to circulate through the heat

exchanger coils, leading to fouling, loss of performance, and eventual

system failure.

Requirement Title: OUTLYING – NMCPAC - ROOF REPAIR MAGAZINE GROUP 23 W 3 THROUGH 13
Requirement Description:
Reroof magazines at West Loch 23 Group. Project is required to repair leaks and prevent future leaks in the roofs of

Magazines. If repairs are not provided, tenant operations will continue to be adversely impacted and experience a

reduction in operational efficiency, which could eventually jeopardize the mission and fleet readiness.

- Water penetration into the magazines

- Erosion of rock cover on roofs

This is not a traditional magazine roof covering. The SOW is to cover each magazine listed below in the 23 group

magazine area with one solid sheet of coated and bonded membrane. The areas that overlap the concrete are secured

by a metal strap and concrete screws and grounded to the magazine grounding strap. At grade a small trench about 14

inches is dug and the membrane covers the trench and back filled with dirt and gravel. The membrane is bonded to this

magazine vent. The result is a total water proof magazine with a 20 year warranty.

Requirement Title: NBPL-77 REM or DEMO ORIGINAL COPPER LINE to Stainless Steel Material
Requirement Description:
NBPL-77: Remove or demo in place original copper line to stainless steel material; ensure current regulators are replaced with non-relieving pressure regulators and install stainless steel compressed nitrogen gas line outside gaseous bottle cage. 



1.    WORK LOCATION Point:  Loma Fuel Lab/ B77 

BASE: Point Loma    

BUILDING: NBPL-77 

ROOM/AREA OF THE BUILDING: From Gaseous Bottle Cage (1 Location) and Inside Lab Testing Room (5 Locations)

INTERIOR/EXTERIOR: Interior and Exterior 

ADDITIONAL LOCATION DETAILS: Point Loma Fuel Lab Facility B77


2.    ISSUE: The gaseous oxygen system in the fuels laboratory has been deemed dangerous and unsafe to operate due to concerns over the tape and pipe compound used during construction of the piping and its incompatibility with pure oxygen gas used during testing. The copper piping stretches from the oxygen bottle cage outside the north end of the building through the ceiling and walls, terminating at five outlets along the testing counters. Requirement Title: (DBB-IH) Replace Heating Loop with Mini Splits, B2200-2009,Bangor
Requirement Description:
Requirement:  IH-DBB project to replace failing HVAC Hot Water Loop suppling multiple buildings within the Bangor Unaccompanied Housing Complex. Add multiple mini splits to provide Heat and HVAC to each unit. Follow the same plan as the B2300 series HVAC/Heat upgrade -(MSR 22144963 2300 series). 

Bangor-2200, Bangor-2201, Bangor-2202, Bangor-2203, Bangor-2204, Bangor-2205, Bangor-2206, Bangor-2207, Bangor 2208 and Bangor-2209.



Justification: Replacement is required to restore the heating loop to fully operational status. Reoccurring leaks in the underground piping system result in makeup water use beyond the design capabilities of the system. Excessive makeup water leads to off gassing of entrained air and the formation of air pockets in the piping that restricts the follow of heating water. This condition affects multiple buildings during the heating season resulting in an unacceptable number of resident rooms with proper heating. Continued failure to provide adequate  heating will result in the reduction of the number of Unaccompanied Military personnel that can be housed on the base.



Needed: Design Awarded . Design Scheduled Acceptance. DD1391 Needed

Service contractor is stating unit has multiple leaks and some of the components are no longer available, recommending replacement. Therefore, replace existing Ultra Air Dryer with an  in-kind replacement cycling dryer. Dryer shall be sized to provide min. 38F dewpoint temperature for full flow of the existing LP Atlas Copco Air-Compressor GA90, Serial Number: AP1604921 at 125 psi. Contractor shall install required fuses, disconnect, motor starter if needed, and new wiring from disconnect. Contractor required to modify and add pipework as required to pipe new dryer. Piping shall be ASTM A53/A53M, Grade B carbon steel, Schedule 40, black. All pipes shall be painted with blue paint to match existing piping. All material shall be procured, installed, and tested per UFGS 43 15 00.00.   All piping shall be considered Class D service and installed per ASME B31.3. Target start date is November 4, 2024. Will need to review the scope/IGE prior to proceeding to Acquisition.

Requirement Title: CI / CRAISL-CI251/ DRAINAGE IMPROVEMENT AROUND THE TRUCK LOADING SHED
Requirement Description:
The existing truck loading facility drainage is deficient and the area floods during heavy rain events. 

A construction project in 2013 changed the drainage path from the area around the truck loading stand. The modification resulted in restricted flow from the area and caused the current flooding problem. The basic problem is the open ditch elevation, along the roadway, is not low enough to allow rain water to flow out of the area.  To correct this the open ditch needs to be replaced with buried drainage culvert. The underground culverts and open drainage ditches need to be modified and re-graded to allow proper flow in order to drain the area. This will require installing new underground drain piping, road culverts, drop inlets, and paving repairs where road cuts are made. The length of new drainage piping is approximately 900 feet and there are three road crossings.Current situation requires the area be manually pumped out to keep the truck loading area dry. When the area is not dry loading trucks is not possible. Design should be started in FY23 for construction award in Fy24.

Requirement Title: WBH285_IDIQ Paving_Sinkhole Project_White Beach, Okinawa Japan
Requirement Description:
1. Excavate/dispose and backfill with compaction and prepare the ground to required bedding surface for this project.

2. Replace existing asphalt pavement concrete structure with new including 50mm thick asphalt concrete course, 150mm thick sub base course, 100mm thick base course that will be affected by this project.

3. Provide shoring, including sheet piling to protect workmen, banks, adjacent paving, structures, fence line and utilities in accordance with Corps of Engineers manual EM 385-1-1.

4. Remove and dispose corroded existing SGP drainage pipes and install new Ribbed rigid PVC drainage pipes with fittings.

5. Provide 6 inches thick sand cushion all around new drainage pipes and marking tape for metal reaction detector type. 

6. Provide backfill of cavity with satisfactory materials by compaction.

7. Provide water sealing measures to new drainpipe connection points in existing catch basins.

8. Remove and dispose sediment from existing catch basin.

9. Temporary removal and restoration of a portion of the existing guardrail and posts affected by the construction. 

10. Provide temporary drainage system to maintain existing storm drainage flow during construction.

Requirement Title: OUTLYING - NCTPAC 242 - REMOVE UST AND CONSTRUCT AST
Requirement Description:
It is being observed throughout the state of Hawaii that many underground storage tanks (USTs) that are 25+ years old

are beginning to fail. Building 242 UTS was installed in 1998 (24 years). In addition, the building’s UTS is located above a

drinking water aquifer, the systems should be removed to prevent potential fuel releases into the water table. Our

command would like to initiate a project to remove the existing Underground Storage Tank (UST) and to design and

construct a replacement Aboveground Storage Tank (AST).

1. Permanently close the UST and associated tank system (e.g., piping, etc.) in accordance with Hawaii Administrative

Rules Title 11, Chapter 281 (HAR 11-281).

(a) Prior to closure, prepare written notification to be submitted to the State of Hawaii Department of Health (DOH) by

the Navy.

(b) Empty the UST and tank system by removing all liquid contents and accumulated sludge from the UST and

appropriate sections of tank system.

(c) Remove the UST and tank system (e.g., piping, etc.) from the ground. Excavate concrete, asphalt and/or soil as

necessary.

(d) Conduct a site assessment of the area beneath and around the UST and tank system in accordance with HAR

11-281-83.

(e) Permanently close the underground storage tank site.

(f) Prepare written closure report to be submitted to DOH by the Navy.

existing NPW System Tank 6, reducing the base's reliance on potable water for irrigation.

the installation of new connections, valves, and appurtenances. The proposed

construction includes the installation of approximately 5,650 LF of 12-inch diameter

recycled water main from the WWTP to the NPW System Tank 6, as well as extensions

and connections to Felix Field Complex, Lake Boomer, and Shadow Mountain Park.

Requirement Title: UM - REPLACE/RE-CONSTRUCT CHLORINATION DISINFECTION SYSTEM AND BLDG AT WAIAWA, HALAWA, AND NCTAMS PUMP STATIONS
Requirement Description:
Project to replace the existing chlorination system at Waiawa, Red Hill, and Halawa Fresh Water Pump Stations. The

replacement should include the following:

- On-Site Electrolytic Chlorination Skid-Mounted System

- Hypochlorite Generation System

The Waiawa, Red Hill, and Halawa Fresh Water Pump Stations collectively produce 100% of the fresh water that is

supplied to JBPHH. Per AWWA standards, a chlorination solution is injected into raw water for disinfection purposes.

Previously, the Navy would own and operate a ChlorTec sodium hypochlorite system at the three main water pump

stations. The hypoclorite system would produce the chlorine solution at the respective stations by introducing an

electrical current to a brine solution. However, current practice has been to purchase 330 gallon totes of a pre-made

chlorine solution. Due to supply issues, procuring the chlorine totes have become an issue, thus the need to return to

the hypochloride system. The hypochloride system would allow for a more reliable source of chlorine to meet

standards and regulations.

Project preference is for AE design and design-bid-build process. Project will require planning and EV documents; and

generation of design documents (i.e. basis of design, cost estimate, construction plans, specifications, etc.).

Requirement Title: REPAIR VALVE PITS ML1 TO ML6
Requirement Description:
Repair Valve Pits Repair Valve Pits ML-1, ML-2, ML-3, ML-4, ML-5, and ML-6.  These valve pits are along Santa Maria Street in the bulk fuel farm and contain all of the main, large diameter fuel pipelines.  The pits all have major water intrusion problems causing pipeline corrosion and the pits to be ineffective for containment.  Additionally, may of the pits have pipelines directly cast into the concrete, in violation of UFC and leading directly causing pitting corrosion, resulting in a leak and emergency repair and additional preventative repairs.  Proper repair of these valve pits will require extensive excavation, shoring, and de-watering to repair the pits.  Some of the pits were constructed without water stops and cold joints between the walls and floor.  In addition to correcting the water intrusion problems, the concrete walls need to be demolished where they are cast directly against the fuel pipes and sleeves and with elastomeric seals need to be installed.  



Valve Pits are part of the fuel pipeline, facility POLLF, RPUID 78051.

     a. Please see the enclosed "FY22 Inspection Report of Dry dock Facility conducted by NAVFAC PW5".

The current configuration of TSV/PSV's for the POL pipelines creates an unsafe cascading pressure condition. The set points and locations of the new TSVs shall prevent valves from opening during normal operation, yet still prevent an over-pressure event when main valves are closed. All provided TSVs shall be ANSI Class 150 or Class 300 to match piping class, and shall be flanged. TSV loops shall contain test tees and isolation all valves. Small bore piping shall be Sched 160 flanged/welded. All piping components shall be constructed of carbon or stainless steel.

Requirement Title: (UTIL) BARGO NEIGHBORHOODS REPLACE SEWER MAINS & MANHOLES (CNIC)
Requirement Description:
Replace existing Sewer pipe with HDPE sewer pipe main along with the existing sanitary sewer manholes to bring the system up to current UFC standards of construction. The work shall include: 

 Design build.  Excavate and replace approximately 6,800 linear feet of sewer mains.  Provide an imported fill material to be placed around the new sewer main piping.  Backfill and compact IAW the UFC.  Install warning tape. (maximum of 12 inches above new pipe).  Excavate and replace all manholes.  Grout and seal all pipe entrances into manholes to prevent inflow/infiltration of rain and ground water.  If necessary, raise the manhole cover to an elevation of 2 inches above the existing grade to prevent storm water runoff from pooling on and around the covers.  Provide sanitary sewer by-pass pumping as required to keep the system fully operational during the construction.  Laterals from houses are PVC.

Requirement Title: UM - Re-Construct Chlorination Bldg S75, Waiawa Pump Station
Requirement Description:
Re-Construct Waiawa Pump Station Chlorination Bldg S75. Existing facility is a 225 square feet, single-story, 3-sided CMU structure with double doors on one side (left photo below). Facility is used to stage chemical disinfectant totes for

potable water production. Foundation and rear wall on south side of facility is starting to crack due to differential

settlement (right photo below). In addition, existing facility does not have adequate storage space, resulting in

chemical disinfectant totes being stored exposed to the elements. A 2022 EPA audit listed this as a deficiency that is

required to be resolved.

Proposed reconstruction includes demolition of existing structure and building new stand alone structure 15 ft wide by

36 ft long, with concrete slab on grade, CMU walls, and metal beam roofing. Required utilities include appurtenant

electrical power and lighting. Facility shall be accessible via separate 2 doorways.

Project preference is for design-bid-build process and will require planning and EV documentation. Project will require

either in-house or A/E design documentation including but not limited to construction drawings, specifications, cost

estimate, basis of design and schedule. Project can either be constructed with JBPHH Shops or contractor.

Where:

Camp Smith Bldg 700 

B700 was built in 2003, No HAZMAT/No Historical concerns

Laydown areas will be provided as needed. 

No relocation necessary

In addition, the overhang located in the exterior near the supply room which is about 30’x40’ in size needs to be painted.  

Painting shall include but not be limited to exterior and interior walls, conduits, boxes, cabinets, piping, miscellaneous wiring, exterior exposed roof joists, roof eaves, roof fascia's, door frames, doors, and fire sprinkler risers shall be painted. The building is to be painted with premium paint with the colors to be selected by historical.

Requirement Title: INSTALL UNGULATE SKIRTING ON MAIN FENCE LINE, NAVFAC EV, NBG
Requirement Description:
PRIMARY OBJECTIVE



The primary objective of this project is to install fence skirting to the existing security fence, to exclude ungulates (Philippine deer and pigs) on Naval Base Guam (NBG), especially Camp Covington where there is potential habitat for Threatened or Endangered Species. The skirting will keep ungulates from browsing, rooting and trampling vegetation on NBG as well as keeping ungulates out of trash cans.



The project work plan shall include all of the necessary labor and equipment associated with meeting the objective.



Construction of the ungulate skirting require specifications detailed in Joint Region Marianas (JRM) Materials and Construction Standards for Ungulate Fencing on Guam and discussed in the PWS. This project area is located in a probability area of encountering Munitions Explosives of Concern (MEC)/Unexploded Ordnances (UXO).  The Contractor shall hire a UXO Contractor to survey the fence line for Anomaly Avoidance and Surface Clearance. 



See attached PWS, IGE and Figure

Requirement Title: UM - RM21-1405 Repair SWWCAAS near Bravo Docks B1 & B2
Requirement Description:
The existing 10-inch VCP line from sewer manholes (SMHs) D8 through D5 experiences oil/water infiltration through failed gaskets in the pipe joints and backwater conditions.  Low wastewater velocities and flow through conditions at SY-008 causes solids, debris, and oil to build up in upstream manholes.



The following scope of proposed work is provided:



1.  Install approximately 1000 feet of 6-inch pressure HDPE pipe through existing 10-inch VCP.

2.  Rehabilitate/replace SMHs D8, D7 and D6 and epoxy coat.

3.  Reconfigure SMHs D8 and D7 for new pressure line connection.

4.  Install transition SMH downstream of SY-008 to allow gravity flow to SMH D4.



New pressure line and rehabilitation/repair of the existing manholes will eliminate the oil infiltration from the current sewers constructed within IRP plume.

Requirement Description:
MSR 22683079 CAT2: DBB-AE  Design: Q1 FY24; Construction:   Q1 FY25



The Smallcraft Refueling Station by Olympic Pier need replacement of all refueling equipment and all services equipment to include hoses and electrical lines originating from the pier. 

The services equipment includes hoses and associated reels, and the electrical lines and associated reels.  These service hoses and electrical lines are getting battered between the pier and the floating refueling dock causing damage to the hoses and reels and creates fuel and SOD  spills to the Pugent Sound water.  



Redesign and Replacement of Services includes:



1. SOD Hose

2. Diesel Fuel Hose

3. Storm Drain Hose

4. Water Hose

5. LP Air Hose

5. CHT Hose

6. Three Electrical lines



Replacement of Smallcraft Refueling Station Assets/Equipment



1. Floating Dock, Collars, and Fenders (PORTOPS will purchase and provide) 

2. Three Diesel Refueling Station

3. SUMP Pumps

4. LP Air Station

5. SOD Pumps

6. Storm Drain Pumps

7. CHT Pumps

Requirement Description:

REQUESTED SCHEDULE: FY2024, SW

1391: Yes





1.    REQUIREMENT: 

Repair various deficiencies found during MDP overhaul. Contract# N44255-17-D-4015, RFI 17. 





1.    Replace pump bearing trough drain system with new piping. 

RFI NOTE: The pump bearing trough drain, which drains the cooling water from around the upper pump bearing, is completely clogged and will not drain. This pipe is an iron pipe that has internal build up from years of corrosion and is beyond repair. This issue was brought to our attention by the pump well operator and we field verified this issue. The current project scope of work has us reusing the trough drain piping. See Sheet M-501, Detail A4, Note 2 to identify location of trough drain. The complete pipeline is not shown on the drawings, but it runs the length of the pump well to pick up all 3 pumps and dump into the wet well. We recommend replacing this piping with new. Requires further guidance from the DOR. This would be additional work and would result in additional costs and schedule impact. 



2.    Replace pump vent system with new piping.  

RFI NOTE: The pump vent piping, which allows air to be vented out of the pump, is completely clogged and will not drain. The section of brass piping from the pump to the horizontal run is in good condition, but the iron pipe horizontal run has internal build up from years of corrosion and is beyond repair. This issue was brought to our attention by the pump well operator and we field verified this issue. The current project scope of work has us replacing only the vertical section from the pump to the horizontal run, but not the horizontal section of piping. Requirement Title: NSN CEP-186B OWWO Pump Station Renovations
Requirement Description:
The CT-4 OWWO pump station is located adjacent to the CEP-186B sanitary sewer pump which is equidistant between Cruiser and Escort Avenue. This station provides OWWO collection services for Piers 4-5.  There is no redundancy in service, as this is the only station that can be used for this coverage area.



Originally constructed in 1999, this submersible pump station is equipped with two 60 HP 460 V Yeomans pumps.  Yeomans pumps are no longer manufactured, and service parts are unavailable.  The intent of this project is to provide mechanical and electrical repairs to the CT-4 oily waste/waste oil (OWWO) pump station. NAVFAC Midlant UEM developed a prototype station renovation template which has been utilized at CT-3 and is also scheduled at CT-5 (Fall 2023 construction start). PWD Civil already has the existing CAD files for the awarded renovation of CT-5 OWWO station.



The general scope of work for the station includes but is not limited to:

Wet Well

•    Demolition and removal of existing pumps, level controls, power cables, guide rails, discharge elbows and brackets

•    Demolition and removal of power and control cables from the wet well

•    Installation of new pumps, rails, discharge piping, brackets and cabling. The new pumps have already been sized by NAVFAC Midlant UEM. No further hydraulic analysis is required.



Valve Vault

•    demolition and removal of existing valves, fittings, and magnetic flow meter

•    installation of new valves, fittings, limit switches, and magmeter



Top Side Work

•    removal and replacement of electrical cabling, conduit, and exterior junction box

•    new transducer, single level float, and NEMA 4 junction box (to be mounted flush with wet well top slab)

Requirement Title: 17303411, CONSTRUCT_Repair Drainage Around Tank Containment, B2910-T1, NASWI
Requirement Description:
DBB Construction project/follow up to SR# 13533102 A&E Study/Design to:

1) Analyze the effect of the high water level on the integrity and longevity of the Fuel Tanks and Flexible Membrane Liner containments. Study shall include review of Construction Drawings,for Swales & Drainage, previous Geotechnical Surveys and a Hydrologic Analysis.

2) Design a repair of the exterior drainage ditch/swale and increase the culvert size to allow for proper drainage.

3) If ground water level is determined to have a harmful impact to the fuel farm, design a dewatering system to provide adequate drainage around the tanks.

Justification: Swale backs up with excess water due to undersized swale and culvert pipe, as well as possibly due to improper slope.  Water is backing up under the tank containment liner for the fuel farm.

This is DLA-E Reimbursable Work.  Funding POC for labor and contract funding is Brice Frey, NAVFAC NW Regional POL Engineer, 360-476-1133

This project is for DLA-E Deficiency D.2018.000291

Requirement Title: MSR#20923176_1829890 -- (IH-DB_20923176) Modernize Passenger Elevator #3 Controls, B290, PSNS
Requirement Description:
BACKGROUND:

B290 Passenger Elevator #3 was replaced in its current configuration in 1976 and the operator controls were upgraded to Swift Controls in 1985. The operator controls are at the end of their life, causing the elevator to break down frequently. Elevator #3 is the main passenger elevator for the 9-stories of B290. Recently, the "BK" contactor failed, rendering the elevator inoperable. Nobody makes these anymore and the OEM (now TKElevator) says there are no substitutes manufactured; Swift parts are obsolete. Since Swift parts are no longer available, further delay on upgrading the controls for this elevator will jeopardize keeping it functional for the facility. Full modernization of the operator controls are required. 



SCOPE:  

Modernize/replace the following components of Passenger Elevator #3:

1) Roping

2) Door operator

3) Wearable door components

4) Machine (motor)

5) Add E-brake

6) Controls/drive

7) Fixtures & COP (Car Operating Panel)

8) Penthouse environmental controls 

9) Penthouse thermal upgrades (if needed for air conditioning for environmental controls. Similar to B460 East elevator penthouse upgrade)



Upgrades to the interior of the car are not included in this upgrade. This is intended to be a minimum upgrade to keep the mechanicals of the elevator in functioning order, not a beautification effort.

Requirement Title: RM23-0857 REPLACE 36 INCH WATERLINE ALONG PEARL HARBOR BIKE PATH
Requirement Description:
This project will replace approximately 15,300 linear feet (LF) of 36" cast iron water line transmission main with 36" pipe (material TBD in design) located along the Pearl Harbor bike path from Pearl City Peninsula (Lehua Avenue) to the Northern tip of Richardson Recreation Center (just past Aiea stream).  The pipeline is 68 years old and visual inspections at the various stream crossings displays severe deterioration and extensive corrosion.  Should this transmission main fail, the entire JBPHH potable water system will be severely compromised.



The existing water line will remain in service during construction and will be removed after the new water line installation is complete.



Project preference is for Design-Bid-Build.  Project will require updating planning and EV documents, and generation of design documents (i.e. basis of design, cost estimate, construction plans, specifications, etc).

King Fisher Transmitter Batteries

Reciever KF In-house programming

Coaxial Cable transmitter to Antenna - LMR 400 Cable Low Noise - 150'

New Addressable FACP to replace existing noncompatible conventional panel.

Conventional circuit adapters

This project will replace the existing deteriorated asphalt/concrete road intersection with concrete located at BSVE, approximately 560 square meters. The scope of this project are the following but not limited to:

2. Sawcut, break, remove and dispose existing deteriorated

asphalt/concrete road including unsuitable base material.

4. Provide new 200mm [8-inches] thick concrete with 100mm [4-inches] thick satisfactory base course material complete with required joints & formworks.

5. Provide reinforcing bars for portions of road that are required to be reinforced.

6. Provide standard road markings.

7. Grade surrounding area of the new road for proper drainage and water run-off.

8. Provide all required road signage, safety and traffic control,

equipment and its operator to perform and accomplish all tasks.

9. Incidental related works.

Notes:

1. Road shall be repaired one lane at a time to allow continuous flow of traffic and avoid rerouting.

Requirement Title: Construction award for UM-Replace 12-In Water Line near O'Malley Gate, Hickam
Requirement Description:
Project proposes to replace approximately 1,650 linear feet of 12 inch asbestos cement pipe near the O'Malley Gate entering Hickam AFB. 



The original pipe was installed in 1943 and has served beyond the typical 50 year life span.  The line provides water to various residential units, fire protection, and flight line facilities.  The existing water line is directly below the freeway off ramp.  Any failures to the existing line will result in loss of water to critical facilities.  In addition repair work for this line will require extensive methods and will impact traffic around the main gate entering Hickam AFB.



New piping shall be PVC or polyethylene wrapped cement mortar-lined ductile iron.  Due to the proposed alignment for the new water line, portions of this project may prefer the micro-tunneling construction method.  All other portions may be installed via open trenching.



Project preference is for AE design and design-bid-build process.  Project will require a charette to confirm the design scope; planning and EV documents; and generation of design documents (i.e. basis of design, cost estimate, construction plans, specifications, etc.)

Requirement Title: REPLACE WASTE WATER SANITARY SEWER PIPELINE AT CAPO SS-SA-2
Requirement Description:
A CCTV survey performed on 2019, including inspection of the sanitary sewer line between B440 (C4I) and B453, has reported the following issues:

-) Pipe misalignment and cracks in different sections leading to waste water infiltrating in the surrounding subsoil (IFGS C4.3.1.6.).

-) Pipe ovalization and inflection, thus leading to the loss of positive gradient, wastewater stagnation and even backflows at the sewage laterals (UFC 3-240-01 Chapter 3-3.2 Section 33.41).

-) Lateral connections with no junction manhole (UFC 3-240-01 Chapter 3-3.3 Section 34.1)

-) Manholes obstructed by coarse heterogeneous waste, including construction material (e.g. wooden formwork elements).



Requirement is to provide all labor, materials and supervision to:                                                                                                                                                     

-) Replace and re-design the D200 (8”) sanitary sewer piping, including manholes and all related fittings and components, from the B440 connection manhole “P0” to the junction manhole “F15” on the main line between B461 (East Parking garage) and B453 (NGIS). 

-) Replace the following laterals:

        Connection serving B442B and B442A from pit “F4” to pit “F6”

        Connection serving B452, from pit “F9” to the pipeline. 

-) Install junction manhole at the following connection points:

        At the junction between B452 lateral and sewage main

        At the junction between B463 lateral and sewage main

        At the junction between B451 lateral and sewage main

Requirement Title: WR 177109 B7064 TASK ORDER TO REPLACE HOT WATER PIPING
Requirement Description:
Please include "WR 177109" in the title for MCBH tracking purposes.

General Scope:  Replace existing deteriorated above ground and buried insulated hot water supply and return piping from boiler plant 7064 to barracks 7061, 7062 and 7063.  Provide new buried insulated hot water supply and return piping.  Provide new copper, type-K insulated supply and return piping buried underground from the barracks’ valve boxes to the boilers’ supply and return piping.  Protect buried piping from vehicular traffic.  Replace existing isolation valves on the return lines, balancing valves on the supply lines, hot water circulation pump, check valve and provide new thermostatic valve on the main hot water supply piping to the barracks to ensure hot water does not exceed 120F.  Install new Double Check Valve Assembly to protect makeup potable water line to the hot water storage tank.  Replace existing potable water shut off valve, hot water supply balancing (globe) valves, hot water return isolation (ball) valves, and hot water check valve.  Provide other valve(s), piping and fittings as required for proper hot water system operation.  Insulate all hot water piping after leak testing is complete.



See attached SOW and 7064 Boiler Plant location for further details.

Requirement Description:
1.    Coordinate gravity line outage with UEM and OWWO treatment plant staff.

2.    Install a 6-inch x 4-inch flange x cam-lock adapter at the 6-inch drain valve

3.    Temporarily provide 60 feet of 4-inch hard hose to direct flow to adjacent catch basin.  This catch basin drains to the T-9 OWWO pump station and not the storm collection system.  OWWO plant personnel will operate the drain valve and lower the tank levels.

4.    Demolish and replace one 12-inch eccentric plug valve with hand wheel actuator and one 12-inch lug style pneumatically operated butterfly valve with pneumatic actuator

5.    Valves and gasket material shall be compatible with petroleum products.  Both the eccentric plug valve and butterfly shall have nitrile internal components. 

6.     Reconnect existing the pneumatic line to the butterfly valve actuator. 

7.    Reinsulate the two new valves, one existing valve and adjacent fittings.

T-1 PIPE REPLACEMENT 

3.    UEM assumes that the PIV located directly outside the station will not adequately secure flow.  UEM assumes the PIV’s located adjacent to Tank T2D will be the appropriate valves to secure. As such, there will be 12,000 gallons of OWWO product in the line.

a.    remove 12-inch check valve and install 6-inch cam-lock connection

b.    drain product through 6-inch hard hose back to T-1 wet well

c.    reinstall existing 12-inch check valve

Work will include removal, disposal, and replacement of 12-inch diameter (approximately 10,662 LF) and 14-inch diameter (approximately 4,000 LF) ACP with new 12 to 14 inch diameter inch heat fused joint Polyvinyl Chloride (PVC) pipe, associated fittings, gate valves, meter, metering vaults, manholes, thrust blocks, taping backfill and compaction. The project includes and but not limited to clearing, cutting, trenching, excavation, removal, disposal and restoration of roadway including asphalt pavement, Portland cement concrete, base course, sub base and sub grade. Water supply service shall remain active during construction of the replacement and maybe accomplished by installing a temporary water transmission line.

Requirement Title: NWC Road and Parking Lot Repairs
Requirement Description:
NWC B_52 Address drainage issues at the intersection of the Schonland Hall and Hewitt Hall Gravel Parking Lots.

NWC Schonland Hall storm drainage system has multiple underground failures resulting in ponding water/flooding parking lots.  NWC internal investigation revealed CB 3-164B to CB 3-164C has multiple roots penetrating the underground piping, several sections of piping no longer connected.  CB 3-164C to CB 3-164A has multiple sections of piping no longer connected.  CB 3-164A is failing, brickwork is collapsing, piping from 3-164A to 3-164 was unable to pass camera due to obstructions.  CB 3-164 was removed during a prior project and not reinstalled.  CB 3-163 to 3-164, piping is separated in several sections, CB 3-163 to 3-162 piping is separated in several areas.  Requesting IDIQ contractor replacing all piping from CG 3-164 to 3-162, remove/replace CB C-164A, to be inline with new piping, install CB 3-164 to be inline with new piping.  See attached PDF with locations	

Also: Repaving of Luce Ave, to the west of Pringle to Hewitt. And Perform miscellaneous road, parking lot, sidewalk, and exterior stair repairs.  Locations include sidewalk and stairs at McCarty Little Hall and various sidewalks.

3. PROJECT TITLE: Remove and Replace plumbing in the Pipe Chasewall PH1518

4. IMPACT: Old and deteriorated piping for cold water, domestic hot water and

Drain, Waste and Vent is severely corroded and needs replacement throughout the

pipe chase walls of the facility. Multiple issues arise from inadequate design or

deterioration of systems well exceeding life-cycle of equipment. Installing booster

pumps to alleviate low water pressure issues from municipal feed. Installing

domestic hot water circulation system ensures troops on 3rd deck receive adequate

hot water service vice needing to wait for 1st floor occupants to clear. Replacing

DWV system and clearing obstructions for sewer alleviates constant work order

callouts.

Requirement Title: UM - RM23-1481 - SLUDGE THICKENING IMPROVEMENTS AT JBPHH WWTP
Requirement Description:
This project combines UM - WW - REPLACE WWTP SUBNATANT PIPING and UM - INSTALL DRUM THICKENERS AT JBPHH WWTP projects.



Scope for Subnatant Piping:

Scope involves constructing a replacement 8-inch subnatant force main from the Disolved Air Flotation Tanks System Subnatant Wetwell Pump Station to the Influent Channel of the Anoxic/Aeration Tanks.  Work will include trenching and installing approximately 140 feet of new HDPE force main, connecting the force main to the existing subnatant pumps, and coring a hole through the wall of the influent channel and affixing the new pipe end in place.  The existing force main is severely corroded and has recently (within the last nine months) broken several times; each time, a spill is recorded and reported to the State Department of Health.



Scope for Drum Thickeners:

Justification: Induction of this project is required due to the recent Notice of Violation Order (NOVO) for the WWTP. Several deficiencies were identified that need to corrective action which involves repairs.



Project scope involves: purchasing and installing two new drum thickeners outside of the existing dissolved air floatation tanks (DAFTs) building; connecting primary sludge and waste activated sludge lines to inlet of floculation tanks for drum thickeners; connecting polymer tote to polymer feeder; connecting drum thickener outlet to existing sludge transfer pumps; connecting power to new drum thickeners.

Requirement Title: WATERFRONT - CBMM - B 1341 HVAC REPLACEMENT & REDUNDANCY INSTALLATION
Requirement Description:
This project will remove and replace the deteriorated heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) system at Building 1341 (B1341) SUBPAC Admin N7 at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii.



The mechanical scope of work includes the replacement of two air cooled chillers, two chilled water pumps, first floor central air handling unit (AHU-1), and two AHUs in Rooms 112 and 111/113. The main ductwork from AHU-1 to adjacent Room 116 will be replaced and remaining AHU-1 ductwork will be duct cleaned and external insulation will be reinsulated. Additionally, chilled water piping and ductwork serving Rooms 112 and 111/113 will be replaced. Replace chilled water piping to Room 102 AHU and failed chilled water piping insulation in various areas. The existing direct digital control (DDC) system will be replaced. Interface existing and installed equipment to the new DDC.



The electrical scope of work includes removal of the existing power connections, new power connections to the installed equipment, and removal and reinstallation of light fixtures as required for the ductwork re-insulation.



The architectural scope of work includes ceiling tile replacements for the ductwork reinsulation

and patch and repair work.

Requirement Title: WR 177129 QTC B212 REMOVE AND REPLACE ROOFING P2 of 2
Requirement Description:
B212 WEST SIDE SELECT ROOF REMOVE AND REPLACEMENT

Remove and replace approximately 918SF of built-up roof materials and rafters by select demolition of the deteriorated roof system. Barracks Manager Gary Johnson to clear spaces to access construction areas. Contractor to remove old scullery equipment and terminate electrical at the circuit breaker box. Provide safety fencing around laydown area and areas under deconstruction.

Scope:

1.1 Coordinate demolition schedule with B212 users.

1.2 Test all materials for LCM and ACM substances.

1.3 Terminate all electrical at the circuit breaker box.

1.4 Remove and dispose of old scullery equipment.

1.5 Stage equipment and dumpster at the laydown area.

1.6 Cut roof into sections and load into the dumpster.

1.7 Remove and replace all wood rafters. (Rafter architectural details to be matched for historical purposes). 

1.8 Remove and replace ceiling joists/flat roof portion. Approx. 800SF

1.9 Install roof sheathing. Approx. 1000SF

1.10 Install new BUR on pitched roof and flat roofs.

1.11 Prep prime and paint all new exterior construction.

1.12 Cleanup interior and exterior areas.

1.13 Restore the laydown area and grounds to original conditions.



Request work be sent to contract.

Site visit mandatory.

For the safety of their employees,the contractor will be responsible to sample/test ( and abate,if necessary ) any suspected hazardous material in the areas covered on the contract.

TITLE:     SUPSIT 314 Replace Exterior Sewer Line /UEM URT



1.    CURRENT CONDITION / refer to the attached sketches:

•    UEM reports several overflow issues form sewer manhole 159 (UEM ID=MH#11)

•    Manhole 159 is located between sewer manholes 185 (MH#10) and 98 (MH#12)

•    Sewer line from manhole MH-11 to Manhole MH12 may suffer of roots infestation, which may cause clogging. 

•    Estimated length of the sewer line is about 10mt.



2.    BASIC REQUIREMENT: 

•    Clear area from vegetation.

•    Excavate area to expose and remove existing 200mm sewer pipe (cement and/or PVC)

•    Replace existing with new 200mm diameter.

•    Test and backfill



3.    DESCRIPTION OF WORK:

3.1    Provide required actions (labor, equipment, material, transportations, excavations, site restorations, etc.) to replace the existing partially obstructed sewer pipe.

3.2    The work includes, but is not limited to, the following actions:

Excavate area in order to allow sufficient safety space for the repair/replacement operations of the existing sewer piping.

•    As CDC building 314 will remain in operation during the execution of the work, the Contractor shall provide temporary sump pump and piping to drain the effluents from manhole MH10 to existing underground 300mm sewer line. Refer to attached Utilities plans.

•    Expose and remove Drainage line from Manhole MH11 to Manhole MH12 approx. length 10mt; Remove existing pipe and replace with new. 

•    Connect the new pipe to the existing manholes. 

•    Test for proper drainage flow.

•    Backfill trench with sand and restore topsoil.

•    Restore top surface to match original landscape conditions

Requirement Title: NSN CRAISL CI-294 OWWO TREATMENT PLANT UPGRADES
Requirement Description:
This project will systematically overhaul the central components of the treatment plant to ensure adequacy and resiliency to operations for the foreseeable future.  Specifically, the scope of work will include: 

1) cleaning and coating system overhaul for all basins and oil water separators, 

2) replacement of pumps, piping, and controls for primary pump station, 

3) valve and vault overhaul for holding tanks and reactor basins, 

4) replacement of aeration system components including blowers, controls, and piping system, 

5) spall and crack repair to basins and concrete structures, 

6) installation of new chemical feed systems, 

7) replacement of catwalks and accesses, 

8) replacement of control and power conduits throughout the facility, 

9) overhaul of PLC and SCADA control system, 

10) replacement of decant arms in each reactor basin, 

11) overhaul of facility compressor system and desiccant dryers, and 

12) installation of new backup power generator.

Requirement Description:
Please include "WR 177111" in the title for MCBH tracking purposes.

Furnish labor and materials to repair the 2ea Cooling Towers at Bldg 7243, located at MCBH.  Mechanical Repairs (Elite)

1. Preset and assemble fan blade with pitch at the shop.

2. Setup safety barriers for Crane (will need to backup Crane from main road).  Lift shall comply with P-307

3. LOTO, shut down and drain down cooling tower.

4. Remove fan grille and build platform on fills to create a stable work station to access fan assembly.

5. Disconnect electrical wiring from the motor and disassemble.

6. Remove old motor and fan blades by using crane, hoist up new motor and fan blades then set into place.

7. Connect wiring for new motor, install new fan blades and hub. Will adjust pitch of blades if needed.

8. Remove and replace expansion tank.

9. Remove LOTO, startup and test for normal operations.

10. Provide 2ea spare chill water pump motors and 2ea spare condenser water pump motors.

Electrical

1. Run new conduits to new bucket location by the adjacent wall across from MCC. Mount 4ea ABB VFDs

(2ea per CT).

2. Shut down power and LOTO. Disconnect and abandon 4 buckets.

*Preform pre-check with Base's Main Power Electricians before shut down and for start up.

3. Connect and tie in wire for new VFDs.

4. Remove LOTO, startup, program and check for normal operations for the VFDs.

DOC

1. Program and confirm proper connection of newly installed VFDs to the DDC.

Requirement Description:
Provide the complete D/B/B to convert the existing B3049 (RBC) HVAC instrumentation, field control devices, and

building control systems to fully functional, Direct Digital Control (DDC) systems. The building has unique

architectural, structural, and mechanical requirements to reflect safety objectives as required for blast and

contamination isolation zones, shock and gas overpressure loads, HVAC and air purge systems. Technical Note

(CUI/DCRIT/UCNI) N-1706 (Basis of Design for Explosives and Contamination Safety of MCON Project P-312M,

Reentry Body Complex, SWFLANT, Kings Bay, GA) contains those requirements. The design shall assure

compliance with Basis of Design explosive and contamination safety requirements from maximum credible events

(explosions) from inside and out. Any departure from design criteria and any conflicts with other compliance

documents shall be submitted for review and approval. Consideration must be given to: (1) original existing

design based on electro-pneumatic, NOVAR digital systems, building wide analog and digital data communication

networks; (2) recently installed partially functional but incompletely tested DISTECH based HVAC control system

with electronic analog and digital field devices, BACnet components, controllers, networks, and workstations; (3)

provide for the conversion and integration of all ancillary systems such as but not limited to; Event Initiated,

Environmental Emergency Shutdown, and Purge System to fully functional DDC systems, with a hardened

communications network as dictated to provide for their safe, reliable operation during emergency conditions.

Requirement Title: ELECTRICAL INFRASTRUCTURE, ON-SITE GENERATION, AND MICROGRID IMPROVEMENTS
Requirement Description:
Proposed construction for this Marine Corps Air Station Miramar (MCASM) project includes the following: 

1 MW of solar photovoltaics, a 1.9 MW battery energy storage system (BESS), 1.4 MW of standby generators and associated interconnections, modernization of underground electrical distribution infrastructure to include high voltage electrical connections, cabling, and manholes, microgrid controls, other supporting systems (metering, remote terminal units, and uninterruptable power supplies), cybersecurity and other general requirements, such as baselining system performance. 



Supporting work includes communications infrastructure, specifically fiber optic cable on all six major power distribution loops across 100 electric pads.

Requirement Description:
- Perform necessary engineering investigation to determine source or cause of apparent floor slab moisture presence. 

- The technical library houses essential records (construction as-builts and OMSIs) in hard copies and digital formates for Naval Base Guam. The volume of these records are increasing. Additionally, Marine Corps Base Camp Blaz records are expected to be accepted and archived. In anticipation for the volume increase and planned space modernization a thorough investigation to the root-cause of floor moisture is crucial.

- Direct water damage and/or improper relative humidity percentage is cause for poor paper preservation. Source: NISO TR-01-1995 Environmental Guidelines for Storage of Paper Records.

- Possible cause: Exterior grade changes (lawn growth, building addition) appears to have altered the topography creating detrimental elevation differences leading to poor drainage flow to existing catch basins. Drain lines from numerous building air condition systems add to the continuous water presence along the building perimeter, thus even during rain-less periods the surrounding grade is saturated and percolates down as opposed to being properly sloped to promote positive conveyance to nearest catch basin. Current soil permeability and hydrology is unknown.

- Known history: The most recent floor renovation was done in 2013. Within a year, various areas of the newly installed vinyl tiles started popping out of place within months. Source: Technical Librarian Virginia Limtiaco.

- Current condition: Duct tape holds tile in place with other tile and attempts to mitigate tripping hazard.

Requirement Title: WATERFRONT - CBMM - SUBTRACENPAC - B 1262 CHILLER REPLACEMENTS
Requirement Description:
This project will remove and replace the deteriorated air cooled chillers and chilled water pumps at Building 1262 (B1262) Submarine Training Center Pacific and Building 1378 (B1378) Technical Training at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH), Hawaii.



The mechanical scope of work includes the replacement of five air cooled chillers, chilled water pumps and associated chilled water piping. Provide N+1 chiller redundancy for each building and right size the new chillers to current and future B1262 and B1378 air conditioning (AC) loads. Update the existing direct digital control (DDC) for the new sequence of operation and installed equipment.



The electrical scope of work includes removal of the existing power connection and new power connection to the chillers and pumps.



The cybersecurity features scope of work includes connecting the existing DDC to the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Hawaii's (NAVFAC HI) control system platform enclave (CSPE) for cybersecurity of Facility-Related Control Systems (FRCS).



The architectural scope of work includes patch work and paint associated with the

installed equipment and chilled water piping.

Requirement Title: MSR #23207821_1787796 -- (23207821) Repair Crane Track and Tunnel Arch Support DD1, PSNS
Requirement Description:
AE design required



Seismic upgrades to the superstructure and substructure include: retrofit of original

building brace connections, restroom modifications, American Barrier Act elements, heat

and ventitlation along with removal and reinstallation of architectural, electrical,

mechanical interferences Seismic upgrades also includes removing and re-installing

interfering plant equipment, shop equipment, lockers, cabinets, ventilation, work

benches, offices and storage racks.

This project upgrades high-bay power distribution panel boards to allow for installation

of a 480VAC, three phase grounded system. This project corrects numberous documented HDA

safety hazard deficiencies RAC 2, RAC 3 and RAC 4 electrical and structural deficiencies.

Station support includes red badge escort, outage coordination, assistance with

hazardous material handling, and a facility production process specialist to assist with

overall project coordination.

Seismic upgrades shall be compliant with the Unified Facility Code (UFC), National Fire

Protection Association (NFPA), and International Building Code (IBC), economical to

maintain and operate, durable and shall fit its use and its surroundings. The machine

shop is on the historical register and requires State Historical Preservation Office

(SHPO) review and concurrence on all facility projects to retain the historical era of

the building.

Seismic upgrades shall be designed to meet or exceed the useful service life specified in

DoD Unified Facility Criteria. Seismic upgrades will incorporate features that provide

the lowest practical life cycle cost solutions satisfying the facility requirements with

the goal of maximizing energy efficiency.

Requirement Description:
NCIS WILL BE TAKING OVER THESE TRAILERS.



The 5 trailers reserved for NCIS staff require security reinforcements and minor interior renovations in order for NCIS to meet the mission requirements.  The security reinforcements shall include perimeter fence that encompasses all trailers with two controlled access points (one for NCIS Staff entrance/exit and one for visitor entrance/exit).  The minor interior renovations shall include repairs on damaged floors and ceilings and cosmetic surfaces, cut loose wires, replace all outlet protrusions on the floors with covers that are flush to the surface of the floors, install TV hanging brackets, and general cleaning and sanitization.





The Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS) is the Department of the Navy’s (DoN) primary law enforcement arm.  Due to the growth of field office, the Sexual Harassment Squad of 40+ staff will be occupying the newly acquired trailers.  In order to carry out their mission effectively and with safety and security concerns, security measurements must be provided to protect the staff and the infrastructural assets. The nature of NCIS work requires additional specialty areas such as victim interview rooms, evidence processing rooms, private offices for supervisory and special agents, professional support staff offices, training classrooms, forensics/IT/computer rooms, conference rooms, and various other required spaces for investigative operations.

-1 -D607 = C200’s Office, 2 -B100 = FLCN Gym HVAC, 3 -E613/E614 = ALL old Rice King HVACs (4 HVACs), 4 -B619 = C400 Transportation Office, 5 -B108 = C500 ILO Supervisor Office, 6 -C608 = PAO’s HVAC, 7 -B629 = C00 Main FLC Security Office, 8 -E600 = NFMT’s Offices & Admin HVACs (2 HVACs), 9 -E604 = NFMT’s small galley , 10 -A601/A602 = Code 500 Director/Deputy Offices, 11 -A603 = C300 Augment Division, 12 -B616 = C200 Solomon Robinson’s Office, 13 -F600, F601 and F602 = C200 PPMAPS (2 HVACs), 14 -C617 = Human Resources Office 





These HVAC units are 15-30 years old and are becoming unreliable to cool and heat the administration spaces.  This causes many employees to experience temperatures not conducive for working at a computer, which can impact their productivity and quality of work.  This also lowers employee’s morale in the workplace and can cause union issues.  Heat exhaustion is also a concern when temperatures rise as high as the mid to upper 80’s in the office spaces.  Limited ability to cool the spaces with temporary A/C’s really do not suffice for the length of time the units are down.  New units will help support energy conservation, as the units will provide much more efficient operating capabilities that will help cut monthly electrical utility costs.

Requirement Description:
Provide architectural and engineering (A-E) services for the development and finalization of this project's DD1391; and complete A-E services to provide full design and construction documentation for providing pavement repairs at 1st Street.  Work shall include but not be limited to road repair and restriping; repairs to curb and gutters; and traffic

control during construction. Visually, this section of pavement is experiencing raveling and aging (pavement surface deterioration), alligator cracking (fatigue cracking), potholes, and areas of settlement.  The paved roadway system is documented on the Property Records as having been originally constructed in 1940. All areas within this project shall be in compliance with applicable ATFP, Fire Suppression, Seismic, Accessibility, ASHRAE, and LEEDs standards (as required) upon completion of the project.  Work shall also include but not be limited to communicating and coordinating with all MCBH stakeholders and NAVFAC agencies involved with this project, along with setting up design presentations and meetings, distributing deliverables and thorough/complete site surveys and investigations. The MCBH Design & Construction Standard (dated 11 Feb 2021) shall be followed as well as any updated documents.

Requirement Description:
This TF-1 is for a complete design package to include cost estimate for the renovation of the CBM+ ES Lab located in Bldg. 1000 Rms. 253 & 255. Design shall include all necessary modifications, alterations, and upgrades required to support the lab mission and to bring the space into compliance with all applicable codes and standards. 

 

Lab renovations requested include:

1. Raised floor in both rooms to improve cable management, ability to route cables between Rms 253 & 255 is required. Cables are Zone D-type. Ramp shall be in RM255.

2. Double-wide door shall be installed connecting the two rooms

3. Server room is required in RM 253 lab space. HVAC & ventilation shall be evaluated. CRAC unit cooling option should be evaluated. Equipment list from the tech code to follow.

4. Power receptacle height shall be modified to account for the raised floor. Additional power receptacles may be required. 

5. Lab entrances shall be CAC-enabled. 

6. CBM+ ES Lab Equipment list & lab layout will be provided.

Requirement Description:
Request FEC preparation of DB RFP and contract award and FEAD construction contract administration for a major renovation of the MWR Clubs and Food Court at B261.  Project is approved for FY25 funding and execution with NAF funds via the HQ CNIC NAF Capital Investment Board.  Concept sketches attached

Club 261 - complete renovate, upgrade and modernize.  Replace all finishes floor, wall, demo ceiling soffits.  Replace lights.  Relocate the bar to the center of the room.  Provide new DJ booth and stage location.  Build in karaoke\special reservation rooms.  Upgrade the entry way from the main corridor.  Upgrade finishes in the hallway to the exterior of the building and provide a new pergola\pavilion to extend the bar patron area outside behind the building.

Officer's Club - replace all flooring, wall coverings, and ceiling.  Provide new lights.  Remove wood paneling and half walls and modernize\re-build the bar.

Chiefs' Mess - replace all flooring, wall coverings, and ceiling, provide new lights, Remove wood paneling and modernize\re-build the bar.

Outer Food Court Corridor - replace all flooring and wall finishes with modern materials

Food court dining area\inner food court - replace all flooring and wall finishes to tie seamlessly with the outer food court corridor.  Replace lighting in the dining area

All areas - adjust fire sprinkler piping to accommodate new work, upgrade electrical and plumbing as needed to support the new scope.  Replace existing CHS pipe insulation in areas of work performed to eliminate condensation and dripping in these areas.  Rearrange any ductwork and diffusers that need to be moved to accommodate the new work.  

Desire is to award by EOFY25.  If FEC does not have capacity, could this be accomplished with PWD Architect lead with reach back to the FEC?

Requirement Title: DB Construction; Stand Alone: P1241 Communication Towers; Twentynine Palms MCAGCC
Requirement Description:
Constructs four steel lattice-type communication towers with support systems comprised of

pipe mast legs, horizontal braces and diagonal braces acting in tension and compression.

Towers to be integrated with ground mounted photovoltaic primary power system and

reinforced shallow concrete foundations for a supporting equipment shelter.

Recapitalizes and repairs seven communication towers in disrepair. Tower repairs consist

of replacement of missing and damaged bolts, washers, nuts, re-tensioning of loose guy

cables, replacement of deteriorated ground bus bars, re-weatherproofing of existing

antennas, re-galvanization of eroded parts and cracked foundation repair.

Requirement Title: (IH-DBB_21225817) Design and Install Drainage Water Diffuser, Bremer-706, PSNS
Requirement Description:
DELIVERABLE: CAT-2, IH-DBB TO PRI4, 

REQUESTED SCHEDULE: FY2026

LOCATION: Dry Dock 6, BREMER-706, PSNS

1391: No

In Water

REQUIREMENT: 

Design and install a drainage outfall diffuser. 



1.    Design the diffuser to meet C/106 requirements. 

2.    Model design using C/106 software

3.    Contract construction of the diffuser. 











NOTES:



JUSTIFICATION:

The NPDES permit copper limits are set by multiplying the copper water quality standard (4.8 parts per billion) and a dilution factor that is determined by how well the dry dock outfall discharge mixes with the water in Sinclair Inlet (calculated by modeling software).  The more rapidly the dry dock discharges mix in the Inlet, the higher the dilution factor, and the higher the limits.  In order to keep the NPDES permit limits as high as possible and increase our ability to maintain compliance with the permit, we need to make sure these outfalls dilution factors are high.  



In their current condition, the dilution factors at the dry dock outfalls are so low that the resulting NPDES permit copper limits would be nearly impossible for PSNS & IMF to maintain compliance with.  These diffusers will significantly increase the mixing of dry dock outfall discharges and ensure NPDES copper limits are high enough for PSNS & IMF to maintain compliance with the NPDES permit.

Repair/replace plumbing, intrusion detection and automatic access control and fire alarm/mass notification systems as current systems do not meet code/regulations.



Repair Operator's office has sever termite damage, deteriorating plumbing, life safety, FA/MNS, fire suppression deficiencies and security/access control issues.

Requirement Title: DLA-POL Replace Kuahua Truck Loading Rack, FAC S582, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
The existing Kuahua Truck Load Rack (S582) and accompanying canopy (493) at Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam is incapable of safely meeting operational demands and supporting the mission.  The load rack is the primary support for all Pacific sites located on Oahu, which support four (4) different products, F-76, F-24, JP-5 and FOR.  The Pacific sites include USCG Barbers Point, MCBH Kaneohe Bay, Schofield Superstation and Wheeler Army Airfield.  The facility has both loading and offloading capabilities for all four types of product, with multiple fuel source capabilities.



Due to outdated design and fuel components, this facility requires an overhaul.  NAVSUP FLCPH is seeking repairs to facility to bring in line with current codes, technologies, and industry standards; some of the identified repairs are as follows.  The fill stand is currently located in a trench that is inefficient and requires constant repair and maintenance and is open to elements.  Existing canopy support structure is all that remains of the canopy, no cover left to protect the facility.  Lack of cover has accelerated the degradation of the facility.  Fuel additive injection system has failed.  Overfill prevention system is outdated.  Parking for fuel trucks will also need to be examined as the existing containment does not seem to be up to code.  Additionally, the routing of fuel trucks may need to be examined to allow for pull-through operations as required.  The records building requires repair.  Lastly, security of the facility and automation of egress gates will need to be researched.

Requesting Design Team to determine best approach for repairing the existing truck load rack facility to meet operational requirements in accordance with applicable County, State, and Federal guidelines. Work to include design and repairs to facility and coordination with agencies for tie-in with existing AFHE, fire protection, and security systems.

Requirement Title: NSWC PNYA Bldg 1000 - DDG‐51 MCS 4 Lab
Requirement Description:
NSWC PNYA Bldg 1000 - DDG‐51 MCS 4 Lab 

This TF-1 is to complete a detailed design and cost estimate for a new lab space to support DDG-51 MCS 4. The intended location for the new lab space is located in the Northeast corner of the second floor of Bldg. 1000. Currently rooms 283-285, 254A, & 256 - 258 are being considered to meet the requirement. The design shall evaluate combining the spaces to create 1 to 3 new lab areas to support the DDG-51 MCS 4 lab requirements. Design shall include modifications and alterations necessary to support the lab requirements and to bring the space(s) into compliance with current codes and standards. The intent is for the lab space(s) to utilize raised floors and be capable of supporting a modular or adjustable lab layout. Design shall include HVAC, mechanical / electrical / plumbing, fire alarm & suppression, egress / access, etc.



Requested award date is Q4 FY25. Requested period of performance is 9 months or less.

Requirement Description:
The basic SOW is to demolish Facility 548 and in its place, provide an adequately-sized fuel maintenance workshop with shelving, work bench, compressed air, lighting, electrical outlets. Project to provide slip and fuel-resistant floor, emergency shower and eyewash station. The new POL workshop/operations/storage building size is to be determined by design team in coordination with PMRF Fuels.



Currently, PMRF does not have a fuel maintenance workshop or storeroom facility as required by UFC 3-460-01, CH 11. The existing 242-SQ FT Facility 548 is non-compliant building as it is constructed of wood and is inappropriately being used for maintenance and storage of fuel parts and spill response equipment. The site has received a Fire Deficiency citation (attached).



The new facility shall be in compliance with the latest edition of all federal, state, local, and military codes, instructions, manuals, handbooks, regulations, and other guidance/policy documents, as applicable. Apply UFC 3-460-01 POL Design, UFC-1-200-01 General Building Design, UFC 3-600-01 Fire Protection requirements and NFPA, NEC codes as required.

The roofing contract did not include the work to extend the vent ductwork to the new roof plane to exhaust to atmosphere. The vent systems have been exhausting into the building's overhead/attic space since the roof was replaced, causing an air quality issue within the building. This is a RAC-3 deficiency and is being tracked by C/106 under HDA# 20200116. Even though this is a RAC-3 deficiency, C/106 does not have any temporary mitigation requirements for the exhaust air being recirculated in the building. Nonetheless, these systems still needs to be exhausted to the outside atmosphere.

Requirement Title: REPLACE HAND RAILS AND METAL PLATFORMS, SASA VALEY and TENJO VISTA, NBG
Requirement Description:
REQUEST NAVFAC SRM TO REPLACE NON-COMPLIANT HAND RAILING SYSTEM AND METAL STAIR PLATFORMS ON UNDERGROUND SASA FUEL STORAGE TANKS .  



CURRENT CONDITION

UPPER SASA VALLEY UST - There are 2 handrails and metal stair platform per tank, total of 20 Underground Storage Tanks, constructed by Navy Seabees Reserve personnel.  These handrails are not within standard height, metal platforms not having handrails, both combined making it unsafe for Fuels Operators to grab on during entry and exiting!



TENJO VISTA UST - There are 3 handrails and metal stair platform per tank, total of 7 Underground Storage Tanks, constructed by Navy Seabees Reserve personnel.  These handrails are not within standard height, metal platforms not having handrails, both combined making it unsafe for Fuels Operators to grab on during entry and exiting!



IMPACT IF NOT PROVIDED

Non-compliant hand-railing systems are short of reach for proper holding/gripping entering and exiting of tanks which can put Fuels Operators in a unsafe condition.  Also metal stair type platforms are missing, rusted, and also out of compliance due to not having hand-railing also putting Fuels Operator in unsafe condition.



OSHA definition of handrail — A rail used to provide employees with a handhold for support.

Requirement Title: MSR#11381152_(RM18-1382) Repair Electrical Dist Circuits, Drydock 2 & Pier 5, PSNS (UEM) (DB-IH)
Requirement Description:
BACKGROUND: Circuit 480-5B-9 has suffered multiple failures and is operating at reduced capacity.  Special Project RM027-04 for repair of Pumpwell 2 main dewatering pumps and motors split this into two circuits, 480-9-10 and 412-10-5B to serve new equipment at Sub 10.

This project addresses three High Severity Utility Key Critical Areas as defined by the Project Development and Assessment Guide for FY21 Navy Working Capital Fund (NWCF) Major Maintenance Repair Program (MMRP) Centrally Managed Restoration and Modernization (RM) Projects:

-    Electrical Infrastructure “Backbone” Deficiencies

-    Shipyard Utility Infrastructure Improvements

-    Increased security and reliability of utility infrastructure directly supporting nuclear maintenance or weapons facilities.



These circuits provide service to Dry Dock 1, Dry Dock 2, and Pier 5 submarine shore and industrial power along with Pumpwell 2 [dry dock dewatering] and other Shipyard production, training, and administration facilities.

SCOPE: Design-build work includes removal of existing 11.75 kV, 16-MVA circuit conductors for circuits 480-9-10 and 412-10-5B and replacing them with new 16-MVA EPR circuit conductors.  Remove all existing circuits between manhole 94 and Dry Dock 2 Pumpwell (Building 168), replace crumbling duct bank and install new cabling to return all circuits to service.  Replace cable racks, provide grounding, arc-proofing tape and commissioning.

Requirement Title:
Design and construction services for a 1,355 square foot office renovation at the National Maritime

Intelligence Center (NMIC), suite 2A123-124A.
Requirement Description:
Renovate 2196sqft space. Work may include, but is not limited to field survey / investigation, full and complete design services to include furniture disassembly and transport to government warehouse, new furniture procurement, office construction to include demountable office partitions walls, doors and frames, life safety to include fire protection, painting, flooring work to include carpeting,  vinyl tile and other miscellaneous flooring used at the NMIC Facility, mechanical to include HVAC and plumbing systems, electrical distribution systems, lighting systems, locksmith services, security card reader installation and programming, and  HAZMAT (e.g. mold remediation) services.  The work shall also include providing as-built drawings in current NMIC CAD format at the completion of each project. Contractor will consult with NAVFAC and ONI (Office of Naval Intelligence) to determine construction phasing schedule (if necessary).



Fire Protection work shall consist of an assessment of the existing fire escape means of egress and reconfiguration of sprinkler heads to meet IBC standards. Existing features of construction will remain as much as practical. Systems furniture will be provided by ONI. The Design, including life safety work and any modifications to the fire protection system, HVAC, and electrical disciplines will need to be addressed by the Design Architectural / Engineering subcontractor hired to perform the design work.



Room 2A123/2A124B is a SCIF (Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility).   All design, materials and renovation work shall comply with UFC 4-010-05 and the latest revision to ICD 705 to meet the Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities Planning, Design and construction requirements.



Preliminary sketch of proposed new lay to follow.
