Requirement Description:
Wharves F-1 and F-1.5 (S369) require refurbishment to accommodate the relocation of (4) Charter Tugs, (4) Work Boats

and (2) Barrier Boats from S-18/19.

This project will require:

Removal of dilapidated wooden pier fascia, broken pilings, and a makeshift landing platform.

Application of ~125 pile wraps on spalling concrete piles and pile caps.

Installation of composite chock/wale fender system with 4-6 pile clusters to accommodate mooring vessels.

Inspection/assessment of these wharves was completed by Collins Engineers Inc. on June 8, 2021 under the

requirements of Delivery Order No. N39430-20-F-4001 of Contract No. N39430-20-D-2209 issued by NAVFAC EXWC.

Construction Contract No. N62478-09-D-4019 (17/06/2016) replaced/repaired the topside of concrete decking, but

didn't address the spalling/deteriorated support structure.

The project being proposed is being coordinated through C3F ISO RIMPAC 22'. Work to be completed by UCT2, MDSU,

and Army 7th Dive personnel. Completion of project twill allow the relocation of Charter Tugs from S-19, thereby

The proposed project's maintenance dredging work will remove approximately 145,000 cubic yards of material (includes approximately one foot over-dredge). Requirement Title: Energy Resiliency Investment at Water Treatment Plant NAS 2 (Design-Build)
Requirement Description:
NAVFAC will prepare a IH DB RFP design to implement a microgrid prototype at NAS Sigonella for the Naval Postgraduate School (NPS) research project funded by Naval Facilities Engineering Command Expeditionary Warfare Center (NAVFAC EXWC) under the program Naval Shore Energy Technology Transition and Integration (NSETTI).  

----------------
The Scope of Work (SOW) for the new microgrid is detailed below.

Install a UPS to supply power to the low voltage side of the existing load of substation 496 in NAS 2 Sigonella. The UPS will be 400 kW and provide on line power only to the 400V 3Ph/50Hz portion of the substation.

Install a 500 kWh battery bank to supply power to the UPS describe above.

Install a new Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) connected to the existing Emergency Power Generator and the low voltage side of substation 496. Re-wiring will be needed to complete this connection. The ATS will be controlled by the supervisory managing system of the microgrid.

Replace the existing low voltage breaker at the substation suppling the MOGAS load with a remote controlled switch to be open when the microgrid will be working in island mode.

Install #2 Photovoltaic (PV) rooftops systems over buildings 535/492 and 612 to achieve totally 70 kWp PV system. These systems will provide renewable power to the microgrid.

Provide low voltage cable connection from building 612 and 535/492 to the new microgrid system (about 100 mt). Power connection will be installed via new duct bank underground. This connection will supply microgrid from new PV systems.

Replace existing #2 low voltage panels at buildings 612 and 535/492.

Upgrade low voltage lines and breakers inside the substation 496 to be supplied by the new UPS and microgrid.

Requirement Title: MUN019_KDN-46101_Replace carpet tiles in office spaces_CUSTOMER FUND
Requirement Description:
Carpet tiles in office spaces except newly constructed area are ruined from years of dirt, rain, spills and mold. 

We recently had a project done inside our building in witch the carpet was replaced.   

The difference in carpet between spaces causes mixed emotions throughout the organization.                           

Approx 7,000SF



Received funding endorsement from NMCPAC. The execution could be FY24 because FY23 MEP (Maintenance Execution Plan) has been confirmed already.  23 Feb 23 Tatsuno



1. All office furniture/cubicles will be moved by NMCPAC personnel?  Yes

2. Does NMCPAC have temporary storage space for them? Yes

3. The replacement needs be done in phase? Yes NMC would like for this to be

done in phase's.



================================================================================



Asbestos:

CFAO 2015 Asbestos Inventory report indicates that the floor materials (i.e., carpet tile mastic, vinyl sheet mastic, and cove base mastic) in KDN 46101 office and training spaces are identified as negative for asbestos-containing materials (ACM).



LBP:

Recent bulk sampling data indicates office area door frames identified to be coated with LBP (greater than or equal to 0.5% lead by weight). As long as this renovation is limited to carpet tile replacement project, there is no potential for worker or occupant exposure to lead particulates.

Requirement Title: WBH156_Various facilities_Install Fire Alarm Building Transmitter unit antenna
Requirement Description:
For WBH-1009, 1103, 1100, 1146A, 1152, 1200, 1508, need install/replace Fire Alarm Building Transmitter unit to include all associated panel box and backup batteries to support transmitting antenna to existing fire alarm panel/ system.

The current system of “Tele dialer system”not working, tried to connect through phone lines MCB G6 to connect however no one within the organization has knowledge of how the system works or is connected through the phone lines /terminals. Furthermore, manufacturer of the Tele dialer system is not exist. 



It would be best to upgrade the system to transmitter antenna that report directly to MCB emergency operations desk.

Recommend to install MONACO’s BT antenna/transmitter because receiver unit at MCB Fire Dispatch is MONACO.

Also, recommend to replace FACP to JN product because most of their service life has passed and quick response for the parts supply/repair and high durability (i.e. JN FACP at KDN-3355, 3358, CSH-8235 and WBH-1162). Refer to UFC3-600-01:34-8.1.1 to choose right FACP. However, if existing fire alarm system at WBH1103, 1110, 1146A, 1152, 1200, and 1508 were relatively small, we should try to replace existing fire alarm system with an addressable Monaco FACP with a built-n transmitter. (Advise from FPE Mr. Goto)



For WBH-1152, existing FACP has been installed on the exterior wall and it’s been exposed to weather. The FACP needs to be installed inside.

Requirement Title: RM19-0331 B14 AGLIE SHOP & SUPPORT SPACE MODERNIZATION SIOP
Requirement Description:
SIOP PROJECT  RM19-0331

Repair and renovate Building 14 at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH). Repair work includes the repair and renovation of building exterior windows which will all be replaced and restored to historic standards up to current optimal efficiency standards. Repair includes removal of deteriorated walls; replacing flooring, and upgrading the existing historic lighting fixtures to LED; repainting; and upgrading fire sprinkler and electrical systems. Construction work includes the addition of interior walls, lighting, electrical power, telecommunications system, and automated access control system, new packaged HVAC systems with SCADA control and installation of an elevator or lift. The project shall comply with the Architectural Barriers Act (ABA) for accessibility as well as other standards and codes. Project will include a elevator lobby with elevator complying with ADA standards. First Floor shops to be repaired for agile shops of various types, providing optimum flexibility , while also providing state of the art shop supervisor offices, training room, showers/lockers, conference rooms, and bathroom.

Requirement Description:
SOW  AIRFLD-585 Replace Fuel AST


1. Current Condition:

1.1 During the inspection in December 13 2023, it was found that the internal coating of the AST 585-S fuel tank is in a status of degradation. The current status causes debris to be released into the fuel, causing the emergency generators powered by the tank to malfunction. Requirement Description:
SCOPE:

This project will remove and dispose of existing oily wastewater treatment system (OWTS)

at Facility 705 (Dry Dock 5). Demolition and disposal will include four associated

water storage tanks to include two 40,000 gallon and two 20,000 gallon tanks. New

OWTS will be installed to restore system to its original 200 gallon per minute (GPM)

capacity. Work will include install of replacement tanks of the same size as those

removed with newly installed tanks being double walled. Tank installation will

include seismic bracing as required to meet current code requirements.



OWTS plants employ physical separation of oily wastewater followed by

precipitation, emulsification, coagulation, flocculation, and settling to

remove oil, heavy metals, and other contaminants (i.e., settleable solids)

from ships' wastewater (i.e., bilge and ballast water) and from drydock

process water.  



Delay in this project will subject the Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and

Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS&IMF) and the Bremerton Naval Complex

(BNC) to an increased risk of accidental discharge of ship's bilge, ballast,

or drydock process wastewater into Sinclair Inlet.  Discharges of this type

violate the PSNS&IMF National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES)

and the State Waste Discharge Permit (SWDP) discharge permits.

Requirement Title: Construction of AC Boundaries at Building 261; NSA I
Requirement Description:
This project consists construction of 01 vestibule at NEX main store entry and the upgrading of the existing vestibules at Building 261.



SCOPE:

•  redesign and replace existing interior vestibules in accordance with appropriate ATFP / UFC / NFPA guidance. 

•  Design and construct vestibule located at the existing ingress/egress of the NEX space



BACKGROUND:

Building 261 built in 2006 is designated safe haven and is the most used facility within NSA Bahrain. It is designed to withhold exterior blast and acts as the personnel collection point in event of an attack. Facility is also the base support center and provides vital services to the service members and families of the NSA Bahrain including fitness facilities, dining, banking, cinema and shopping. In the last 3 months NSA safety received at least 4 (four) injury reports of personnel sustaining injury and there was at least one significant/serious incident that caused partial dismemberment of the injured persons finger.

CURRENT SITUATION

 • Unsafe design flaws: Insufficient and poorly designed hinges to secure/hold the very heavy metal door.

 • The deformed door frames are causing the top hinge to separate and, consequently, the doors to collapse.

• Being exposed to extreme desert temperatures, makes the metal dilate and extremely difficult to open.

• Replacement parts are not available in the market (hinge brackets, hinge axes, hinge rings).

• Over time, due to high traffic and elements, some door bar locks are inoperative and create a serious danger for service members on board at the NSA Bahrain.



IMPACT IF NOT PROVIDED:

Vestibule will provide energy efficiency to the HVAC system along with protection to the exterior blast doors. Other vestibule needed an upgrade as they are at the end if life expectancy and rated as R in the ICAP.

communication.

Requirement Title: AZU-244, WHARF REPAIRS AT HAKOZAKI ISLAND
Requirement Description:
1. Scope of Work:

     Description of Project:

     a. Canal Dock 8600409: 

         (1) Repair of deteriorated and cracked concrete surfaces (including new coating at beams and pile caps).

         (2) The removal of six existing 10 Metric Tonne bollards. 

         (3) The installation of four new 10 Metric Tonne landside bollards and associated anchored foundations.

         (4) The refurbishing of four existing wharf-side bollards. 

         (5) The replacement of a stainless-steel ladder.

     b. Fueling Wharf 244: 

         (1) Repair of deteriorated and cracked concrete surfaces (including topside concrete curbs).

         (2) The refurbishing of four existing wharf-side bollards.

         (3) Application of coating to beams and pile caps.

     c. Fueling Wharf 244 Connector Pier: 

         (1) Clean and recoat all structural steel to MHW elevation and coat steel piles with Splash Zone epoxy paste from MHW to approx. 0.64 meters below MLW elevation.

     d. Fueling Wharf 246:

         (1) Repair of deteriorated and cracked concrete surfaces. 

         (2) Replacement of four rubber fenders. 

         (3) The refurbishing of four existing landside wharf-side bollards.

2. Remove & provide cables & conduit, conduit support & fittings for HVAC control system.

Requirement Title: NSN CEP-200  REPLACE AHU-2, AHU-5 & DDC INSTALLATION
Requirement Description:
Description of Problem/Requirement:

As part of MARMCs Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) Sustainment Plan, MARMC Facilities has a requirement for the replacement of two Climate Performance Changers in building CEP-200 and one (1) DX Unit.  These units are no longer within the service life expectancy with no factory support and the best estimated age of the existing AHUs is 40 years.  Combined with the unit’s age, lack of factory support and parts availability creates a vulnerability for failure in the habitability for MARMC employees.



AHU # 2

A.    Replace existing Air Handling Unit (AHU) located inside of Machine Room 1042 (SW side of bldg.)

B.    Provide new BACnet Digital Data Controller (DDC)

C.    Provide and install maintenance platform and/or cat walks around AHU with safety railings to include access ladder from ground level.

AHU # 5

A.    Replace existing Air Handling Unit (AHU) located above the Vending / Break Room (1st Floor).

B.    Provide new BACnet Digital Data Controller (DDC)

C.    Provide and install maintenance platform and/or cat walks around AHU with safety railings to include access ladder from ground level.

DX Unit

A.    It’s estimated this unit was relocated to the vending / break room around 20 years and is currently not providing conditioned air to the space.  The condenser and AHU are in the overhead approximately 10 feet from AHU #5.  MARMC would like to have this unit removed and the space be tied into the new AHU #5

Requirement Title: (23522220) Delta Pier Voltage Regulator Replacement, B7035 Bangor
Requirement Description:
DBB-IH (Old MSR 22055102 for history)

The existing Delta Pier voltage regulator has failed multiple times and is under-sized, resulting in significant risk to mission capabilities. Rebuilding the existing regulator does not solve the sizing problem. 



Perform complex short-circuit, load-flow, and transient stability engineering analysis and design to determine the quantity, ratings, location, and settings of regulators required to provide regulated voltage to the shore and industrial power loads on Delta Pier. Analysis and design shall include normal and emergency power scenarios and scenarios where the Delta North and South feeders at B7035 are looped (both breakers closed) and radial (one breaker open). Design shall include seismic requirements for the anchorage of the voltage regulators.



Design shall include the demolition of existing regulator, protection, equipment pads, and conductors.



Design shall regulate voltages within the limits required for submarine shore power as specified in the latest edition of UFC 4-150-02. 



Perform field investigation and gathering of metering data to perform the analysis. 



Install temporary demand meters where existing facilities are not metered and where existing meters are not functional. 



Design shall provide microprocessor-based relays for thermal, overcurrent, and differential protection of the regulators. Protection shall coordinate with existing equipment connected to the line and load side of the regulators. Design shall include modifications to existing equipment.



Design shall provide for pad-mounted, metal-enclosed voltage regulators of dead-front construction. 



Design shall provide dead-front bypass switches for regulator maintenance. 



Controls shall be located in stainless steel enclosure accessible to personnel without opening the high-voltage termination compartment.

Requirement Title: (DBB-AE) Conduct Fire Protection Design, Dry-Dock Pump Well, Bldg. 7424, TRF-Bangor (20340242)
Requirement Description:
DELIVERABLE: CAT2, DBB-AE 

PSC CODE: C1EC – ARCHITECT AND ENGINEERING-CONSTRUCTION, OTHER INDUSTRIAL FACILITES

UNIFORMAT MASTER SYSYTEM: D40 – FIRE PROTECTION

REQUESTED SCHEDULE: DESIGN FY24 Q4 – CONSTRUCTION FY25 Q4

LOCATION: PMPG STA, BELOW DECK, BLDG. 7420, NBK-BANGOR

1391 REQUIRED: YES FOR CONSTRUCTION PACKAGE 





REQUIREMENT:  



This Service Request tasking is to design a fire protection system for the Bangor Dry-dock, Pump-well, B7424, to include UFC 3-600-1 compliant sprinkler systems, alarm systems, and smoke evacuation systems in the

Pump-well as per recommende4d within the listed survey report referenced below. Design shall also include structural modifications and meet emergency egress requirements.  It is expected that these designs will support follow-on Sustainment, Restoration and Modernization Program Projects, tentatively planned for FY25 at the earliest.





BACKGROUND:



The April 2021 PSNS&IMF Fire Protection Engineering Surveys Report, Trident Refit Facility, Bangor, identified fire protection deficiencies in the Bangor Dry-dock Pump-well, B7424.  The Pump-well is classified as multi-story below-grade building requiring fire protection.  The Pump-well is a special purpose industrial occupancy and is not equipped with fire sprinkler, fire alarm or smoke exhaust systems.  The building houses the main dewatering pumps, drainage pumps, controls and electrical substations that are essential for dry-dock operations and lack emergency occupant egress openings.





JUSTIFICATION:  Life Safety Compliance

Pump-well as per recommende4d within the listed survey report referenced below. Design shall also include structural modifications and meet emergency egress requirements.  It is expected that these designs will support follow-on Sustainment, Restoration and Modernization Program Projects, tentatively planned for FY25 at the earliest.





BACKGROUND:



The April 2021 PSNS&IMF Fire Protection Engineering Surveys Report, Trident Refit Facility, Bangor, identified fire protection deficiencies in the Bangor Dry-dock Pump-well, B7424.  The Pump-well is classified as multi-story below-grade building requiring fire protection.  The Pump-well is a special purpose industrial occupancy and is not equipped with fire sprinkler, fire alarm or smoke exhaust systems.  The building houses the main dewatering pumps, drainage pumps, controls and electrical substations that are essential for dry-dock operations and lack emergency occupant egress openings.





JUSTIFICATION:  Life Safety Compliance

Requirement Description:
Constructs a standalone building to supplement the current Code 452 Launcher Laboratory facilities at Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division Newport (NUWC). Such a facility will provide the land-based facilities to support the land-based RDT&E as well as life cycle support of weapon systems for the Platform and Payload Integration Laboratory at NUWC Division Newport. The new building will house multiple, separate land-based test facilities and their supporting sub-systems designed to address emerging mission/platform specific submarine warfare technical areas that cannot be supported by existing facilities/equipment within the Platform and Payload Integration Laboratory dedicated to RDT&E and lifecycle support. Platforms and systems supported by this project will include Subsea and Seabed Warfare Capability for certain ocean interface aspects of the VIRGINIA/COLUMBIA/SSN(X) platforms, Tactical Missile Integration/Lifecycle Support and Internal Auxiliary Launcher advanced development and integration facilities for the VIRGINIA/COLUMBIA/SSN(X) platforms. These new land-based facilities will provide the

necessary RDT&E/Lifecyle facilities to allow for the engineering, development and integration of additional submarine warfare capability into new and existing submarine platforms without the need and expense of diverting active-duty submarine platforms for lengthy at-sea developmental testing of new systems.

Requirement Title: TEN017_RM20-905 Repair Ammunition Berthing Pier, TP(Design)
Requirement Description:
This project will repair/maintain damaged and deteriorated components of ammunition pier

Facility 500.



REQUIREMENT:

Adequate facility to support the loading/unloading of ammunition from various Department Of Defense Service components in the island of Okinawa. Tengan Pier provides support to all branches of the Department of Defense in Okinawa. The facility serves as the only ammunition loading and off-loading pier that provides such capacity to support essential mission in Okinawa. Due to the critical importance of this facility, it is imperative that the pier maintains its structural integrity and service capabilities at all times. Tengan Pier Facility 500 was constructed in July 1966 and has passed its expected service life of 50-years. This project is required to repair/maintain critical components of the pier that is currently damaged or deteriorated in order to extend its service life. There is no alternative structure/facility that can provide the same allowable capacity to support the mission of the various service components within the island.





Impact if not provided: 

Tengan Pier is the only ordnance handling pier for the entire island of Okinawa. This pier needs critical component repairs to avoid unexpected failures and to extend its service life. If this facility is not repaired and experiences section failure, the island will be without an authorized ordnance load/offloading pier facility and this will compromise mission for all service components in the island.

Due to the critical importance of this facility, it is imperative that the pier maintains its structural integrity and service capabilities at all times. Tengan Pier Facility 500 was constructed in July 1966 and has passed its expected service life of 50-years. This project is required to repair/maintain critical components of the pier that is currently damaged or deteriorated in order to extend its service life. There is no alternative structure/facility that can provide the same allowable capacity to support the mission of the various service components within the island.





Impact if not provided: 

Tengan Pier is the only ordnance handling pier for the entire island of Okinawa. This pier needs critical component repairs to avoid unexpected failures and to extend its service life. If this facility is not repaired and experiences section failure, the island will be without an authorized ordnance load/offloading pier facility and this will compromise mission for all service components in the island.

Requirement Title: NSA NH-139 Renovate Room 179 for Computer Lab - NIWDC
Requirement Description:
NIWDC has a requirement that supports a Navy-wide initiative to develop an Information Training Program and a cornerstone of the initiative is to develop a computer lab that allows for NIWDC personnel to have a dedicated work space that can support multiple computer towers and a traditional office work environment. NIWDC has identified that NH-139, Room 179 would sufficiently meet their requirements, but would need to be renovated from its current use a Storage Room.



NIWDC has two clear requirements for this project:



1.    NIWDC requires the renovation of NH-139, Room 179, which currently serves as a storage room, into an office space that supports multiple computer workstations. There is currently a fire main located in the back of the room that will need to be separated from the current space in order to meet all future fire protection codes.

2.    NIWDC also requires a new storage area for the various office supplies that are currently housed in Room 179. They would like to explore external storage options such as, Conex boxes, PODS, or other nearby facilities that have the appropriate environmental controls. NIWDC is currently looking to reduce the inventory of the storage room in order to facilitate its relocation.

Requirement Description:
In 2010 the toilets in the Boorda Hall complex were upgraded from conventional (3.5 Gpf) toilets to high efficiency "power assist" flush units under the ESPC phase 1 contract by Constellation Energy.  The Navy's contract with Constellation provided for the standard 1 year construction warrantee and puts the long term operation, maintenance, repair and replacement responsibility on the Navy.  The "power assist" mechanism is covered by a 10 year OEM parts warrantee which will expire in 2019/2020.  Constellation has been coordinating with the OEM to ensure we are getting the OEM replacements parts and will continue to do so until that warrantee runs out.  



These units have an excessively high rate of failure and will become a burden if the Navy has to procure the replacement parts post warrantee hence the move to replace that technology. As per Peter Behrens, please replace a total of 455 toilets (284 in B30, 36 in B31, 45 in B32, 45 in B33, and 45 in B34) throughout Boorda Hall with high efficiency power assist flush units.

Requirement Description:
Design a replacement of the building 10 stairwell fresh air system with a code-compliant stairwell pressurization system.

The existing system is a smoke exhaust system that contains fans and motors in unserviceable locations. NFPA requires the system to be a stairwell pressurization system.



The number of stories in the building requires a smoke control system per NFPA guidelines required by UFC3-360-01. System is beyond useful life, repair will require an entire system replacement. The existing system is smoke evacuation (building code from 1970s), current code requires a positive pressure system. Lack of maintenance has put the entire system out of service. Typically this would be a RESTORATION repair, but the significant code change requires a redesign and a change of ventilation technique.

Requirement Title: Focused Electrode Leak Location Inspection B4142
Requirement Description: Focused Electrode Leak Location Inspection B4142. The intent of this project is to inspect all underground pool filtration-related piping with electronic scanning equipment capable of finding pinhole leaks in underground piping systems. Technicians will need PWD support for pipe access, but pipes will be open and full of clean water at the time of inspection. Technicians will push a self-leveling (neutral buoyancy) probe through all underground pool piping for a total inspection linear length of approximately 1000 ft. Technicians will then compile all data collected in the field (including CCTV data) and provide a report on the location and severity of any/all leaks.

Requirement Title: NDW25SW+ B6105  INSTALL FIRE SUPPRESION SYSTEM SUPPORT STORAGE AND OFFICE -
Requirement Description:
The existing fire sprinkler system currently installed in Bldg. 6105 is not completed. There is a sprinkler systems installed in the conference room but the sprinklers are capped off once they exit the conference room. This gives the occupants of the conference room (When full occupancy of 50) the feeling they are protected in case of a fire when they actually are not. I would like to see the completion of the installation of the sprinkler system throughout this building to protect the occupants of the building. Currently there are no sprinklers in any of the office spaces, hallways or in Supply Cage Kitting, receiving or shipping areas. There are no water supply lines installed to feed any sprinklers. It appears that NAVY once paid to have this work done but it was never completed.



This is a safety concern / fire hazard in this wooden building.



This is a  fire / safety hazard that need to be addressed to prevent a fire from happening.

Requirement Description:
It has been found that 3 of the Fresh Water Ship Connection lines under the Pier have failed. First location is 325 foot marker on the Southside, second is 450 foot marker on the Northside, and third is 550 foot marker on the Northside. In order to maintain mission these connections need to be repaired as soon as possible.

The intent of the project is to restore operations of providing Ships with potable water while docked at Pier 5. 

•    Remove 4” Ductile Iron Water Lateral from top side 90⁰ Flange to the Main. Roughly 20 feet from flange to Main.

•    Install a Gate Valve off the main and replace new lateral with HDPE. This will allow the Water service to be restored to the rest of the Pier while work continues. 

•    Replace all Hangers and Hardware with Stainless Steel non corrosive materials. 

•    Replace 2 – 6” x 4” Ductile Iron tee’s

•    Replace 2 – 6” Sleeves

•    Replace 20 feet of 6” Ductile Iron Pipe.

Requirement Description:
Over the past 3 years there have been several instances of leaks requiring patching/repair by BGS (BOSS contractor). In Sept of 21 BGS contracted Baker roofing to repair the most recent leak but the contractor found that the tar-paper barrier was broken down and holding water and could not be repaired. Repairs to the roof isn't recommended contractor said the roof needs to be replaced 



While replacing the roof we would like to add as options to replace/repair the gutter system along with the down spouts on this building.



Guttering on bldg. 14, and the attached generator / mechanical building is rusted through in several areas. Additionally several of the down-spouts are clogged after they transition under the ground causing them to pool water at and under the foundation of Bldg.

Leaking gutters and downspouts allow water to penetrate the perimeter of the building and wash soil away from the foundation, resulting in degradation of supporting soil, collapsing exterior sidewalk, and possible exterior wall failure. 



These started as 2 separate projects under SR's 21504651 , 21504614

Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152787 RM21-1777 DD1 Sewage Piping Replacement, JBPHH

sewer main connected to scuppers below the dock floor, relining may be an alternative if deemed

feasible. For all portions of sewer line within DD1 suction chamber, replace piping. Replace all

(sewer inlet valve) connected to the dock sewer line located within DD1 pumpwell. Replace sewer

discharge connection at the mezzanine level of DD1 pumpwell. Replace sewage vent piping in

pumpwell. The flanged connection piping stub into the concrete wall is corroded.

Requirement Title: E2 (UEM) REPAIR STEAM LINE PH 1 B1600 TO SA13
Requirement Description:
SCOPE:

The project scope is based on the findings of Steam and Condensate Systems

Utility System Assessment (USA) at Naval Air Facility, Atsugi, Japan (dated

September 2022).

PROJECT:

This project will be repairing all additional leak problems for the West Side

Main Steam Piping Loop on Naval Air Facility Atsugi.

These repairs will include replacing sections of steam piping, steam pit

crack repairs, and steam casing repairs.

REQUIREMENT:

Naval Air Facility Atsugi requires a properly maintained, reliable and

efficient steam distribution system. Part of providing a reliable steam

system is repairing all leakage areas throughout the steam distribution

system.

CURRENT SITUATION:

Currently, on the west side of the Naval Air Facility Atsugi, steam from

boiler plant #1 (Bldg. 1600) is being supplied to the Main area of the base.

This Main area distribution loop is adequately sized to support the loads for

each building connected to the system. Currently, there are leaks throughout

the Main loop, cracks within certain steam pits, and steam casings that need

to be repaired. Future repairs to these areas will greatly improve the

efficiency of the west side steam distribution system.

IMPACT IF NOT PROVIDED:

Without the implementation of this project, the Naval Air Facility Atsugi

will not be running as efficiently as it should be for steam production

during peak loads for the west side main distribution loop.

Requirement Title: (20648851) (DBB-AE) Replace 4 USTs at GOV Fuel Station, B1204, Bangor
Requirement Description:
CAT 2 AE-DBB FY23 Design/FY24 Constr.



DELIVERABLE: Develop a CAT2 design for the replacement of 4 single wall USTs that are at end of life with code compliant Double wall fiberglass USTs.


SCOPE:

Replace 4 USTs total (3 18,000 gallon and one 20,000 gallon) with new USTs of comparable capacity that meet all current environmental regulation and engineering code requirements, including but not limited to federal/WA state regulations for USTs and UFC requirements (interstitial monitoring, sump monitoring, etc).  Project scope needs to include leak detection sensors and connections to the TLI (upgrade TLI if necessary).



JUSTIFICATION:  Existing USTs are old, single-wall USTs and do not meet current code requirements for secondary containment (double-walled) and other current environmental regulations.



ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:  

This project may require  design work, as this location is in a heavy vehicle traffic area, and there are underground utilities in close proximity, as are rail tracks.  Construction will likely need to be phased to maintain existing operations.

AM and EV will need to engage in the project planning/development stage.

Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152919 K3 HELO PAD FENCE
Requirement Description:
The existing helo pad fence near B1770 is currently in poor condition. When the helo pad is in use, the end user OT (Ocean Terminals) needs to clear out a majority of the surrounding parking to protect people and vehicles from injury or damage. The parking surrounding the helo pad accomodates the SY workers in B1770 and other federal employees in the buildings nearby. Parking is already a challenge when the helo pad is not in use, so when the helo pad is in use, it takes a significant amount of stalls away. 



The goal of this project is to install a blast fence that will protect the people and vehicles from injury or damage without clearing the surrounding parking lot.



*Note that SY does not have the helo pad in AOR.



BDI Inc. provided some initial engineering and drawings based on the Osprey helicopter. From OT, they said that the Osprey is the aircraft that causes the most downpour of draft. BDI could provide the material and supervision services for a contractor during the install. (See attached for fencing layout and detail)



The blast fencing could be fixed into ground or mounted to concrete bases to be movable. Preferably, the blast fencing would be fixed into ground so appropriate funding could be used. There has been discussion for this project to be awarded in FY24 and the funding split 50/50 with SY and JBPHH.

each building connected to the system. Currently, there are leaks throughout

the Main loop, cracks within certain steam pits, and steam casings that need

to be repaired. Future repairs to these areas will greatly improve the

efficiency of the west side steam distribution system.

IMPACT IF NOT PROVIDED:



Without the implementation of this project, the Naval Air Facility Atsugi

will not be running as efficiently as it should be for steam production

during peak loads for the west side main distribution loop.

Requirement Title: Mitigation of Storm Water Deficiencies - Sasa Valley and Tenjo Vista, NBG Guam
Requirement Description:
*#FY18 PAC OAB*Fuel Farm Road Repairs-Storm-water Mitigation - Sasa Valley and Tenjo Vista



Request perform Storm-water mitigation for identified deficiencies reference NAVFAC Marianas BMcD Project

 No. 88407, NAVFAC Contract No. N62742-10-D-0007. for all affected areas of Sasa Valley and Tenjo Vista. 

 Recommended repairs are listed within the document mentioned for identified areas of concern to follow. 



 JUSTIFICATION:



3.4.1 STORMWATER REGULATIONS AND DESIGN STORM:  As stated in UFC 3-201-01 Civil Engineering Para. 3-1.2, 

a 10 year storm frequency shall be used for calculating peak flow rate.  There are various local storm-water

 drainage manuals for the island of Guam but there are no any specific requirements on the design storm 

event to use for a culvert in a extremely rural area such like the areas in which the fuel facility drainage structures are located.  The Guam Department of Transportation Stormwater Drainage Manual requies a 25-year, 1-hour design storm event for all "secondary" culverts, however this is meant for more of a subdivision land cover.

Additionally, request to modify the east end of L-206 in order to separate it from the western end of the room to create the Flag Mess dining area.

3. PROJECT TITLE: UH – Replace Roof PH1477

4. IMPACT: The roof covering is a built-up roof installed in 1994, approximately 12,400 square feet. The roof surface is degraded and spongy as you walk over the built-up. Remove the built-up roof.

Repair the two roof hatches, the springs are not working, and metal parts are worn down with minor surface rust, seal gaps to prevent moisture penetration.

Replace the built-up roof with a better covering material, single-ply membrane roofing or similar.

Repair or replace the gutters and downspouts that are damaged, corroded or beyond repair.

Seal all roof protrusions.

Install a non-slip walking surface at the center line of the roof for Technicians to use while conducting preventive maintenance to the vents.

Replace the two safety roof hatch handrails, they are corroded beyond repair.

Requirement Description: Bldg. 633 Sprinkler System has approximately 11 sprinkler air vents. The existing air vents are Potter PAAR-B Vents, which have been problematic since installation. The air vent drain pipe/tube shall be properly supported. The existing tampers shall remain for the isolation valves of the new PAV units. Requirement Title: CNIC BLDG 3288 PWD SUPPORT FOR IU WEATHER STATION
Requirement Description:
Request support for Indiana Geological & Water Survey (IGWS), Indiana University, to install a weather station at NSA Crane. Proposed location is at the running track and will require a 100 SF area for a weather monitoring station and a 20 SF area for an auxiliary station. The weather station requires a small concrete pad and fencing. The auxiliary station consists of a post with a small probe mounted on top. 



The weather station provides real-time (and historical) data including air temperature, soil temperature and moisture, solar radiation, relative humidity, precipitation, and wind speed and direction that may assist with operations on NSA Crane (e.g., demo range, UAS flying). There will be no cost to NSA Crane for the stations. All equipment will be owned by IGWS who is responsible for operations and maintenance.

Requirement Title: NBPL-633 INSTLL SPLIT A/C UNIT ROOM 315 INSIDE NMCI ROOM
Requirement Description:
CAP Items:  CATEX, SAR, and HAZMAT



NBPL-633 room, 315, Install split AC unit inside NMCI room.



1. WORK LOCATION: 

BASE: NBPL

BUILDING: B633

ROOM/AREA OF THE BUILDING: 3rd Floor, Room 315 Network Room

INTERIOR/EXTERIOR: Interior

ADDITIONAL LOCATION DETAILS: 



3. ISSUE: At NBPL B633 Room 315, this network room has been primarily cooled for the last 15 years by a mobile cooling unit.



4.    IMPACT: PNS-DETSD is constantly having issues with the mobile cooling units in this network room and a new unit just had to be swapped out with a faulty unit.  A permanent HVAC mini split system should be installed in the network room to provide a more reliable cooling source.



5.    DESCRIPTION OF WORK: 

PNS-DETSD is requesting NAVFAC SW to install a HVAC mini split system in NBPL B633 Room 315 Network Room so that the area housing the NMCI network equipment is adequately cooled.  A reliable cooling and ventilation system for this space must maintain an ideal temperature of between 68 and 71 degrees Fahrenheit all year round.

There are 2 network cabinets full of electronic equipment, thus suggest a system that can deliver 36,000 BTU. Power requirements for the chosen unit will need to be ran to the room and condenser location, a condensation drain is currently in the room. Condenser equipment can be mounted on the roof of building 633. Current room dimensions are 6’ wide x 16’ deep x 8’ high.

Requirement Description:
The scope of this project is to design and construct an new effluent disinfection system to satisfy the requirements

of the DOH Notice of Violation and Order (NOVO), dated 6 May 2022, Docket No. 2022-CW-EO-04, in accordance

with the National Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (NPDES) Permit No. HI0110078.

This work includes engineering assessment, design, and construction services to design and construct a new

effluent disinfection system for the Water Reclamation Facility (WRF) to meet the requirements of the NOVO, in

place complete. At a minimum, a disinfection unit capable treating 100% effluent to comply with single samples of

no more than 130 colony forming units (CFU) per 100 ml and monthly geometric mean averages complying with a

value of 35 CFU per 100 ml for enterococci shall be provided.

Requirement Title: Design and Install roof top fall protection system
Requirement Description:
NBPL-35, Design and install rooftop fall protection system/work platform for NBPL-35, 36, and 77



1.    WORK LOCATION Point:  Loma Fuel Department/  B35, B36, and B77

BASE: Point Loma    

BUILDING: NBPL-35, 36, and 77

ROOM/AREA OF THE BUILDING: Roof of each facility

INTERIOR/EXTERIOR: Exterior 

ADDITIONAL LOCATION DETAILS: Point Loma Fuel Facilities B35, B36, and B77



2.    ISSUE: Each of the facilities listed above have roof ventilation and or HVAC equipment that requires periodic maintenance. Access to the equipment is dangerous due to the absence of fall protection devices on each of the roofs listed. In order to access the equipment on the roofs, fall protection devices need to be installed.



3.    IMPACT: If fall protection devices are not available on the roofs, technicians are unable to access the roofs to perform periodic maintenance (visual inspection and lubrication) on the facility HVAC and ventilation equipment.       DESCRIPTION OF WORK: 

•    Design and install roof access and roof work platform/fall protection system to allow access to all pieces of equipment on each of the roofs of NBPL-35,36 and 77 that require periodic inspection and maintenance. NBPL-35, 36, and 77 all have exhaust vents requiring periodic maintenance.

Requirement Title: P1080 - Construct Power & Water Resilience Upgrades
Requirement Description:
The project will provide increased reliability, resiliency, and capacity to the existing electric and water utility systems primarily responsible for the protection of nuclear-powered submarines and nuclear support facilities at Portsmouth Navy Shipyard (PNSY). Electrical:										

Provides modifications to the commercial power supply provided by Central Maine Power (CMP) to PNSY that includes utility modifications, a rebuild of the existing transmission line, and a second transmission line to increase commercial power capacity, redundancy, and resiliency.At PNSY, provides upgrades and modifications to shipyard power distribution, energy storage, and onsite generation to increase capacity, capability, and resiliency of the microgrid.	Water:										

Provides modifications to the commercial water utility supply provided Kittery Water District (KWD) to PNSY that includes increase the water production at the Water Treatment Plant from 5 MGD to 7 MGD and improvements to the distribution lines to accommodate the increased flows to PNSY.At PNSY, provides two new water connections from KWD to PNSY for the additional water capacity to meet 2035 requirements. The new water lines will provide increased reliability in-water supply to the installation and increases on-yard storage capability by providing a new 2.5MG water storage tower.

Requirement Title: REPAIR AND ESTABLISH MAINTENANCE FOR LIGHTNING PROTECTION AND GROUNDING SYSTEMS AT BLDGS 440, 443, 103, AND 105, CAPODICHINO AND LAGO PATRIA
Requirement Description:
Capodichino, Bldg. 440

- Main LPS conductors are separated from north side of B440 to south side of B440.  The LPS main conductor does not interconnect to all stake terminal devices.  Install a main LPS conductor that connects the portion of the structure separated by the courtyard, as this is the single building. 

- Most metallic objects on roof lack bonding to the LPS main conductor to mitigate lightning induced side flash.  Bond all metallic features on C4I roof to the LPS main conductor per UFC 3-575-01 and NFPA 780. 

- Install air terminals at a minimum of 10 inches above the cameras. 

Capodichino, Bldg. 443

- Install grounding unit to protect UHF antennas on Bldg. 443 roof. 

SATOCM, Bldg. 103 and Bldg. 105

- Repair LPS system to comply with UFC and NFPA requirements 

- Install grounding on all roof access ladders according to UFC requirements.  Recommend 2 points of grounding per ladder. 

- Remove abandoned antennas and cabling from rooftops. 

*LPS and ground systems require routine maintenance to ensure a low impedance path to ground to conduct energy to earth safely.  There is no maintenance or testing program for the LPS and ground systems.  Implement a maintenance and test program for the grounding and LPS in accordance with best practice found in NFPA 780, UFC 3-575-01, and TM 5-690.

Requirement Title: B40 Install copper roof edge guard system (only).
Requirement Description:
Install copper edge guard system & perform slate maintenance to existing slate (Front and back). A contractor inspection found a  variety of defects and missing and broken slate throughout the slate roof system. The slates are falling as a result multiple issues. With no current guard system, slates can fall off the building if dislodged. The contractor proposes a copper edge guard to prevent any future slate falling from the front of the building. A copper edge guard system will be installed to the front edge of building. The guard system will be fabricated

from solid copper bar and 16 oz copper sheet. Guard system will allow water to pass but will not

allow broke slate to pass giving safe passage for personnel and parked cars.

Copper fabrication shall include a C style bend reinforced by solid copper bar and soldered

joint. Guard system shall be sectional to allow replacement of any damaged section of guard

system if required.

Copper bar shall secure guard system to building and shall integrate into historical slate roof

properly with regard for historical accuracy and functionality. Existing slate: Vermont Purp / Class: S1 / Type: Hard Slate / Quarry of Origin: Greenstone VT.

"

Requirement Title: Repair by Replacement of Fuel Dispenser and Pumps; LSA - Isa AB
Requirement Description:
Requesting to upgrade existing Fuel tanks, pumps and dispenser by repair by replacement. The Following actions are necessary to bring the LSA Fuel Point to Operational Conditions.



1. Drain and Purge existing tanks and remove pump systems and Hoses

2. provide 2 each, 5k Diesel tanks and pump systems, Prepare Ground Works for new Impervious coated Concrete pads and containments for 2 each, 5k Diesel tanks and pump systems.

3. Pour concrete slabs in recommended thickness.

4. Pour concrete containment walls in recommended thickness.

5. Install new Tanks and Pumps systems

6. Activate Systems

7. Gravel entire Fuel Point areas and tamp

8. Any other Environmental coordination and support

Existing fuel dispensers and pumps located at LSA fuel point are not fully functional, require to go for repairing this asset in order to dispense fuels to USG vehicles, Power Generators,  other supporting Contractor's equipment in safely and timely.

Currently a Fuel truck is stationed at fuel point to serve the customers, which is neither safe nor best practice for fuel dispensing.

Requirement Title: 1828345 -- Create berthing space for newly hired shipboard firefighters
Requirement Description:
Modify space for Bunk rooms at Fire Station I;BLDG 245;NSAI 



NSAB FESD is requesting to renovate / modify the existing designated partially partitioned lounge area to provide minimum of 5-6 bunk spaces with an attached lounge area which will be utilized by FESD personnel. This project will support the accommodation of incoming newly hired personnel and will serve as an interim solution to support the mission prior to the major facility renovation.



Requirements:

- Construct partitions which will serve as enclosed bunk rooms

- Extend existing partitioned space to accommodate for lounge area

- Install false ceilings and lighting fixtures 

- Provide fire suppression system within the constructed spaces

- Provide split AC units for the constructed spaces

- Provide integrated fire alarm detection and notification system within the constructed spaces

- Provide x2 power outlets in each bunk room and x4 power outlets in the lounge area 

- Install separate sub panel to accommodate for split AC units and power outlets

Requirement Title: WON 1736639 REPAIR SPECIAL PURPOSE TRACKED VEHICLE, WAIAWA PUMP STATION
Requirement Description:
Replace special purpose tracked vehicle at Waiawa Pump Station. Existing tracked vehicle was replaced in 2017, but

has experienced numerous mechanical failures resulting in unacceptable down times. When tracked vehicle is out of

service, no movement of mission critical pumps, motors, control systems and piping/appurtenances can occur in/out of

the pump room (denoted by yellow arrow on left photo below). Pump room is located approximately 100 ft below the

finished floor of Bldg S71 and is accessed through a 255 ft long 30-deg inclined portal.

Due to the Red Hill water crisis, Waiawa Pump Station is currently the only potable water source available for JBPHH,

serving over 93,000 military and civilian personnel, and all shoreside water demands in support of the warfighter. Any

issue requiring removal/transport of mission critical equipment in/out of the station pump room will be impeded by a

non-working tracked vehicle.

The new tracked vehicle will need to fit the existing space within the pump station portal and pump room. Vehicle shall

be capable of carrying at least two passengers with a carrying capacity of at least 6,000 pounds with a flatbed carrier

with appropriate tie-down mounts. New tracked vehicle is desired to not have a linked traveling power supply as

denoted by blue arrow on right photo below. This traveling power supply has failed numerous times, along with

vehicle sensors and programming cards that cause automatic shutdown of the vehicle, sometimes on the 30-deg

inclined section of the portal.

It is also desired to select a tracked vehicle that can utilize the existing tracks. However, project may require demolition

of existing vehicle tracks and will require removal of existing tracked vehicle electrical equipment. Any demolition work

will be likely confined to Bldg S71 interior. Install ...

Requirement Title: INSTALL LOW FLUSH URINALS/SINK FAUCETS/SHOWER HEADS
Requirement Description: Project will lower water consumption intensity as mandated by executive order 13693 by reducing the water flows in sink faucet, kitchen faucet, showers, urinals and toilets of a 159 facilities located in Downtown area, villages and southern part of Diego Garcia. For existing urinals in good working condition they shall be used and retrofit as necessary. Low flow aerators will be installed in sink and kitchen faucets. Shower heads will be replace with low flow shower heads and displacement object will be installed in toilet tanks. Project includes associated restoration of existing interior wall, ceiling, floor slab, and finishes affected by the plumbing upgrades for the urinal, and repair/replacement of plumbing hardware not in good working condition or incompatible with higher efficiency hardware retrofit.

Requirement Title: WATERFRONT - CNIC - NAVPEA BAC REPAIR FALLING HILLSIDE KAM HWY
Requirement Description:
Portions of an existing gunite covered hillside on the west side of Kamehameha Highway between the Center Drive and Radford Drive intersections has debonded from its substrate.



An Engineering investigation was conducted in September of 2018, the following recommendations were provided.



- Invasive vegetation and trees should be removed down to its roots from the top of the gunite covered hillside along its entire length.



- After invasive vegetation and tree removal, an herbicide should be applied to the top of the hillside to reduce the potential for the invasive vegetation and trees from re-growing.



- Measures such as chemical root barriers should be provided to prevent roots from landscape vegetation and trees located above the hillside from growing down the hillside.



- For the area adjacent to fallen gunite, the remaining portion of debonded gunite should be removed up to the top of the hillside.



- After removing debonded portions of gunite, the exposed volcanic tuff rock substrate should be cleaned of any vegetation, roots, and loose material.



-Prior to applying new gunite, a wire mesh reinforcing should be provided.  It should be anchored to the top of the hillside and draped over the cleaned volcanic tuff rock substrate.



- The new gunite should be applied over the wire mesh and volcanic tuff rock substrate.

Requirement Title: HI2618R AN FPN-68A PAR INSTALLATION, KBAY
Requirement Description: Provide complete architectural and engineering (A-E) services and deliver full design and construction documents to install a new raised concrete pad and supporting infrastructure on the airfield at MCBH, K-Bay to support Navy's new Commercial Off-The-Shelf PAR (Precision Approach Radar) equipment and shelter. Scope of work for this project includes site prep required for a new concrete pad, construction of a new concrete pad approximately 40 feet by 20 feet near the existing PAR off of Taxiway Alpha, installation of site electrical to support the PAR, installation of back-up generator as required, installation of communication infrastructure to include underground fiber optic lines and conduits to support Single Mode fiber optics, and installation of a separate grounding system for lightning protection/obstruction (as required). Areas affected by repair/construction will be in compliance with applicable ATFP, fire suppression, seismic, accessibility, ASHRAE, LEED, and flood plain codes and standards (as required). Work shall include but not limited to communicating and coordinating with all involved MCBH stakeholders and NAVFAC agencies; organizing & setting up design presentations for the preliminary & 35% design submittal, meetings, distributing document deliverables (physically & electronically) and do thorough / complete site surveys / investigations. The latest MCBH Design & Construction Standard shall be followed as well as any updated requirements obtained from MCBH Facilities Depart. Note: This is a NAVAIR funded project and is not funded by MCBH’s O&M appropriations. Additionally, SOW & cost estimate doesn't reflect trenching across Taxiway Alpha. If trenching is required for elect./comm work, an updated DD1391 & Cost Estimate will be required.

Requirement Description:
ST450-17



Brief Scope: Replace 28 infrared 1000 BTUH  heaters, 2000 LF of 4" 16 gauge porcelain coated combustion chamber, 9 control panels and associated components.

This project will replace all 28 infared heaters and combustion chamber in warehouse CAD 565 Williamsburg VA.

Affected sqft: 125,000

Builder FCI :94

Execution Agent: NAVFAC

Acquisition Method: D/B

Current Situation  Existing Heaters are at the end of their life cycle heaters require more maintenance and repairs as they age.  When the combustion chamber fails the system will be inoperable and patching will be extremely difficult as older parts are increasingly difficult to procure.

Impact If Not Provided:  If these heaters are not replaced soon they will fail to provide adequate heating to the building.  Assemblages of packaged hospitals and Bio-medical labs will be at risk of not meeting mission build requirements by allowing material and equipment to freeze.

Requirement Title: INSTALL GROUNDING PLATES AT PUMP STATIONS 1, 2 AND 3
Requirement Description:
DESCRIPTION OF PROPOSED WORK: Provide a steel grounding plate with personnel handle on pump room exterior wall adjacent to the entry door at 1.5 m above grade for personnel grounding dissipation. Bond grounding plate to the existing pump house grounding system with a 16 mm2 insulated green grounding conductor. Provide sign adjacent to grounding plate that reads “Grasp handle prior to entry” (in both English and Japanese).



JUSTIFICATION: Personnel grounding plates provide a common point for all operations and maintenance personnel to discharge any built up electrostatic energy upon entry to the pump house. The release of static electricity within an active pump house has the potential to create an explosion.



CURRENT SITUATION: The existing pump house does not have personnel grounding plates at the main ingress points into the pump house.



IMPACT IF NOT PROVIDED: Operators entering the pump house could create an electrostatic discharge which could ignite explosive concentrations of fuel vapor when touching metallic objects.

restoration to provide continued seamless and safe support to the Navy and railway

operators.

Requirement Title: KDN210_Power Upgrade in Room 203 for PGS KDN-3360
Requirement Description:
PGS is a system that allows us to do our pre and post mission requirements 



for the various flights out here.  It is an upgrade to our current system we

have in ADP.



As A TacMobile site with PGS a minimum power requirement of three phase 125

amps feed for the TS enclave and 175 Amps per phase for the secret enclave

is required. During NIWC's survey they noted that the floor does not have

enough power and the first step would be 1 of 2 options to get the power.

Option 1 is to run a power feed from the first-floor electrical room and

connect it to the 175 Amp spare breaker on the main panel. This would

require a core through the second-floor concrete floor.

Option 2 is to run a power feed from the new 400 Amp CP233 Panel. That run

would require two cores through concrete walls for either ADP or Analysis.



Cooling: The complete system cooling requirement for both enclaves equals

180,332 BTU/Hr.  At the moment ADP will not be able to support both enclaves

of PGS without adding another 4 tons of cooling.



There are two COAs that we are considering at the moment.



COA 1: The first COA we discussed was leaving the ADP enterprise operations

in room 203.  Upgrade would include an additional 225 AMPS and 4 tons of

cooling.



COA 2: Swap ADP operations to room 227.  Upgrade would include an additional

175 AMPS, and confirmation that the appropriate cooling (assumption is RM

227 has roughly 183k BTU/Hr cooling) is enough.



Hopefully that helps with the RFI e-mail.  If there is any other questions,

send them my way and I'll try and get the answers for you.

Requirement Description:
he current truck off load facility, CI-282, shares the JP-5 line with the secondary truck loading facility, CI-251. This causes contamination of the fuel issue line to the truck loading stand. This project is to install a new 4 inch receipt fuel line from CI-282 to the main JP-5 return line along Ocean Road.

The new line will be 4 inch diameter with the necessary isolation valves, thermal relief valves, low point drains, and high point vents. The new line will be approximately 460 feet long. The pipe supports will be guide slides mounted on concrete spread footings. Pipe installation, testing, and coating shall be IAW the UFGS for above ground fuel piping. The new line will allow off specification fuel to be separated from the supply line to the secondary truck loading facility. The current situation can cause contamination of the fuel issue line to the truck stand.

Design and construction in FY-24. This will eliminate the possible cross contamination of off specification fuel with ready to issue fuel at the secondary truck loading stand.

If the new line is not installed the use of the loading stand will be impacted until off specification fuel is removed from the line serving the truck rack.

Requirement Title: B1424 Replace Sulfuric Acid and Caustic Systems, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Both T-20 and T-21 tanks are in need of replacement as they are constantly leaking at their bases and at several tank connection locations.  

 

T-20 holds sulfuric acid of 95% concentration and T-21 holds sodium hydroxide of 50% concentration.  Both chemicals are highly corrosive and are hazardous to personnel. Because the tanks are each in a concrete containment, threats to the environment due to a major leak are lessened.  However, the safety and health hazards to personnel due to the continued slow leakage are high and require expedited action.

 

In order to accomplish this task and eliminate the current hazard to the personnel, the following will need to happen: 

 

•         Chemical removal from tanks and cleanup up of containments, tank flushing, demolition and disposal. 

•         Flushing of and surface prep of the secondary concrete containments to ensure they are ready to receive the new           tanks.

•         New tank installation and testing to ensure proper functioning 

 

For additional safety and scope of work notes, each tank is above ground and has 2000 gallon capacity. In addition to the tank replacement, the discharge pump and piping system for T-21 that delivers the chemical to the treatment plant require replacement as well due to solids buildup in the piping system.



Similar to the tank replacement: 

•         Chemical removal, pipe demo and disposal

•         Removal and disposal of existing pumps; Install new pumps and associated electrical equipment and accessories such as wiring and control panel

•         Configure new pump and connections to the existing SCADA system 

•         New piping, valves, and support installation

•         Testing for functions such as pipe leak and flow

Requirement Title: 580A INSTALL FIBER OPTIC CABLE MIDWAY GATE TO ELMER
Requirement Description:
Provide fiber connectivity to the 580A ELMR shelter, connecting back to C-71 to tie into the Enterprise Ashore Enclave (EAE) network.  The optimal path is from the Midway gate enclosure out to ELMR Shelter Building 580 for future expansion and minimal tree cutting.  There is adequately scoped existing fiber available from the Midway gate enclosure with connectivity back to C-71.

Requirements

·         Outdoor rated single mode fiber

·         Adhere to industry standards and best practices

·         Terminate fiber in 580A shelter

·         Add auxiliary enclosure and terminate fiber adjacent to Midway gate enclosure

·         48 Strands

·         Leave service loops for expansion at the following locations

                   En-route to FA-2 (intersection of Midway and Munda).

                   En-route to HA-1 (intersection of Midway and Guadalcanal).

                   En-route to MA-3, MA-5 (service pole behind MA-3).

·         Require end-to-end testing and certification of fiber post-installation.

NBPL-231, Repair roofing system and sidings of six (6EA) vision towers, Enclave. Roofs on all these facilities have significant deterioration  and water penetrates during rainy season.



1. WORK LOCATION: 

BASE: NBPL

BUILDING:   NBPL-231/232/233/234/235/236

ROOM/AREA OF THE BUILDING:  Roofs and Windows/sidings

INTERIOR/EXTERIOR: Exterior

ADDITIONAL LOCATION DETAILS: NBPL South Pier 5002


3. ISSUE: The structural insulated roof panels have suffered a lot of corrosion, which allows water to penetrate through the .021 inch aluminum skin.  All waterproofing systems like the ridge beam top, snap caps, flex seal tape between panels, and caulking, have all started to fail.  Leaking water is constantly destroying the ceiling tiles and puddles sometimes form on the floor.  Windows and panel seals on the side of the buildings have also begun to fail where water penetrates into the interior of the buildings.

  

4. IMPACT: These spaces are critical to our mission of maintaining and repairing

Requirement Title: DB Construction; MACC TO; RM18-0287; REPAIR POTABLE WATER SYSTEM, POINT MUGU & LAGUNA PEAK; NBVC
Requirement Description: Project repairs by replacement and rehabilitates the deteriorated water mains and associated valves and hydrants with new corrosion resistant water mains, fire hydrants and system valves at Naval Base Ventura County, Point Mugu and Laguna Peak. Repair high failure rate areas approximately 60,165 lineal feet of old, deteriorated cast iron and steel piping and associated fire hydrants and valves with new non-metallic piping. The distribution piping ranges from 4-inch to 18-inch in size. If this project is not provided, the intermittent interrupted delivery of adequate water supply and fire suppression water supporting critical mission will continue. In August 2020, increased monthly flushing to 2.6M gal/month to maintain water quality per State requirements. Water distribution system will increase disruption due respectively to tuberculation and deteriorated piping. NOV received April 2020 for elevated disinfectant byproduct due to poor water circulation. This project contributes to closing CAPGAP No. 281 with IR = 10 color RED.

Requirement Title: NSWC BLDG 142 REPLACE STEAM AND CONDENSATE LINES AND RENOVATE B144A
Requirement Description:
EM25 NSWC BLDG 142 144A REPLACE STEAM AND CONDENSATE LINES RENOVATE 144A 27427776


WHY:

* Renovate as needed 144A, roof, doors penetrations, etc...

• Replace all steam and condensate lines with insulated direct burial line. 

• Run main steam and condensate line from point A over to building 144A.

• Install 3 flange bolted crane rising stem gave valves on the wall. These valves will be used as individual isolation valves for building 142 (B), 2707 (C), steam line running over to D supplying buildings 109 and 143.  Condensate lines will need ran to each point as well. 

• Replace any defective parts inside the square pit along with valves, line and replace insulation after replacement has been done. 

• Fill in the old pit located inside 144A so that there is no confined space required. 

• Install two new dual steam pumps inside building 144A along with all associated steam and condensate lines. Drip legs need installed throughout the system to ensure there is no chance of water hammer. Isolation valves need installed so that maintenance can be performed while one pump remains in service. Stainless steel spring check valves with Inconel seats must be installed so that the chemical in the steam and condensate does not deteriorate the seats.

• All condensate will be routed back to building 144A to the dual steam pumps. 

• Replace wall mounted steam heaters inside building 144A so that the building stays properly heated. 

• I will look over the SOW once its created so that things can be gone over to avoid missing something. 

I have attached an areal view with the letters A,B,C and D illustrating the locations of each.

Requirement Description:
SIOP PROJECT ST21-2134

This project proposes to overhaul the Dry Dock 1 caisson at the Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard & Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PHNSY & IMF). Repair scope of work includes performing 10-year ultrasonic testing (UT) of the entire caisson in accordance with MIL-STD-1625D including, but not limited to, plating of the entire hull, top deck (weather deck), machinery deck, internal strength decks, bulkheads including breast hooks, ballast tank and machinery deck internal structural members such as stiffeners, truss frame members and seachests/ballast piping seaward of the first closure valve. UT shall be performed at different locations from previous inspections.

Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152943 BRAVO 1 / BRAVO 2 UNDER PIER HPA PIPING REPLACEMENT, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
Request replacement of piping and pipe supports under Bravo 1 and Bravo 2 Piers. High Pressure Air (HPA) piping shall conform to commercially available standard practices. Piping shall also conform to MIL-HDBK-1003/8. Preference to keep replacement pipe material same as existing piping. Existing pipe material: Monel Cu-Ni. Approximate pipe run: 685 feet. Current pipe support: clevis hanger.



A pipe support failure under Bravo 1 & Bravo 2 Piers have caused irreparable damage to existing HPA piping and pipe supports. Piping distributes high pressure air from S-1182 HPAC facility. 



Pipe supports were made from reinforced fiberglass, which becomes brittle over time from sun and seawater exposure. Request to explore alternative options for stronger, prolonged life pipe hangers.

Requirement Title: (RM19-1082) Repair Emergency Generator, Bldg. #3 Switchgear, Bldg. 7702, UEM Bangor
Requirement Description:
(RM19-1082)(CMP) Repair Emergency Generator, Bldg. #3 Switchgear, Bldg. 7702, UEM 

Bangor O&MN, RM19-1082: 22274171 



The scope of work replaces existing switchgear at Emergency Generator Building #3 (EGB3 FAC 7702) with new metal-clad 15kV modular type switchgear and provides a cable bus tie from EGB3 to Emergency Generation Building #4 (EGB4 FAC 7707). Switchgear will include microprocessor-based protection, metering, and controls for all source, feeder, and tie circuits. Project replaces existing generator paralleling switchgear and generator controls. Project replaces the existing battery and charger with new battery and charger sized to provide coverage for an 8-hour loss of AC power.





If this project is not funded, the switchgear will fail, and spare parts will not be available for repairs.        Additionally, generator #1 will fail again due to the thermal stresses.    This decreases the reliability of the emergency electrical power system and decreases the reliability of the entire electrical grid which poses a threat to operations on Bangor.    Without a well-maintained electrical system, Naval Base Kitsap - Bangor's ability to complete its mission will be jeopardized.    This creates higher costs, adverse effects to maintenance availability completion dates and will ultimately affect fleet readiness.

Requirement Description:
WORK SUMMARY:

system with the appropriately sized pipe, Rebuild the leaking Hot water pump and return to proper operations.

The Project will provide materials and labor to accomplish the following scope of work:

♦ Receive and deliver all materials needed to complete this project.

♦ Isolate Make up water and make safe for Demo.

♦ Demo all Make up water piping from systems to backflow.

♦ Install new piping and supports for all make up water piping in mechanical room and out to the cooling tower.

♦ Replace the tower Fill solenoid valve.

♦ Rebuild the isolated Hot water pump with new seals gaskets and plate seals.

♦ Insulate removed insulation on the cooling tower

♦ Fill systems and check operation of make up water and chilled water pump

Requirement Description:
Current Situation:

The retaining walls at Camp legacy in front and sides of CLU’s 488L and 491L, and DC112 & DC114 are damaged and not stable. The retaining wall has numerous horizontal and vertical cracks running through the surfaces of the walls both top and sides where pressure is greatest. The cracks vary in size from hairline fracture to wider, gaping cracks, and they extend across multiple sections of the retaining wall. In some sections, the retaining wall is leaning or bulging inward due to the pressure of the soil it is retaining, indicating a loss of structural integrity. Chunks of concrete and mortar have chipped away near the cracks leaving the reinforcements/steel exposed to the environment and corroded. The topsoil is also rich with sulfate which causes detrimental/degradation of the retaining wall concrete when in direct contact during rains or when soil is wet. The entire retaining wall could collapse entirely, and this could create a hazardous situation if not rebuilt



Cited Requirement: Construct new retaining wall in accordance with UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering and UFC 3-201-01, Civil Engineering, and all applicable codes and standards to assist in slowing down flow of surface water and prevent floods, reduce the impact of soil erosion, and holding back soil.



Impact if Not Provided

If this is not repaired or rebuilt there is the possibility that this area of the retaining wall could completely collapse and cause further damages. Retaining walls assist in the slowing down of water flow and reduce the impact of soil erosion. If not addressed the topsoil/ground or that area in general will not be able to be used as it is currently as there could be serious soil

Requirement Description:
CN3SRJ / NEW DIVING AND LIFE SUPPORT ENGINEERING FACILITY CIP PROJECT

 

The Diving and Life Support Engineering Facility will be an approximately 120' X 40' structure with an open high bay on one end.  It will include an office space able to accommodate 9 workstations, three dedicated RDT&E labs spaces, a conference room with kitchenette, and two unisex restrooms. A large frontal roll-up door is to be included in the high bay to provide sufficient clearance to safely support all internal handling operations. 

 

See attached project quad sheet, list of facility requirements, and concept sketches.

 

Preferred site for new facility is a replacement facility for B584.



Construction of this facility will extend a significant cost savings to E-Dept by removing the logistical problems associated with having numerous satellite work areas coupled with off-site storage. By eliminating these logistical issues, more of our sponsor allocated funding will be devoted to end product design and integration.



Low pressure shop air and water supply in labs and high bay

240V electric supply in all spaces (exterior wall)

Exterior water supply and 110V electrical

Floor drains in labs and high bay

Exhaust fan in high bay

Gypsum board ceiling in lab spaces in lieu of acoustic ceiling tile, control ventilation for UBA repair and development

Space available for future Automatic Transfer Switch and generator hookup

20' overhead roll-up doors to allow easy access for Material Handling Equipment

Oxygen bottle farm

Position exhaust ductwork, electric supply, and water supply over lab spaces with access panels to accommodate future reconfiguration

Eliminate excess building height/volume

Mechanical Room with sufficient space to house HVAC, electrical, air compressors, fire suppression, and network switches

Requirement Title: (DBB-AE) Replace Damaged Timber Pile, B7454, NBK, Bangor (21851224)
Requirement Description:
Requirement: Replace damaged timber bridge piles.



At Bents 5 and 6, one of the three supporting timber piles at each bent exhibits severe

deterioration near the groundline. Portions of the outer shell were removed to reveal

substantial section loss of the interior of the pile.



At Bent 5, Pile 2 the interior section loss is estimated at 75% with only the outer

¾" shell remaining. Hollow sounding timber suggests the deterioration extends 4 ft

high. 



At Bent 6, Pile 1 the interior section loss is estimated at 85% with only the outer

½" shell remaining. Hollow sounding timber suggests the deterioration extends 2 ft

high. 



At Bent 2, Pile 2 has been retrofitted with a square timber column. The top of the column

is non-load bearing with the cap. There is up to a ¾" wide gap between the top of the

column and bottom of the bent cap.



Justification: On August 13, 2022, Marine Solutions, Inc. (Marine Solutions) performed a routine inspection on Bridge 7454 located at SUBASE Bangor. As per the subject contract Statement of Work, Section F3, this correspondence is to report a safety related deficiency found during the field inspection that requires immediate follow-up action. Bridge 1WA7454 consists of timber beams supporting a timber plank deck carrying vehicular traffic over a ravine. The superstructure is supported by six timber bents comprised of three timber piles each. Inventory direction for this structure is from the south and the west. 



Marine Solutions has recommended immediate closure of bridge until repairs can be made.

Requirement Description:
CO Bathroom Remodel Rm 220: 



This was a shops project that got shut down due to asbestos containing material in the bathroom.



Replace outdated flooring and baseboards with terrazzo, replace outdated ceiling lighting with brighter lights, replace degraded toilet (included seat), install toilet paper dispenser, replace entire stall partition, remove INOP urinal, install shower head with hot/cold taps in place of urinal, install shower drainage, check and upgrade ventilation, remove INOP floor heater/control panel, remove two sinks, install new heat w/hot and cold water, install sink counter, remove two small mirrors, install one large vanity mirror above sink, replace paper towel dispenser, replace damaged ceiling tiles.

O-6 Commanding Officer’s bathroom is outdated and degraded. Due to the large number of items needing maintenance, it has been determined that the space needs to be updated. Many of the fixtures seem to be original to the building.

Material condition of the bathroom will continue to deteriorate leading to increased cost in maintenance/repair and possible unsuitability for continued use.



Breakroom Rm 201:



 Install kitchen sink with garbage disposal and hot/cold water, replace counter/cabinets as necessary to fit sink.  The breakroom currently does not have a sink and the entire floor has to use the cleaning closet sink or bathroom sinks, which are both down the hall.

Staff need a proper place to wash dishes/breast pumping supplies/hands that does not involve a bathroom or cleaning gear closet that contains cleaning supplies.

Staff will continue to use the cleaning gear locker or bathroom for rinsing dishes/breast pumping supplies. Restroom is only place to wash hands on 2nd floor.

Requirement Title: PD22801796 - EN - REPAIR - CONCRETE STAIRS - FALLBR-380 - NAVAIR- HA 580
Requirement Description:
There is an existing set of concrete stairs providing access for employees of Building 380 from the hillside parking lot to Building 380. There subgrade soil underneath the stairs has considerable erosion due to rodent burrowing. The erosion is impacting the integrity of the stairs subgrade soil and may lead to damaged stairs that would not be safe to use. The existing

galvanized handrail does not have end rail loops that are needed to provide adequate support when walking from a sloped to a flat surface.

The project will fill in the voids in the soil subgrade under the concrete stairs to provide a solid and stable foundation and to prevent any damage to the stairs. The project will also include the placement of 6”-12” sized rock on the slope along the sides of the stairs for erosion protection. The project will include in the installation of galvanized handrail loops to be connected to the existing handrails.
