Requirement Description:
Project to repair and reinforce the existing Waiawa Stream Bridge connection

Waihona Street to the Potable Water fresh water pumping station in Pearl

City, Oahu.  The existing bridge is severely deteriorating and is in need of

repairs and upgrades to ensure safe travel to and from the pump station.

Per a bridge study conducted in 2019, the repair project shall focus on but

is not limited to three main areas of interest, structural repair, safety

improvements, and maintenance.  



Structural Repairs: 

- Repair deteriorated concrete in the deck underside

- Replace existing expansion joints

- Replace corroded bearings at the abutments

- Repair deteriorated abutments



Safety Improvements: 

- Install guardrails above structure and on  both approaches. 



Maintenance:

- Clean and restore original steel beams

- Remove any debris that has been built up on the abutment(s).



In addition, the repair project shall include additional requirements for

seismic load and increased truck load. 



Project preference is Design-Bid-Build.  Project will require planning and

EV documentation, and generation of design docs.

Requirement Title: DFSP Heckscher Drive Repair JAX Pier 111 Fire Protection Pipelines
Requirement Description:
The existing brackish water fire protection system dates back to the late 1980's and is antiquated and parts of it are in serious states of deterioration. The worst portions of the system are on JAX Pier 111. The brackish water from the St. Johns River is the source for the fire protection system water.  This piping of concern under this project is aboveground, has been exposed to the elements for 30 years, and is need of repair in order to keep it functional.  The fire system piping on the pier is comprised of 1,200 LF of ductile iron piping ranging in size from 8” to 16” in diameter.  There is heavy corrosion on the 16” piping at the foot of the pier and multiple U-bolts that attach the fire piping to joists have failed and are no longer present.  There is one mechanical clamp to address a leak that occurred several years ago. There are multiple flange locations where mechanical nuts have corroded and are severely compromised or failed.  Continued below in Additional Information Section.



Mission, Regulatory, Life Safety.  Applicable codes include NFPA, UFC, OSHA, industry standards, local, and environmental codes.



Collect a minimum of ten (10) coating samples from the fire pipeline system and equipment to analyze for heavy metals. 



Review readily available plans, specs, reports, etc. to assess the condition of the piping and associated equipment (i.e., valves, nozzles, hardware).  Perform a site visit(s) to verify existing conditions.  Develop a scope of work to repair fire main piping, replace valves, and provide protective coating of elements of the existing aboveground system to sustain the existing fuel system for a minimum of 6 years.  Advertise and contract an A/E to prepare a plan design and specifications for the repairs to maintain the aboveground fire protection system piping.  Photos attached at the end of this document.

Requirement Title: Water Main Corrosion Repairs from Clearwell Reservoir Bldg. 560 to Tupo Reservoir Bldg. 1480
Requirement Description:
Replace approximately 1100 LF of existing 30" CI waterline with new 30" PVC waterline.





1. Request Engineering service to provide RFP SOW/IGE. Provide DD1391, SAR and NEPA approval. Complete the RFP Package ( Project Documents) and award Project FY 26 Q2

2. RFP Package to be completed earlier than 29 December 2025 and design release to ACQ  not later than 23 Jan 2026.

3. DD1391  need to start  earlier than 24 June 2025  and be completed , signed by PWO/ARE not later than 4 December 2025.

4. NEPA/CATEX/SAR  need to start the development earlier than 25 August 2025 and must be completed 23 Nov 2025.

5. 35% RFP submittal must be completed 11 September 2025;  65% RFP Submittal to be completed 7 October 2025 and 100% RFP to be completed 19 Nov 2025.



PROEJCT OBJECTIVE:

A.  The Project is to replace approximately 1100 LF of  existing 30-inches CI  transmission line with new 30-inches BFPVC waterline. Provide fittings/transition fittings, reaction/thrust blocks and other appurtenance as required to  ensure a complete and usable final product.

B. Disconnect, cut and abandon-in-place existing  water transmission line and fill entire pipe with flowable concrete once the new line is completed and ready for connection.  The existing line shall remain active for continuous service during the construction of the new water transmission line.

C. The new water transmission shall be placed in a new trench within the Department of Defense real estate interest boundaries and easement, and shall be parallel to the existing water transmission line.



The existing 30"waterline is over 60 years old and has exceeded its life expectancy. Failure to replace this waterline will results in the inability to store 5200 Kgal of potable water which provides fire and domestic water to all of NBG

Requirement Description:

Drainage system B is a minor system along the West segment

of 1st Street. The system has two catch basins for the B6181 (apron electric building) driveway along the

north side of 1st Street. These two catch basins (K6 and K7) connect to the other drainage system that collects

Hangar 104 roof storm water and discharges into Kaneohe Bay beneath the apron.  A hydraulic analysis shows that five of the lines in this system appear to be undersized.  The C drainage system is a major system which collects storm water runoff flows along 1st Street, B Street, and Third Street. Drainage system C is separated into two separate drainage systems (C1 and C2) at inlet L15 along Third Street. Drainage system C1 is the lower half of Drainage System C.  A hydraulic analysis determined that the C drainage system is incapable of accommodating the storm water runoff flows for the 10-yr design rainfall flow.  The lack of capacity causes overflowing of the drainage manholes which results in flooding problems along B Street from First Street to Third Street. Requirement Title: PHNSY - WR152854 BLDG 394 Repair Emergency Exit Stairs, JBPHH
Requirement Description:
GENERAL: 

Building 394 lacks a safe means of egress to the first floor within existing corner fire emergency exit (mauka stair) due to heavily termite damaged wood. (See attached enclosure to location of stair). Reconstruct and improve fire emergency stair to meet code requirements to provide fire life safety of users. Continuous degradation leading to closure of stairs will impact mission functions as it promotes a hazardous work environment. Currently, building occupants are briefed to not utilize corner stairs unless of an emergency due to poor condition. Per NFPA 101 – Section 7.6 - Measurement of Travel Distance (table A.7.6 Common Path, Dead end, and Travel Distance), corner stairs shall remain operable as total closure will not meet NFPA means of egress travel limits. 



EXISTING CONDITION:

Building 394 is a Category III Type Historical Classification. Building 394 is a two-story structure with a total gross floor area of 139,000 SF. Building is constructed as concrete and wood framed walls with corrugated metal panels anchored to framing. Concrete columns are utilized on the first floor and wood columns on the second floor which support wood truss roof structure. Stair #2 is constructed of wood and is suspended through wood framing. 



IMPROVEMENT: 

- Demolish Stair #2 (Corner Wood Frame Stairs) due to excessive termite damage 

- Design / Replace overall stairs with non-combustible pre-fab stairs or termite treated wood. 

- Provide fire rated shaft to protect Stair #2 (currently exposed wood frame stairs to second floor) 

- Provide direct exit to the exterior of building per fire code requirements. (stairs currently exits into interior space of building)

Requirement Title: UM - REPLACE ROOF FOR LUALUALEI TANK S280
Requirement Description:
Complete replacement of the roof of an existing partially buried concrete potable water storage tank.  The tank is approximately 200' long, 50' wide and 11' deep.  The existing roof, which appears to be constructed of wood and asphalt is severely deteriorated and failing, and will need to be removed.  The new roof will be fixed to the top portion of the tank, which is above ground level.  The roof must completely enclose the tank and be impervious to outside elements, as it will house potable water.  Access hatches shall be provided for preventative maintenance purposes.  Screened air vents may included, as needed.  The tank can be drained during construction.

Planning and EV docs requested.

A/E required for design.

Requirement Title: OC B1116 - REPAIRS AND MAINTENANCE TO HUSH HOUSE (SEAS)
Requirement Description:
1.Rust at the bases of rigid frame columns.  These columns are constructed of two structural steel channels each.



2.Paint peeling and grout spalling at base of walls/top of foundation wall.



3.Rusting of personnel doors and frames.



4.Steel plate adjacent to hanger door rails.  Original coating/paint is gone and plate is rusting.



5.Hanger door rails wearing and possibly settling.



6.Personnel door in east elevation has a large hole rusted through the frame.



7.Rubber isolators (or bushings) in anchor bolt assemblies are deteriorating and becoming hard and crumbling.



8.Winch baseplate and lower chassis has peeling paint and is rusting.



9.Compressed air system piping has peeling paint and is rusting.



10.Exterior slab has settled around the office area of the building and has broken the sealant.



11.Large valve for oil-water separator is broken.  This is underground in a vault under a manhole cover.



12.Exterior store room/mechanical room door is rusted through (adjacent to main entry door).



13.Door sweeps on exterior doors are worn out and not working.



14.All exterior doors and frames need either complete renovation or replacement.



15.Exterior piping for sprinkler system (FDC) has peeling paint and oxidation.



16.Exterior compressed air tanks are oxidizing and have peeling paint.



17.The base of the hangar walls at the southwest corner shows evidence of more water getting into the building than other areas, and is rusting more severely.



18.Cracks in the concrete walls of the exhaust stack are very evident as are the concrete joints.  More severe cracks are in the concrete walls at foundation level adjacent to the retaining walls on two sides.

Requirement Title: NSN PIER 9 Underground Steam Main Replacement
Requirement Description:
Existing 300 LF of direct buried 8” high pressure steam piping that serves Pier 9 has reached the end of its useful life. The existing steam line that requires replacement is from where the pipe enters the ground east of Decatur Avenue to a vault at the head of Pier 9, see Figure 1. In November 15, 2024, two sinkholes were reported at the head of Pier 9 and the parking lot as a result of high pressure steam leakage, see Figures 2 and 3. Steam was seen leaking from the vault cover at the head of Pier 9 and downstream of the pressure reducing station east of Decatur Avenue, see Figures 4 and 5.

The purpose of this task order is to recommend contractor response to replace the existing steam line. If the steam line is not replaced, further disruption to waterfront operations will continue as there will be inadequate berthing of ships in Naval Station Norfolk. This disruption resulted in relocation of a ship scheduled to arrive in December 6, 2024 in Pier 9. In addition, leaking underground steam piping causes instability of the surrounding ground and/or continuous soil erosion. Steam plume being emitted can cause significant driver visibility issue.

tank size

•    Replace tension sheave for speed governor including the safety switches.

•    Replace lower portion if the guide rail.

•    Loop governor rope

•    Pit stop safety switches 

•    Pit hoist way lights (2ea)

•    Oil buffers (2ea)

•    220V Service outlets

•    Replace intercom system between machine room and elevator pit.

•    Replace sump pump capacity 3000GL/hr.

•    Test for proper functionality.

Requirement Title: WATERFRONT - PORT OPS - BRAVO 15-16 REPLACE PNEUMATIC FENDERS WITH FOAM FILLED FENDERS
Requirement Description:
Mission impact statement:  Project is needed in order to replace existing pneumatic type fenders with durable foam filled fenders. Over the past year we have had 6 pneumatic fenders rupture. Should the fenders continue to fail without being replaced ships will no longer be able to moor on Bravo15-16.  Bravo15-16 are two of the four repair births located on Pearl Harbor.



SOW:

Procure, deliver and install (16) new foam filled fenders. Fenders will be floating, foam filled, net-less type fenders with a 10ft diameter and a 18ft length. 

Deliver and install (2) chain assemblies per fender. 

-10ft diameter x 18ft long ocean guard net-less foam filled fenders

-Energy absorption (60% compression) - 2,390ft Kips

-Reaction force (when EA is achieved) - 889 Kips

-End pull-through strength- 70 kips

-End fitting to accept 2-1/2" shackle



Chain Assembly Details (quantity:32)

-Galvanized chain, open-link 2-1/2"

-15 links per side 

-Galvanized, 2" shackle (Chain to fender)

-Galvanized, 1-1/2 shackle (Chain to piling)



Maintenance requirements Pneumatic vs Foam filled fenders: 

-Pneumatic Fenders: Require cleaning (annual), pop-test of the installed relief valve (triennial). Life expectancy is 10 years.   

-Foam filled: cleaning (annual). life expectancy is 10 years.

1.    Background Information:

a.    2017/2018 CFAO Sanitary survey reported the significant water pressure drop in CSH-7216J 4-story BEQ. The minimum psi requirement for Navy facilities is 20psi. The average PSI for CSH-7216J can be lower than 10PSI when fire hydrant flow discharges  925 GPM(gallon per minutes), with which any toilet flushing will malfunction.   



b.    Hydrant Test Frequency

    Hydrant Flow Test: 1 per every 5 years.

    Line after passing BFP/PRV: 34.8PSI

    1F: 32 PSI

    2F: 27PSI

    3F: 22PSI

    4F: 15-16PSI

d.    Pipe size:

    From water main to BFP: 5inch (125mm)

    From BFP to 1st branch lines: 2.5~4inch (65-100mm)

    From 1st branches to the end user lines: :  0.8~2inch(20-50mm)



2.    Relocate the existing BFP at CSH-7216J 1F Mech room.

a.    Require easy access to all internal check valve parts and maintenance activities for the back-flow preventer.



3.    Remove 3ea of PRV (Pressure Reduce Valve) in 1F Mech room.

a.    Those PRV are located after BFP in 1F Mechroom and broken now. KTR created a bypass.

b.    KTR confirmed they are not necessary but only will contribute the low pressure becoming worse.



4.    Fix low water pressure at BEQ.

a.    Provide 2~3 booster pumps, whose system needs to work corporately to response various water consumption by daily and weekly. (Refer to BOSC KTR survey report attached.)

b.    Request PWD Engineer to consider drawbacks after boosting water pressure.

    Water cut during power outage.

    Possible Water leak from  any aged piping



c.    FOS recommendation

Requirement Title: NDW25E B2952 Repair Building Deficiencies CN9MRX/CM6TLN/CNSTW7
Requirement Description:
Two electrical deficiencies need attention at B2952, Inert Storage facility due to recent power surge.



Both went COMP-OS.



1.  Both exhausts fans are down and no high voltage to fan starters. Located breakers and reset power and checked voltage at starters. Had 480 volt at starters but when reset overloads breakers tripped. One fan motor is showing short to ground. Will need to get scissor lift out here to check motors and wiring. Surge protector on panel showing a fault on A phase.



2. Half of the overhead lighting is out. Automatic light sensor is inoperable.  EMI scoped work and trouble shot lights. Tested voltage up at lights, but ballasts had no output voltage. All 16 ballasts burned up when they had a power surge a while ago. Called Ashley Johnson to come and check out surge protector just to get another opinion. Job is going to exceed limit of liability with material/ labor.



IMPACT: This building is used to charge the electric forklift. This is a work stoppage.



3. Personnel entry door and frame is damaged Beyond repair also with Associated Hardware entry door single point of entry repairs will exceed 2,500 level of effort to include new 3070 steel door and frame 22 Rim exit device outside trim, Simplex 1000 push button entry lock with key override door closure gasket set threshold and locksmith to provide new core and key for personnel door Job exceeds LOL.



MISSION IMPACT: Personnel need a functioning entry door to carry out their mission.

Requirement Title: REPLACE ROOF COVERING ABOVE ROOM 108A & MECHANICAL ROOM PM34
Requirement Description:
1.  WORK LOCATION

BASE: NBVC Point Mugu, CA.

BUILDING NO.:  Building 34 


3.  PROJECT TITLE: Replace Roof Covering Above RM 108A & Mechanical Room, PM34



4.  IMPACT: Due to multiple cracks on the roof covering and low spots where water pools after heavy rain, the lower roof at the entrance to Building 34 leaks.  The water leaks into the wall areas, through the ceiling tiles, and into electrical junction boxes of Room 108A where maintenance admin department personnel work.  The water intrusion causes water damage to the interior of the office space area. The carpet, walls, ceiling, and floor become soaked from torrential rains pooling up on the roof and dripping from the ceiling. 

Citation: 29 CFR 1910 141(a)(3)-(iii).



5.  DETAIL DESCRIPTION OF WORK: This work shall consist of the contractor furnishing all labor, equipment and materials in performing all operations necessary to replace the single-ply membrane roof covering on the lower section of roof that covers both Room 108A and the Mechanical Room at NBVC Point Mugu Building 34.  This section of roof is located on the South side of the building near the front main entrance to Building 34. This lower roof section totals approximately 675 square feet.

Requirement Description:
Project Title: E2 (UEM) YSK-J209 REPLACE DEAERATOR

Scope of Work: 

  Replace and provide new deaerator assembly (deaerator tank, steam pressure control valve, feed water control valve, miscellaneous piping and gauges), top/bottom 

 platform/railings and other portions of the base frame (severely corroded) to include pipe insulation/cladding



Justification / Reason:

  Steam outage in J-Areas. Total steam capacity in CFAY (3 boiler plants) is 207ton/hr; J209 boiler plant is responsible for 36% steam production overall in CFAY that serves: (J area) Admin buildings, DODEA schools, NEX, Family Housing and Navy Lodge. Severe corrosion of platforms and railings are unsafe during daily checks/services. Deaerator installed in 2007 and has exceeded the average lifespan for boiler equipment and has severely corroded. Boiler deaerators must condition feed water to remove dissolved gases before it can be used in the boiler system, to protect the steam network and prevent corrosion and failure. 



Recommendation / Information /Special

  REPLACE WITH YSK-A43 SPECS: DEAERATOR AND STORAGE TANK Deaerator (50 m3/h)   MAKE: HOT SPRAY SER: 35DH09

  EXISTING: DEAERATOR AND STORAGE TANK, JD-01; Deaerator (50m3/h); MAKE- SHINEI MODEL-DSQ50-1 5; SER-TSQ708

  CONTROL VALVE, JDSFCV-01; Steam flow control valve for deaerator(98kpa); MAKE-AZBIL; MODEL-HCB; SER-R-J2AM7-41-011

  CONTROL VALVE, JDWFCV-01; Feed water flow control valve for deaerator (98kpa); MAKE-AZBIL; MODEL-HCB; SER-R-J2AM7-41-021

Requirement Title:
23894740 - REHABILITATE FACILITY PM602

COMPLETE INTERIOR AND EXTERIOR RENOVATION OF EXISTING BUILDING THAT IS CURRENTLY IN DISREPAIR
Requirement Description:
1. WORK LOCATION  

    BASE: Point Mugu

    BUILDING NO.: 602
 


3. PROJECT TITLE: WIB Rehabilitate Facility PM 602

4. IMPACT:  This fuels maintenance operations facility is almost uninhabitable due to leaking roof, water damage, lack of heating, broken stairs, NEC code violations.  The building is extensively used by operational and administrative staff, no alternate location exist near the facility to support functional requirements.  Funding and execution of work detailed should commence without delay.     



5. DETAIL DESCRIPTION OF WORK: Request removal and replacement of corroded/failed galvanized roofing/siding panels throughout building. Replace bathroom fixtures (except shower) and water damaged gypsum paneling behind the sink.  Reinstall bathroom ceiling exhaust fan ductwork.  Replace (1) broken window, Restore function to two (2) wind powered roof ventilation and install motorized mechanical louvers.  Complete the installation of the four (4) wall mounted 220v heaters, the units are new and never fully installed, currently missing thermostats and incomplete wiring to main panel.  Replace rear entrance wooden staircase/landing with a suitable OSHA Compliant galvanized or concrete.  Repair/patch numerous holes and ventilation covers on the galvanized siding.  Install knockouts in open electrical junction boxes.   Install two (2) modular type 12’x 12’ prefabricated warehouse office enclosures with supporting lighting, electrical, HVAC features. Include 40ft temporary storage unit for operational staff during project.

Requirement Title: 1821748 -- SUPSIT-225 Repair Collapsed perimeter wall at loading area
Requirement Description:
1.    CURRENT CONDITION:

The Concrete wall and portion of the exterior slab located in the far southern corner of the loading area, are seriously damaged and partially collapsed due to erosion of the sloped landscape area. Existing piping system from cogeneration equipment and natural gas pipeline are impacted by the settlement of the concrete surfaces.



2.    BASIC REQUIREMENT: 

2.1    Provide labor, materials and equipment to clear the area from over-grown vegetation.

2.2    Reshape landscape and provide new retaining walls with gabions

2.3    Demolish the collapsed concrete structures (walls and slab).

2.4    Rebuilt concrete slab and parapet wall. 



3.    DESCRIPTION OF WORK:

3.1    Clear all the area and sloped landscape from overgrown vegetation. This task will involve the use of mechanical means (front loader, backhoe, transportations, etc.)

3.2    Reshape the profile of the sloped the landscape area, to install new retaining wall with gabions. This will protect the road leading to building 230. (Estimated  about 50mt in length for 3 levels of gabions)

3.3    Provide temporary structure to support the existing piping system (hydronic and gas line) during demolition work the floor slab. (1)

3.4    Demolish cracked portion of the concrete slab (approx. 30m2) and the existing cracked concrete parapet walls about 20mt. 

3.5    Rebuilt the concrete slab and the parapet wall. Provide plastering finish to match existing conditions.

3.6    Reinstall, bolt and restore functional conditions the piping system connected with cogeneration plant. (1)



    NOTES:

(1)    This phase of work will require coordination with Siemens in quality proprietary of the cogeneration plant.

Requirement Title: 1783814 -- 21952122 - REPAIR THE FACILITY DUE TO RESTRICTIONS AND STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY PH803
Requirement Description:
1. WORK LOCATION 803



    BASE: Port Hueneme



    BUILDING NO.: 803

 
3. PROJECT TITLE: Repair the facility do to restrictions and structural integrity at PH803.

4. IMPACT: HEALTH AND SAFETY ISSUE.



5. DETAIL DESCRIPTION OF WORK: The purpose for this project is repair the facility PH803 based on the results from the structural inspection. Contractor shall repair the severe flaking and corrosion stated in the inspection. Contractor shall remove and replace (3) bolt connections at the bottom of the wind girt. Repair deformation in the steel tension-only rods. Repair surface corrosion on the caged ladder located in the high-bay. Repair deformation on the bottom steel braced frame and supporting top-riding double girder crane. Repair corrosion on the steel frame supporting the cylindrical towers. Repair corrosion on the steel brace connection from the cylindrical tower. Repair corrosion on the compressor room door and door frame. Repair minor horizontal cracks in the concrete stem wall supporting the lean-to structure. And repair metal panel corrosion on the perimeter of the building and on the door frame (refer to the structural integrity report attached).

Requirement Description:
WORK INCLUDES:

1.  Repair/replace outdated, deteriorated, and non-functional building ventilation system equipment to include fans, motors, controls, switches, disconnects, wiring, screens, and control panel.   Conduct engineering evaluation to validate  existing ventilation system for bldg 1747, a hazardous material storage warehouse, meets current Federal, DoD and industry standards. 8. Construct 1600 sf of temperature-controlled HAZMAT storage.

Prepare DD1391 and design for FY15 construction contract award to repair Building 1747 to meet applicable DoD facility criteria and correct life, safety and health deficiencies.

Equipment: PLC/Computer/Display Enclosure NEMA 04X, 3 Transducers, remote computer

Display: User-friendly touchscreen with option to display multiple tabs and user inputs: 

Tab 1: graphical display of current water in wetwell/drydock and which stage/pumps are operating, flowrate, backup battery status, and which signal primary/secondary is operating system. 

Tab 2: Graph displaying up to 7-day display of pump/level activity with option to flag/timestamp events (user input) similar/mimic the current chart recorders. 

    Tab 3: Alarm Log. 

    Tab 4: Mode selection and maintenance notes.

Tab 5: Simulation/test mode- simulation based on new inputs, override level signals for PMI maintenance, ie Alarms.

Modes: Normal, Drydock Flooded- Secure pumps, High Discharge-Start pumps based on stage two parameters with automatic lowered set points previously set by user, Maintenance- selectively secure a pump for maintenance



Program/operation parameters: Program to operate drainage pumps based on primary or secondary wetwell levels inputs, with ability for user to adjust set points. Sequence drainage pumps 1 through 3 every three cycles, unless one secured for maintenance. There are three stages. 

Stage 1: Turn one pump on at 55’, and off at 51.6’ (one pump running, two pumps on standby).

Stage 2: Second pump on at 56’ and off at 52’ (two pumps running, one on standby). 

Stage 3: Last pump on at 57’ and off at 53’ (All pumps running). 

Program operate based on one signal from either primary or secondary transducer. Able to self-troubleshoot  ...

Requirement Title: 1732063 -- NSWC Pkg 3 B633 Roof Modification for Crane Access
Requirement Description:
This design project will result in the production of a set of bid documents (including a basis of design, specification, drawings, cost estimate, etc) suitable for construction award. The design will account for modification of the roof over the CTF Low Speed Shaftline to allow for rigging shaftline components via boom crane through a removable roof penetration. This effort is expected to require permanent re-routing of fire suppression, electrical, lighting, mechanical/HVAC ductwork, plumbing piping, conduit, support structures, and any other interferences which prevents free and clear access to the shaftline components via the removable roof opening. The opening must accommodate/incorporate a removable, 100% water-tight panel.

 

Details/reference drawings will follow during SAES generation and design development.

Requirement Title: FSS REPAIR SOUTH TANK FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEM, F-202705
Requirement Description:
This project will design and provide a complete Fluorine-Free Foam (F3) Fire Protection System for Tank 20, 21 and 22 located at Pacific Air Forces (PACAF) South Tank Farm Air Ops Site. The work includes design and installation of fire pumps, electrical connections, controllers, fire alarm systems, foam concentrate bladder tank, foam ratio controllers, pipelines, foam chambers, valves, fittings, supports and

related appurtenances. Remove and provide Fire Hydrants no's. 179, 180,181,182 and 183 including underground water supply pipelines, valves, collars, steel bollards supports and accessories. Design and modification of F-905 Fire pump room to accomodate new piping lay-out, and to conform to UFC 3-600-01 and NFPA 20. Remove and provide roof mounted exhaust fan for F-905. Provide additional lightings and fire

protection sprinklers for F-905.Remove and provide Fire Alarm Control Panel (FACP), including reporting system at F-904. Provide power supply and controllers to new equipment. Repair defects, and remove and provide appurtenances of Fire Protection Water Storage Concrete Tank F-903.

Remove and provide underground and exterior piping, fill-in pipes, discharge pipes, level indicator, valves, fittings, railings, hatch, ladders and appurtenances for non-potable concrete water tank F-903. Provide cathodic protection to new underground piping. Remove and provide access stair and hatch for tanks 20, 21 and 22. Drain fuel, cleaning and gas freeing of tank one at a time. Perform complete testing and commissioning. Off-island disposal of hazardous and non-burnable construction waste materials. Refer to Part 3 - Project Program and Part 4 - Performance Technical Specification for further and detail information.

Requirement Title: DLA-POL Demo 5 South Fuel Farm USTs, Install 5 South Fuel Farm ASTs & Demo 4 North Fuel Farm USTs, PMRF
Requirement Description:
The Pacific Missile Range Facility (PMRF) currently has nine (9) each USTs containing approximately 50,000 gallons each for bulk fuel storage. Future design and planning for the facility will require a transition from underground to aboveground fuel storage facilities. This project will undertake the entire demo of (5) USTs on the south fuel farm with replacement by 5 ASTs and demo (4) USTs on the north fuel farm. The 5 replacement ASTs on the south side will have enough capacity to support the DFSP's mission requirements.

Underground Storage Tanks are becoming more and more scrutinized due to the high-risk potential for leaks and spills into the environment. Despite

operations, inspections, and repairs in accordance with industry standards, regulatory agencies are pushing for all UST systems to be brought aboveground

by 2038. Failure to comply with their requirements will only lead to violations fines and possible shutdown of the facility. Installation of ASTs will allow PMRF to meet mission fueling requirements while complying with storage tank environmental regulations.

Contractor to determine best method to install new aboveground tank system that meets operational requirements in accordance with applicable County,State, and Federal guidelines. Work to potentially include sizing of new system, installation, secondary containment, weather protection, and commissioning

of new system as required. Contractor to coordinate with local government POC to provide notifications and documentation as required to DOH.

All federal, state, local, Navy, and Marine Corps codes and regulations shall be followed and considered to the extent applicable. UFC 1-200-01, General

Building Requirements UFC 3-301-01, Structural Engineering UFC 3-460-01, Design: Petroleum Fuel Facilities UFC 3-460-03, Operation and Maintenance

of Petroleum Systems. Hawaii Administrative Rules, HAR.

Requirement Title: ASWSD-564 Replace Existing Fire Alarm System
Requirement Description:
1.  WORK LOCATION



BASE:  HD

BUILDING:  564

FLOOR(s): ALL

ROOM(s): ALL

INTERIOR/EXTERIOR:  INTERIOR

ADD'L LOCATION DETAILS: ISSUE: Existing fire system is continually breaking down and is getting too expensive to maintain due to inability to get parts.



4. IMPACT: SAFETY



5. DESCRIPTION OF WORK:



1.   Multiple indications of unknown fire troubles in Main panel (anywhere from old age, obsolete hardware, defective devices or faulty circuit).



2.   Not enough NAC (Notification Appliance Circuit) throughout the building, all SCIF area don’t have notification devices and we are unable to hear the audible alarm in the SCIF area.



3.   No automatic devices are installed and associated with the fire alarm panel (i.e. smoke detectors in common area, flow switch on WET-PIPE RISER). The existing water pressure switch initiating device (retard chamber type) is not known to be operational to trigger the alarm panel in the event of presence of water flow.



4.   Obsolete dialer (DACT Signal Transmitter) programmed for alarm signal only; no Supervisory and Trouble signal capability.



5.   Notification devices are not ADA compliance.



6.   Duct Detectors mounted to AHU (Air Handling Unit) (3x) were mounted outside the unit and not protected to weather, 1 out of 3 already corroded heavily with rain water.



7.   ONLY pull station devices were programmed to report to dispatch but without description.



This would have to be a FEAD project and will need engineering support to have a system IAW current FP code.  



8.  This is shops entered project.

Requirement Title: CNIC-211 New AF PEB Install Overhead Crane, CLDJ
Requirement Description:
CURRENT SITUATION:

The maintenance bay on the east side of the new AF PEB currently under construction was designed to accommodate up to a 6-ton overhead crane.  The project as currently scoped does not include provision for providing or installation of a crane--only the mount and supporting utilities.



REQUIREMENT:

726 EABS maintains wide variety of vehicles and heavy equipment for AF assets on CLDJ and CADJ. Related tasks include, but are not limited, to removal/installation of engines, transfer cases, cabs and related heavy components.  The AF requires support with procuring, installing, and certifying overhead crane equipment with the following characteristics:



- Fully motorized, 

- Monorail 

- Dual axis 

- (minimum) 3-ton capacity

- Installed on the currently designed/constructed mounts 



MISSION IMPACT:

Vehicles and the missions they enable will be at significant risk of extended non-mission capability without the benefit of local capability to perform heavy maintenance.  Our supported vehicle fleet evolves as missions and threat pictures evolve. For example, our fleet is projected to gain up armored vehicles in the near future, to support AFOSI missions outside the wire. Without this capability, repair and maintenance tasks requiring use of an overhead crane will instead require full vehicle replacement instead, an exceedingly lengthy reality that will place our force protection posture at risk. Without the capabilities of a motorized overhead crane, the risk of injury to technicians will also increase significantly.

Requirement Title: DLA-POL Hotel Pier Pipeline Repairs and Trench Cover Replacement
Requirement Description:
Remove approximately 400ft of existing FRP pipe from Hotel Pier sump to VS-3 and replace with internally and

externally coated carbon steel pipe.

- Install a check valve at VS-3.



- Repair or replace non-standard pipe shoes that are corroding in the Hotel pier trench.

- Replace wooden valve pit covers.

- Provide isolation for conduit connected to pipe.

- Replace non-standard pipe fittings.



- Remove approximately 2400 feet of existing PVC drain pipe form 26 valve pits to the Hotel pier sump and replace with

internally and externally coated carbon steel. The new drain line must be sloped from every pit to the existing Hotel

Pier sump.

The current concrete trench covers shall be removed and replaced with trench grating. The trench grating will be heavy-duty, corrosion resistant, and allow operators to perform visual inspections and maintenance. Grating must be placed in 1 foot wide removable strips and be capable of withstanding the load of pedestrian traffic without deflecting to such an extent it damages the fuel pipe within the trench. The trench covers shall be placed in the existing trench on the existing concrete grating supports. Requirement Description:
The Surface/Aviation Interoperability Laboratory (SAIL) facility has a former Spruance-class destroyer aft mast which is installed on top

of a 64' high working platform. The tower is of Aluminum construction, and its total hight above ground is 168'. installed in 2002, it now

has peeling paint, and cracks in some welds which secure the top platform (151') to the main mast, secure the starboard hazard light,

and the base of the ladder at the 64' platform. There are likely other welds that have or are failing that are yet to be identified.

We seek to have the welds to the 151 foot platform brackets repaired, to prep the entire tower for painting, and then to repaint the

tower with the NAVSEA recommended paint. Pitch pockets at the mast base will need to be repaired after painting is completed.

The SAIL is a secure facility, and has controlled access. Work on the tower will cause interruptions in the organization's ability to

support customers, and meet the needs of the fleet. Work will need to coordinated between the contractor, and the SAIL to minimize

these interruptions.



If the maintenance to the mast is not addressed it will, in time, become a safety hazard. Bare aluminum will continue to corrode and

welds will fail. At present time the pitch pockets around the tower legs are leaking, and water at times drips from the ceiling of room

401. This is in part due to the peeling paint on the mast legs, which the pitch is bonded too, and once peeled away from the mast

Requirement Title: Bldgs. 3217 and 3212A/B/C RDT&E Phase 3 effort with GTI
Requirement Description:
Problem Statement: NSGL is continuing its effort to support GTI in their demonstration of emerging technologies. NSGL identified the three warehouse facilities (3212A/B/C) are heated in the winter only by an aging inefficient steam boiler plant in B-3217. 



Scope of Work:   FEAD will review the designs and provide construction oversight for the RDT&E Phase 3.

This project includes replacing steam equipment with high efficiency heat pumps for air distribution heating and cooling. Steam-driven equipment in 3212-A and 3212-C is to be replaced with prototype heat pump designs. The technologies selected for preliminary assessment are the dual-fuel heat pump, air-to-water heat pump and very-high-efficiency ERV/HRV. 



This project should be able to:

- Quantify energy savings, life cycle costs, GHG emissions, and/or resilience.

- Develop best practices for installation, operation and maintenance.

Project restores, reconfigures and upgrades mechanical, electrical, structural and life safety systems to such a condition that Building 7201, Nuclear Repair Facility, may effectively be used for its designated functional purpose. Scope includes but is not limited to roof replacement, interior reconfigurations, life safety, egress and energy along with restrooms and lighting upgrades. Minor construction provides for new exterior Envelope to house relocated mechanical plenums.



REQUIREMENT:



Providing Adequate, properly configured and reliable Controlled Industrial Facilities CIF) are critical in direct support to all nuclear operations and functions supporting Fleet operations and schedules across the Sub Base Bangor mission.

The existing structural, mechanical, and electrical and safety systems which were installed at the time of building construction in 1978 are at the end of their serviceable life. The majority portion of the facility systems have deteriorated well beyond the maintenance and sustainment model of minor repair now requiring restoration. The facility is continually challenged to maintain current nuclear and energy standards affecting nuclear production capabilities.

Requirement Title: (FLC FUELS) POL 13 LEEWARD CROSS BAY JP5 TIDAL AREA CONSTRUCT NEW VAULT & REPAIR PIPELINE (DLA)
Requirement Description:
Civil work: 

1.    Excavate piping to allow air-to-ground transition to be sufficiently relocated away from low area where water collects. 

2.    Construct 5-sided vault allowing piping to transition from being buried to final elevation unobstructed. Piping supports within the vault shall meet UFC requirements. Vault design shall prevent any tidal water intrusion within the vault.

3.    Design vault to allow for a low point to allow any rainwater accumulation to be removed. 

4.    Install pipeline supports within the tidal area as required IAW UFC standards.

Pipeline work:

1.    Remove piping between excavated areas.

2.    Fabricate new section of piping to allow for increased elevation with sweeping transitions to allow for pipeline pigging.

3.    Install low point drains in transition vaults.

4.    Install high point maintenance vent.



Sections of piping are not exposed preventing proper inspection and maintenance creating the potential for excessive corrosion diminishing piping integrity, undetected leaks, and shortened service performance.

Requirement Title: NSA SDA-343 Repair CO2 System to Meet Certification Requirements
Requirement Description:
Requesting Mechanical Engineer to evaluate/determine what is needed to get the CO2 system located at Farrier

Fire Fighting School Bldg. SDA343 operational and certified.

Boiler Inspector cited the following as major concerns:

- Code Violation CO2 Outlet being to close to building

- Code Violation of filling CO2 tank inside a building

- Code Violation by not having a Pressure Relief Valve on top of the CO2 tank

- Code Violation by not having an CO2 alarm in the room with the CO2 tank

- Replace refrigerant system for CO2 tank 

- Conduct HVAC Survey to insure it is designed and rated properly to support CO2 room.



SUPPLEMENT 3

INSTALLATION OF LIQUID CARBON DIOXIDE STORAGE VESSELS

S3.1 SCOPE

This supplement provides requirements and guidelines for the installation of Liquid Carbon Dioxide Storage

Vessels (LCDSVs), fill boxes, fill lines, and pressure relief discharge/vent circuits used for carbonated beverage

systems, swimming pool pH control systems, and other fill in place systems storing 1,000 lbs (454 kg)

or less of liquid CO2.

S3.2.1 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS (ENCLOSED AND UNENCLOSED AREAS)

a) LCDSVs shall not be located within 10 feet (3,050 mm) of elevators, unprotected platform ledges, or

other areas where falling would result in dropping distances exceeding half the container height.

b) LCDSVs shall be installed with sufficient clearance for filling, operation, maintenance, inspection, and

replacement.

- The painted coating over the Air Vents and doors has failed.

Requirement Title: E2 (SRF) YSK-DD-4 REPAIR OF DOCK STRUCTURES
Requirement Description:
1. Scope of Work:

   a. Perform complete repair of dock structures (wall alters and floors).

      (1)  Repair of dock structures (wall alters and floors).



2. Justification / Reason: 

   a. Even though Yokosuka Dry dock #4 is U. S. Navy certified dry dock, engineering study for maintenance/repair the dock structure has never conducted before.  

      As a report of annual dry dock inspection conducted by NAVFAC PW5, dock structure shows major cracks and erosion due to age, and also there are leakage of subsurface water from the walls. 

      Since this dry dock is over 100 years old.

      SRF would like to request to perform the complete repairs as required.

Requirement Description:

Due to a cable failure between substation 400 (S400) the BUCCA main distribution panel (MDP), replacement of cable is needed in order to restore utility power to all involved customers. 550' of 4" schedule 80 pvc

Dirt for backfill

Gravel for cover

Impacted operations include a long range UAS system for base defense, medical clinic, J6 assets, and PSYOPS operations. Regular outages to these customers/systems greatly reduce overall base protective posture as well as support for potential down-range missions.

- Change window screen (north elevation)

-Power wash all the facades

- Water proof exterior with a water-based water proofing material (two coats).

Requirement Title: NSWC BLDG 3544 INSTALL THOR GUARD LIGHTNING PREDICTIVE SYSTEM
Requirement Description:
EM24 NSWC BLDG 3544 INSTALL THOR GUARD LIGHTNING PREDICTIVE SYSTEM 24098129

WHO > 10241

WHAT > Thor-Guard Guard Lightening Predictive System Install

WHERE > B3544 

WHY > 

1. The following is required at the Ammunition Burning Ground Building 3544:



a. Install a complete Thor Guard Lightening Predictive system. The Explosives Safety office has the complete Thor Guard system (control box, connecting cables, Sensor, sensor cable, Sensor mounting fixture, software). Additional material requirements are:

i. Approx. 100ft of 1 inch conduit to protect the sensor cable. 

ii. Laptop computer (Any PC with a Windows Operating System currently supported by Microsoft. At least 2GB of usable RAM is recommended) 

iii. Minimum 1 inch ridged galvanized pipe long enough to mount sensor 9-10 ft high. 



b. Mount sensor on the building (or a minimum 1 inch ridged galvanized pipe) per the following parameters:

•  Within the standard 125ft cable length

• At least 5 ft from lightening air terminals

• At least 15ft from (and higher than) air conditioning units, vents fans etc.

• At least 5-10 ft above any surface

• Never under overhanging trees and high power lines

BLUF: Based on PWD Oceana’s FSIP report, NAVFAC MIDLANT is requiring further restriction of bridge crane use at Building 354, Dam Neck Annex in Virginia

 

1.    Who: PWD Oceana’s A/E ‘AECOM’, Adam Hanks, PE and Christine Carlson, AIA, performed FSIP inspection of building 354 located at Dam Neck Annex in Virginia.

2.    What: Building 354 is a single-story steel-framed building. The inspection determined an overall Inspection Rating of 3. The inspection found significant section loss in the steel columns of Bays 11 and 12 that support the bridge crane. Previous bridge crane travel restrictions are already in place at Bay 33 due to already-known section loss at other columns.

3.    Where: Building 354, Dam Neck Annex is used as a boat maintenance facility, and occupied by approximately 100 personnel.

5.    Impact to Installation:  Restricting bridge crane travel to include bays 11 and 12 will have significant impacts to operations. The user is able to operate in other bays of building 354, but loss of the ability to conduct mission critical work in bays 11, 12, and 33 results in increased operations and maintenance costs/time to shift boats in and out of other bays, in order to conduct crane-enabled work. As a result of limited bay availability, cost/time impacts are not linear and may severely inhibit mission support requirements when the facility is not fully functional.

Requirement Description:
Scope: - BASIN WORK

1. Remove all valves, handrails, and hardware necessary to remove the existing galvanized hot water

basins.

2. Power grind all cold-water basin surfaces and all structural supports below the water line to a near

white metal finish.

3. Prep all seams to provide a leak free coating.

4. Provide and install CIM liner on all prepared surfaces.

5. Remove the fill area casing sheets and provide new OEM galvanized sheets.

6. Install new fill area casing sheets and galvanized hot water basin assemblies.

7. New basins include nozzles, gaskets and hardware.

8. Re-install all handrails and remove any coverings from the pipe or sensors in the cold-water basin.

      - FILL WORK

1. Remove existing fill.

2. Install new MX75 fill kit with new supports, diverters, and hangers.

      - MATERIALS AND HOISTING

1. See Siemens’ proposal

2. One 35-ton crane to hoist materials on the roof.

      - EXCLUSIONS AND CLARIFICATIONS

1. Cooling towers to be drained and cleaned by NAVFAC.

2. Basin work must be done within a specific temperature range.

3. Dumpsters for debris and dumpster removal by NAVFAC

Requirement Description:
ENTERED 6/12/2024

REPAIR JP5 PRODUCT RECOVERY SYSTEM.

See attached DWCF request.  EBS# 10551008 (FY25_EMG_NCP_JP5 PROD RECOV SYS)

1. JP-5 system does not have a compliant UFC 03-460-01 Product Recovery Tank (PRT), system, or pump.

2. PRT extends beyond primary containment.

3. PRT pump is unable to overcome system pressure to pump down PRT when high-level reached.

4. Current PRT pump is tied to drain/venting lines as well as PRV downstream piping which disable the automatic pump during maintenance.

5. JP-5 system (including PRT) design schematics, flow diagrams, or drawings IAW UFC 3-460-01, para 2-17A . 

6. JP-5 missing several thermal relief valves around system isolation points IAW UFC 03-460-01.

 Notional SOW. 

1. Update current JP-5 blueprints and engineering drawings for entire system IAW UFC 3-460-01/03.

2. Redesign current JP-5 Product Recovery Tank (PRT), system and pump(s) to meet UFC 3-460-01, paragraph 8-3.14.2, design standards to include all required appurtenances. 

3. Complete engineering analysis of all thermal expansion and pressure relief lines.

4. Extend JP-5 containment to encapsulate PRT or install spray shields on side and back of PRT to provide maximum protection in the event of PRT overfill.

5. Verify/Install thermal expansion around individual isolation valves IAW with UFC plate 20.

6. Receipt pump inlet Replace swing check valve with pressure relief valve or redirect discharge back to system vice Product Recovery Tank.

grading, and compaction.

-	Paving and site improvements include asphalt paving, concrete paving, curb, gutter,

sidewalks, and landscaping.

Requirement Title: PD22078045 - EN - UT - REPLACE - WOOD TO STEEL POLES - CORONA-EL-CKT-1 - NWS SBCH
Requirement Description:
Replace eleven (11) wooden power poles with eleven (11) steel power poles.   Pole Numbers that will be replaced are (3, 7, 8, 10, 11, 102, 104, 107, 109, 110, and 111).  Replace the manhole covers for (MH39, MH9, MH10, MH11, MH12, MH13, MH15,and MH16).



 

3.    ISSUE & IMPACT (If not completed):  Our electrical system at Norco faces vulnerabilities due to the deficiencies with the current wood poles. Buildings that will be impacted by the failure of the support structures system included (B201, B203, B650, and B634).



4.    DESCRIPTION OF WORK : 

This project will solve the deficiencies in our support structures of electrical system at NWSSB- Det Norco.

 

Description of Scope of Work: 

The contractor shall provide all labor, construction, materials, supplies, equipment, functionality testing and supervision to complete work. 

A-

1-Remove existing communications lines and preserve.

2-Remove and dispose eleven existing 45' wood poles.

3-Demolish existing crossarms and hardware.

4-Remove existing  (guy anchors,risers) and preserve to use if possible.

5-Install eleven new 45' steel poles.

6-Install new bolt clamps and re-attach the existing communications lines to the new poles.

7-Install new 10' fiberglass crossarms for the new poles.

8-Install new 4' wood crossarms for the COMM lines.

9-Install new sets of raptor protection for the new poles.

10-Install new pin insulators for the new poles

11-Install fused cut-outs.

12-Install Lightning arresters.

13-Work requiring a power outage requires a minimum 14 days notice to affected tenants.

14- Pole Numbers that will be replaced are (3, 7, 8, 10, 11, 102, 104, 107, 109, 110, and 111).

Requirement Title: Repair Compressed Air Piping Farragut Tunnel B752, PSNS
Requirement Description:
Project demolishes and replaces deteriorated compressed air system components such as piping, valves and supports located in the Farragut Avenue Utility Tunnel.



Project is a design build repair of the Compressed Air piping (CAIR) in the Farragut Utility Tunnel. This portion of the system is serving drydocks, piers and production facilities located in the east and central portions of the Controlled Industrial Area (CIA) of Puget Sound Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility (PSNS/IMF).

Project scope provides for repairs to piping, supports, anchors and incorporates seismic bracing, mechanical repairs by replacement are to carbon steel pipe including associated distribution valves, connectors and manifold devices, site preparation includes implementation of compressed air distribution system access for equipment and personnel, safety features such as traffic control and disposal of debris generated from the removal of the deteriorated piping and associated components, hazardous abatement includes the identification, containment, removal and handling of asbestos containing materials (ACM) and debris along with lead paint,OMSI manuals, and station support for area and utility outages, including relocation of shipyard equipment and materials, lifting and other PSNS/IMF operations requirements.



NEPA: The project is a Categorical Exclusion (CATEX) and completion is in progress. Repairs to the existing facility and components by this project are consistent with land/facility use and, when completed, the use or operation of the facility will continue to comply with regulatory requirements.

Requirement Description:
This project renovates Building 1780 (1,033 SM) at Naval Station Rota, Spain, for the 22nd Naval Construction Regiment.  The scope includes full architectural, structural, mechanical, electrical, and fire protection upgrades, along with AT/FP enhancements and new finishes, complying with all applicable UFCs. The building will house Open Secret Storage (OSS), a medical area, a soils laboratory, and support spaces.



The OSS will feature open office space, private offices, a command suite, a conference room, and a secure telecommunications room. The medical area will include exam and treatment rooms, offices, and specialized storage.  The soils lab will have a dedicated work area and storage. Support spaces encompass upgraded electrical/telecommunications rooms and a janitor/maintenance closet.  Exterior work includes repairs, repainting, and parking lot upgrades.



The project will address asbestos and lead mitigation, and requires seismic evaluation and retrofitting per UFC 3-301-1. Obsolete exterior elements will be demolished. Two concept design layouts will be provided, each with independent exterior access for the OSS, medical area, and soils laboratory.

Requirement Description:
Project proposes to repair Ammunition Wharves W3 and Wl by strengthening existing bearing piles, adding new bearing piles, retaining part of the existing fender pile system, and replacing the deck to create wharves built to current standards. The project will be divided two phases with W3 in fiscal year FY22 and Wl in FY23. The wharves shall meet the requirements of Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC) 4-152-01, 11 Design: Piers and Wharves. 11 The wharf structure will be able to support a uniform live load of 600 psf as well as the unrestricted movement of 90-ton mobile truck cranes with maximum outrigger loads limited to 80 tons. 

Scope of work for each phase is identical. Scope includes demolition of the existing wharf deck. A portion of the existing bearing piles will be repaired and new bearing piles will be installed to accommodate the greater design load A portion of the existing fender system, consisting of pre-cast concrete piles and plastic wales and chocks, will be replaced. Sheet piling will be installed inboard of the wharf structure. The project will also include the reconstruction of wastewater and potable water utility systems, phone lines and grounding system for lightning protection. Utilities will be placed into a utility trench built into the wharf deck. Permanent oil spill containment boom, safety ladders, life ring cabinets, fire alarm system and mooring hardware will be installed.

Built-In Equipment includes a compressed air system, pallet racks and an overhead bridge crane (10-ton).



DEMOLITION includes the demolition of existing 760 m2 facility, Recycling Center Building #2203.

Requirement Title: QC0013 - FSS REPLACE FOAM FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEM, TANKS 12-13, WO#1720632
Requirement Description:
This project will provide design and installation of Fluorine Free Foam fire suppression system for Tanks 12 and 13 and wet pipe sprinkler system for F-497 located at Fuel Farm area to conform with the latest provision of UFC 3-600-01 Fire Protection Engineering for Facilities and NFPA standards.

The following are the scope of work and shall not be limited to complete the project:

I. CIVIL

1. Remove and provide supports including its components and accessories to the following pipelines. This includes painting works.

a. Fire pump pipes and wet pipe sprinkler system at F-497

b. Fill and discharge pipes of Non-Potable Water Storage Tank at F-498

c. Foam solution pipes and foam chambers of Tanks 12 and 13

2. Remove and provide roof hatches, railings and access stairs at Tanks 12 and 13.

II. FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEM:

1. Remove and provide one (1-ea) assembly of Diesel Engine Driven Fire Pump including batteries, pump controllers, piping, valves, fittings, supports and all accessories at F-497.

2. Remove and provide Diesel Tank including fuel piping, valves, fittings and all accessories.

3. Remove and provide foam concentrate tanks including foam concentrate, piping, isolation valves, fittins and related accessories.

4. Remove and provide balanced pressure foam proportioning system assembly composed of foam liquid pump, balancing valve, foam concentrate proportioner, valves, fittings, pump controllers and related accessories.

5. Provide reduced pressure backflow preventer to foam pipeline.

6. Remove and provide foam solutions piping from F-497 through tanks 12 and 13 including foam chambers, valves, fittings, supports and accessories.

7. Remove and provide fill pipes, fill pipe isolation valves, discharge pipes, overflow pipes and level indicator assembly and related accessories for Non-Potable Concrete Water Storage Tank, F-498.

8. Remove and provide wet pipe sprinklers system at F-497 including underground pipe and isolation valve before entering the riser pipe. For U/G

Requirement Description:
Wharves B20 and B21 at Joint Base Pearl Harbor Hickam (JBPHH) are required to support maintenance of Cruiser and Destroyer ships, but will continue to be incapable of supporting such work due to no portal crane capability at B20 and inadequate structural capacity for heavy mobile crane operations at B21. 



In addition, structural capacity at these wharves are further reduced by deterioration of structural members such as the concrete deck, beams, girders, pile caps, and piles.  Mooring hardware such as bollards, double bitts, clears and their associated foundations are damaged and in need of repair.  The existing timber fender system is in disrepair with a significant number of timber fenders broken off underwater and detached from the wharf, rendering them useless.  Shore power electrical facilities no longer provide adequate and reliable power.  



This TF-1 proposes to repair Wharves B20 and B21 to allow for mobile truck and portal crane operations with capacity to meet the requirements of UFC 4-152-01.  To accomplish this work, NAVFAC Waterfront services including environmental planning, design and construction are requested.  The project will be a two phased CMP project.  Phase 1 target award: FY22 Q3 (June 2022).  Phase 2 target award: FY23 Q1 (December 2022).  Phase 1 will include Wharf B20, a portion of Wharf B21, and upgrades to Substation F-10.  Phase 2 will include a portion of Wharf B21. 



Phase 1 will consist of the following:

Wharf B20 - Demolish and reconstruct the superstructure to include the concrete deck, pile caps, beams and girders in order to restore portal crane operations. Existing sheet pile, concrete support piles, drilled shaft foundations and fender piles shall be re-used and additional piles installed as needed in order to support the portal cranes and mooring of surface ships. Requirement Title: INSTALL NEW CROSSOVER PIPE FROM JP8 TO ENROUTE
Requirement Description: Install a pipeline cross connection between the newly constructed JP-8 issue Tanks at the Booster Pumphouse area and the nearby Enroute JP-8 piping at the booster pump/filter stand in the Booster pumphouse area.  The approximate length of piping required is 30 meters and 2 dual block and bleed valves will be needed.  Engineering analysis is needed to determine whether or not an additional booster pump is required to meet existing booster pump suction head requirements. This is a simple piping project that allows the commissioning of Tanks 209/210 once they are ready for return to service. The connection was an oversight of the overall project design. Since the project to convert the waste oil tanks and reconfigure the existing F-76 truck fill stand was split into 3 separate projects this requirement was missed, but is simple and required to provide the needed JP-8 storage and truck fill capability.

Expand laboratory space by providing additional counter space for testing equipment, correcting HVAC issues, and modifying services to accommodate organized testing sample storage space.

The laboratory lacks sufficient counter space for many test protocols, and there is insufficient space to accommodate all required testing equipment. HVAC system in lab is tied to other building systems and is a patchwork of multiple independent systems, thus operates inefficiently and does not provide adequate heating, cooling and ventilation throughout the facility.  

This is a D33 facility, thus qualifying for DLA-E POL SRM program funding.  



Target full design in FY21 and ready for construction funding in FY23.

Requirement Description:
Contractor shall perform continuous snow/ice removal services for all areas included in NSA Bethesda Snow Operations Priority Map for WRNMMC at the frequency listed for their specific Priority levels.





 7. Building 54 & 55 – Parking Garages

1. The Contractor may use a self-propelled snow blower, however, the snow blower may not exceed 400lbs per unit and must be equipped with rubber blades and snow brooms.

2. Contractor shall only use snow removal equipment with rubber tires, snow blades with shoe, rubber tip or small skis to prevent ruptures in the deck coating system.  The use of metal blades without protection is NOT permitted.

3. The Contractor is NOT permitted, nor authorized to remove the snow/ice via jettison over the side of Building 54 or 55.

4. The Contractor shall use de-icing agents as the primary method for snow/ice removal. 

5. The Contractor shall NOT utilize any rock salt (Sodium Chloride) or similar de-icing agents, which may erode the concrete.  

6. The Contractor shall ensure the top two parking levels are cleared to their full width.   

7. The Contractor shall NOT create snow/ice piles on the top two levels of parking garage, Building 54 and 55.  Contactor shall ensure large piles of snow are removed immediately.

Requirement Title: WRNMMC-000, Snow Removal Event #9 08FEB2025. Contractor shall perform continuous snow/ice removal services for all areas included in NSA Bethesda Snow Operations Priority Map for WRNMMC at the frequency listed for their specific Priority levels.
Requirement Description:
5.    Building 54 & 55 – Parking Garages

1.    The Contractor may use a self-propelled snow blower, however, the snow blower may not exceed 400lbs per unit and must be equipped with rubber blades and snow brooms.

2.    Contractor shall only use snow removal equipment with rubber tires, snow blades with shoe, rubber tip or small skis to prevent ruptures in the deck coating system.  The use of metal blades without protection is NOT permitted.

3.    The Contractor is NOT permitted, nor authorized to remove the snow/ice via jettison over the side of Building 54 or 55.

4.    The Contractor shall use de-icing agents as the primary method for snow/ice removal. 

5.    The Contractor shall NOT utilize any rock salt (Sodium Chloride) or similar de-icing agents, which may erode the concrete.  

6.    The Contractor shall ensure the top two parking levels are cleared to their full width.   

7.    The Contractor shall NOT create snow/ice piles on the top two levels of parking garage, Building 54 and 55.  Contactor shall ensure large piles of snow are removed immediately.

7. Building 54 & 55 – Parking Garages

1. The Contractor may use a self-propelled snow blower, however, the snow blower may not exceed 400lbs per unit and must be equipped with rubber blades and snow brooms.

2. Contractor shall only use snow removal equipment with rubber tires, snow blades with shoe, rubber tip or small skis to prevent ruptures in the deck coating system.  The use of metal blades without protection is NOT permitted.

3. The Contractor is NOT permitted, nor authorized to remove the snow/ice via jettison over the side of Building 54 or 55.

4. The Contractor shall use de-icing agents as the primary method for snow/ice removal. 

5. The Contractor shall NOT utilize any rock salt (Sodium Chloride) or similar de-icing agents, which may erode the concrete.  

6. The Contractor shall ensure the top two parking levels are cleared to their full width.   

7. The Contractor shall NOT create snow/ice piles on the top two levels of parking garage, Building 54 and 55.  Contactor shall ensure large piles of snow are removed immediately.

Requirement Title: Specific- SWF - Kings Bay Composite Camel Modifications
Requirement Description:
CPCPNR. The current composite camels at NSB Kings Bay are adequate to support current submarines and the new COLUMBIA class. However, based on a current study being executed by NAVFACSE (POC Evan Boyce), the current composite camels at the EHWs and Site VI Layberth are inadequate to meet UK Dreadnought (UKD) hull pressure requirements. The concept study identified a modification to the existing camels to meet UKD requirements. This project is to design and procure modifications to the five (5) composite camels at the EHWs and the two (2) wide-body composite camels at Site VI Layberth. This project will also design and procure two (2) new wide-body composite camels. This project may also design and procure additional fender pile, pending

confirmation. New and modified camels will be usable for all US and UK submarine classes, including COLUMBIA. Without these camel modifications, UKD will be at risk for hull damage when berthing at the EHWs or Layberth

Requirement Title: WR 177125 URGENT NEW TOTAL RESIDUAL CHLORINE MONITORING SYSTEM AT WRF EFFLUENT
Requirement Description:
This request is for design and construction services to implement this project.

B1684: Furnish and install a new Total Residual Chlorine (TRC) Monitoring System at the Effluent Pump Station

(B1684). This project is necessary to comply with future requirements of the National Pollutant Discharge

Elimination System (NPDES) Permit for the Water Reclamation Facility (WRF), which will require continuous TRC

recordings for the Effluent Sampling Point, located at B1684; the updated NPDES Permit requirements are

anticipated to become effective in September 2024. Please consider a system that will create a quiescent zone

where representative TRC samples can be taken; the intent is to avoid inaccurate readings that could be caused

by short circuiting and other factors within the effluent wet well itself. Recommend the TRC Monitoring System

include residual chlorine analyzer equipment, as well as a separate basin with a baffle configuration (outside of the

effluent wet well), pumps, controls, plumbing, appurtenances, and weather protecting structures.

Request work be sent to contract. Site visit mandatory.

Requirement Title: NDW25SW+ B6103 - INSTALL SPRINKLER DELUGE SYSTEM WELD/FAB MACHINE SHOP
Requirement Description:
There is NO existing fire sprinkler system currently installed in Bldg. 6103. This building is an old dry wooden building dating back to 1940. The NAVY was concerned enough to install a fire alarm system 15 -20 years ago but they never did complete the fire suppression system. This fire alarm system that would notify Patuxent River in case of a fire was just fixed last year and is supposed to work now.  I would like to see an installation of a fire suppression system throughout this building to protect the occupants of the building. Currently there are no sprinklers in any of the office spaces, hallways or in the machine shop and weld shop areas. There are no water supply lines installed to feed any sprinklers. There is a men and women's restroom on the west side of the building about mid center of the building. This would be the likely location where the fire suppression system could be sourced from.



This is a safety concern / fire hazard in this wooden building.



This is a  fire / safety hazard that need to be addressed to prevent a fire from happening.

Requirement Title: REPLACE NH159/SA SUBSTATION, PRIMARY NSA HR POWER NODE
Requirement Description: This project will replace the existing SA substation with a modernized equipment and designed for redundancy. The project will replace the 54 year old, unreliable substation transformer with a new 20MVA, 34.5kV – 11.5kV Substation transformer. The existing outgoing metal-clad switchgear will be replaced with dead-front, metal-clad, draw-out, switchgear assembly of vertical sections, each with 15 kV vacuum circuit breakers. The station grounding resistor will also be replaced with a new one. The project includes the installation of a new 35kV (SF6) 4-way switch that will add redundancy to SA Substation. Currently, SA is feed from the Navy South Switching Station circuit 15 (NS15). If this circuit goes down it will take several hours to reconfigure the distribution system to pick SA’s load. But with the new switch, SA Substation will have access to another Navy South circuit. If the primary feeder (NS15) goes down, power to SA Substation can be restored in less than an hour due to the addition of this 4-way switch. The project will include the salvage, demolition and removal of existing equipment.

PROJECT DESCRIPTION:

 This purpose of this project is Harden Circuit P-2 at Polaris Point north of Polaris point Drive and west of Guard Station by installing 13.8KV, 5 way switch and primary a new primary duct bank system and new pad mounted transformer to feed existing structure 4410PP, 4427PP, 4429PP, 4439PP, 4445PP and 4446PP.  The project also to includes for the removal of all existing overhead primary and secondary feeders and poles and install a new underground pole mounted street lighting system in the area.  Reconnect existing 75KVA pad mount transformer feeding ball field lighting system.

Requirement Title: DALE-06 - Grounds TO, Snow Removal 05JAN2025.  Contractor shall perform snow/ice removal services for all areas included in DALE – IDIQ Snow Priority Map for Dalecarlia at the Priority 3 frequency.
Requirement Description:
1. The contractor shall respond within 2 hours of award and commence work. 

2. Snow removal services will be provided in accordance with Dalecarlia areas.

3. The Contractor shall be responsible for notifying the Government of the locations of any vehicles stuck in snow banks for removal.

4. ELIN E1028 Ice / Snow Pre-Treatment (Roads and Sidewalks) DALE. Chemical deicing material(s) shall be placed on roadway surfaces to prevent ice/snow from accumulating on roadways and to ensure roadways are safe and passable. Deicing material shall be placed on all paved parking areas (to include the top level of parking garages) to ensure areas are safe and passable. Contractor shall respond within 2 hours of notification.  Pre-Treatment shall be completed prior to ice/snow precipitation.   

5. ELIN E1029 Ice / Snow Post-Treatment (Roads and Sidewalks) DALE. Deicing material(s) shall be placed on roads, parking areas, sidewalks, and building entrances following the cessation of ice/snow precipitation event. 

6. ELIN E995 Ice / Snow Removal - Moderate (4"-10") -   DALE. Snow and Ice removal, Moderate event, 4"-10" deep.  The Contractor shall remove ice/snow from runways, taxiways, parking areas, sidewalks, and roads required for operations, safety, fire protection access, and vehicular and pedestrian traffic. No accumulations over 3" from 0530 to 1900, Monday - Friday. Contractor shall respond within 2 hours of notification.  Work shall be completed within 1 calendar day of order.

Requirement Title: PD20905282 - EN - UT -INSTALL- EMERGENCY GENERATOR - SEABEA - 869 - NWS SBCH
Requirement Description:
Install a diesel powered emergency generator (est. 150kW) to the Seal Beach Building 869 Pump Station.  Project includes construction of a concrete pad and electrical connections, including an automatic transfer switch.





NWSSB currently possess one potable water pump station located at Bldg SEABEA-869 ( North Side along Westminster Blvd ) which serves the entire base and its critical missions. In regards to continuity, Pump House 869 is not equipped with a stationary back-up generator. In the event of an unforeseeable base-wide electrical outage, Pump House 869 will lose all electrical power impacting the Pump House, NWSSB fire protection, & potable water systems. There are currently two rooms at SEABEA-869. The first room houses both pumps and all supporting mechanical and electrical utility assets that serves NWSSB. The second room ( dimensions = 7.5 by14 ft ) was used to house a chlorine system which is now abandoned. The Scope of Work below outlines the requirements needed to install a sufficient stationary back-up generator in the abandoned chlorine room:



1- Install new stationary generator (60kw) inside B-869/second room. 

2- Replace the current door with new steel double door.

3- Pour a concrete slab to make the floor inside the room even.

4- Add Automatic Transfer Switch.

5- Connect the new generator with ATS, transformer, and the electrical panel.

6- Add all necessary duct work, ventilation louvers, and exhaust piping.



This project is needed to provide continuity and resiliency to our Pump House. Without this project, the Pump House will lose all electrical power in the event of an unplanned electrical outage severely affecting our fire protection, potable water systems, and critical missions.

Requirement Title: GSTLH6 PNYA-NFPC-1029-Replace CU-6 System #1 Compressor #2 HVAC
Requirement Description:
Contractor to replace the #2 Compressor on System #1 of CU-6 in Bldg. 1029 on the HVAC System.

 

 

 

Scope of Work: CU-6 - System #1, Compressor #2 Replacement

 

 

1.         Lockout / tagout equipment.

 

2.         Recover refrigerant from System #1 and dispose of according to EPA regulations.

 

3.         Remove and replace Compressor #2, on System #1 of CU-6.

 

4.         Furnish and install new compressor, contactor, suppressor, crank case heater, and drier.

 

5.         Purge system with nitrogen and pressure test.

 

6.         Leak check and evacuate system.

 

7.         Charge with up to 75lbs of R410A. Any unused refrigerant up to 75lbs will be left with the customer for customer's stock.

 

8.         Start and check for proper operation.
